ARS § 13-1422 (Adult oriented businesses; location; hours of operation; injunction; classification; definitions): (c) Films, motion pictures, videocassettes, slides or other photographic reproductions that are characterized by the depiction or description of specific sexual activities or specific anatomical areas.
ARS § 13-1422 (Adult oriented businesses; location; hours of operation; injunction; classification; definitions): 4. "Adult motion picture theater" has the same meaning prescribed in section 11-811.
ARS § 13-1422 (Adult oriented businesses; location; hours of operation; injunction; classification; definitions): 5. "Adult oriented business" has the same meaning prescribed in section 11-811.
ARS § 13-1422 (Adult oriented businesses; location; hours of operation; injunction; classification; definitions): 6. "Adult theater" has the same meaning prescribed in section 11-811.

ARS § 13-1422 (Adult oriented businesses; location; hours of operation; injunction; classification; definitions): 7. "Escort" means a person who for consideration agrees or offers to act as a companion, guide or date for another person or who agrees or offers to privately model lingerie or to privately perform a striptease for another person.

ARS § 13-1422 (Adult oriented businesses; location; hours of operation; injunction; classification; definitions): 8. "Escort agency" means a person or business association that furnishes, offers to furnish or advertises the furnishing of escorts as one of its primary business purposes for any fee, tip or other consideration.
ARS § 13-1422 (Adult oriented businesses; location; hours of operation; injunction; classification; definitions): 9. "Nude model studio" has the same meaning prescribed in section 11-811.

ARS § 13-1422 (Adult oriented businesses; location; hours of operation; injunction; classification; definitions): 10. "Nude", "nudity" or "state of nudity" has the same meaning prescribed in section 11-811.

ARS § 13-1422 (Adult oriented businesses; location; hours of operation; injunction; classification; definitions): 11. "Place of worship" means a structure where persons regularly assemble for worship, ceremonies, rituals and education relating to a particular form of religious belief and which a reasonable person would conclude is a place of worship by reason of design, signs or architectural or other features.
ARS § 13-1422 (Adult oriented businesses; location; hours of operation; injunction; classification; definitions): 12. "Residence" means a permanent dwelling place.
ARS § 13-1422 (Adult oriented businesses; location; hours of operation; injunction; classification; definitions): 13. "Seminude" has the same meaning prescribed in section 11-811.
ARS § 13-1422 (Adult oriented businesses; location; hours of operation; injunction; classification; definitions): 14. "Specific anatomical areas" has the same meaning prescribed in section 11-811.
ARS § 13-1422 (Adult oriented businesses; location; hours of operation; injunction; classification; definitions): 15. "Specific sexual activities" has the same meaning prescribed in section 11-811.

ARS § 13-1423 (Violent sexual assault; natural life sentence): A. A person is guilty of violent sexual assault if in the course of committing an offense under section 13-1404, 13-1405, 13-1406 or 13-1410 the offense involved the discharge, use or threatening exhibition of a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument or involved the intentional or knowing infliction of serious physical injury and the person has a historical prior felony conviction for a sexual offense under this chapter or any offense committed outside this state that if committed in this state would constitute a sexual offense under this chapter.

ARS § 13-1423 (Violent sexual assault; natural life sentence): B. Notwithstanding section 13-703, section 13-704, section 13-705, section 13-706, subsection A and section 13-708, subsection D, a person who is guilty of a violent sexual assault shall be sentenced to life imprisonment and the court shall order that the person not be released on any basis for the remainder of the person's natural life.
ARS § 13-1424 (Voyeurism; classification): A. It is unlawful to knowingly invade the privacy of another person without the knowledge of the other person for the purpose of sexual stimulation.

ARS § 13-1424 (Voyeurism; classification): B. It is unlawful for a person to disclose, display, distribute or publish a photograph, videotape, film or digital recording that is made in violation of subsection A of this section without the consent or knowledge of the person depicted.
ARS § 13-1424 (Voyeurism; classification): C. For the purposes of this section, a person's privacy is invaded if both of the following apply:
ARS § 13-1424 (Voyeurism; classification): 1. The person has a reasonable expectation that the person will not be photographed, videotaped, filmed, digitally recorded or otherwise viewed or recorded.
ARS § 13-1424 (Voyeurism; classification): 2. The person is photographed, videotaped, filmed, digitally recorded or otherwise viewed, with or without a device, either:
ARS § 13-1424 (Voyeurism; classification): (a) While the person is in a state of undress or partial dress.
ARS § 13-1424 (Voyeurism; classification): (b) While the person is engaged in sexual intercourse or sexual contact.
ARS § 13-1424 (Voyeurism; classification): (c) While the person is urinating or defecating.

ARS § 13-1424 (Voyeurism; classification): (d) In a manner that directly or indirectly captures or allows the viewing of the person's genitalia, buttock or female breast, whether clothed or unclothed, that is not otherwise visible to the public.
ARS § 13-1424 (Voyeurism; classification): D. This section does not apply to any of the following:

ARS § 13-1424 (Voyeurism; classification): 1. Photographing, videotaping, filming or digitally recording for security purposes if notice of the use of the photographing, videotaping, filming or digital recording equipment is clearly posted in the location and the location is one in which the person has a reasonable expectation of privacy.

ARS § 13-1424 (Voyeurism; classification): 2. Photographing, videotaping, filming or digitally recording by correctional officials for security reasons or in connection with the investigation of alleged misconduct of persons on the premises of a jail or prison.
ARS § 13-1424 (Voyeurism; classification): 3. Photographing, videotaping, filming or digitally recording by law enforcement officers pursuant to an investigation, which is otherwise lawful.
ARS § 13-1424 (Voyeurism; classification): 4. The use of a child monitoring device as defined in section 13-3001.

ARS § 13-1424 (Voyeurism; classification): E. A violation of subsection A or B of this section is a class 5 felony, except that a violation of subsection B of this section is a class 4 felony if the person depicted is recognizable.

ARS § 13-1425 (Unlawful disclosure of images depicting states of nudity or specific sexual activities; classification; definitions): A. It is unlawful for a person to intentionally disclose an image of another person who is identifiable from the image itself or from information displayed in connection with the image if all of the following apply:

ARS § 13-1425 (Unlawful disclosure of images depicting states of nudity or specific sexual activities; classification; definitions): 1. The person in the image is depicted in a state of nudity or is engaged in specific sexual activities.

ARS § 13-1425 (Unlawful disclosure of images depicting states of nudity or specific sexual activities; classification; definitions): 2. The depicted person has a reasonable expectation of privacy.  Evidence that a person has sent an image to another person using an electronic device does not, on its own, remove the person's reasonable expectation of privacy for that image. Unless the realistic pictorial representation is created or modified by the depicted person, this paragraph does not apply to an image that is a realistic pictorial representation.

ARS § 13-1425 (Unlawful disclosure of images depicting states of nudity or specific sexual activities; classification; definitions): 3. The image is disclosed with the intent to harm, harass, intimidate, threaten or coerce the depicted person.
ARS § 13-1425 (Unlawful disclosure of images depicting states of nudity or specific sexual activities; classification; definitions): B. This section does not apply to any of the following:
ARS § 13-1425 (Unlawful disclosure of images depicting states of nudity or specific sexual activities; classification; definitions): 1. The reporting of unlawful conduct.

ARS § 13-1425 (Unlawful disclosure of images depicting states of nudity or specific sexual activities; classification; definitions): 2. Lawful and common practices of law enforcement, criminal reporting, legal proceedings or medical treatment.

ARS § 13-1425 (Unlawful disclosure of images depicting states of nudity or specific sexual activities; classification; definitions): 3. Images involving voluntary exposure in a public or commercial setting.

ARS § 13-1425 (Unlawful disclosure of images depicting states of nudity or specific sexual activities; classification; definitions): 4. An interactive computer service, as defined in 47 United States Code section 230(f)(2), or an information service or cable service, as defined in 47 United States Code section 153, with regard to content wholly provided by another party.

ARS § 13-1425 (Unlawful disclosure of images depicting states of nudity or specific sexual activities; classification; definitions): 5. Any disclosure that is made with the consent of the person who is depicted in the image.

ARS § 13-1425 (Unlawful disclosure of images depicting states of nudity or specific sexual activities; classification; definitions): C. A violation of this section is a class 5 felony, except that a violation of this section is a:
ARS § 13-1425 (Unlawful disclosure of images depicting states of nudity or specific sexual activities; classification; definitions): 1. Class 4 felony if the image is disclosed by electronic means.

ARS § 13-1425 (Unlawful disclosure of images depicting states of nudity or specific sexual activities; classification; definitions): 2. Class 1 misdemeanor if a person threatens to disclose but does not disclose an image that if disclosed would be a violation of this section or if the image is a realistic pictorial representation.
ARS § 13-1425 (Unlawful disclosure of images depicting states of nudity or specific sexual activities; classification; definitions): D. For the purposes of this section:

ARS § 13-1425 (Unlawful disclosure of images depicting states of nudity or specific sexual activities; classification; definitions): 1. "Disclose" means display, distribute, publish, advertise or offer.

ARS § 13-1425 (Unlawful disclosure of images depicting states of nudity or specific sexual activities; classification; definitions): 2. "Disclosed by electronic means" means delivery to an email address, mobile device, tablet or other electronic device and includes disclosure on a website.

ARS § 13-1425 (Unlawful disclosure of images depicting states of nudity or specific sexual activities; classification; definitions): 3. "Harm" means physical injury, financial injury or serious emotional distress.

ARS § 13-1425 (Unlawful disclosure of images depicting states of nudity or specific sexual activities; classification; definitions): 4. "Image" means a photograph, videotape, film, digital recording or realistic pictorial representation.
ARS § 13-1425 (Unlawful disclosure of images depicting states of nudity or specific sexual activities; classification; definitions): 5. "Realistic pictorial representation":

ARS § 13-1425 (Unlawful disclosure of images depicting states of nudity or specific sexual activities; classification; definitions): (a) Means an image that is created or modified to reasonably appear to be an actual image of an identifiable person depicted in a state of nudity or engaged in specific sexual activities that did not actually occur.

ARS § 13-1425 (Unlawful disclosure of images depicting states of nudity or specific sexual activities; classification; definitions): (b) Does not include an image made in the public interest, including scientific or educational activities, a newsworthy event or an issue of public concern.

ARS § 13-1425 (Unlawful disclosure of images depicting states of nudity or specific sexual activities; classification; definitions): 6. "Reasonable expectation of privacy" means the person exhibits an actual expectation of privacy and the expectation is reasonable.

ARS § 13-1425 (Unlawful disclosure of images depicting states of nudity or specific sexual activities; classification; definitions): 7. "Specific sexual activities" has the same meaning prescribed in section 11-811, subsection E, paragraph 18, subdivisions (a) and (b).

ARS § 13-1425 (Unlawful disclosure of images depicting states of nudity or specific sexual activities; classification; definitions): 8. "State of nudity" has the same meaning prescribed in section 11-811, subsection E, paragraph 14, subdivision (a).

ARS § 13-1426 (Sexual assault investigations; collected biological evidence testing; definitions): A. A health care facility that obtains written consent to release sexual assault kit evidence shall notify the investigating law enforcement agency, if known, or the law enforcement agency that has jurisdiction in that portion of the local unit of government in which the health care facility is located within forty-eight hours after the sexual assault kit evidence collection.

ARS § 13-1426 (Sexual assault investigations; collected biological evidence testing; definitions): B. A law enforcement agency that receives notice pursuant to subsection A of this section must take possession of the sexual assault kit evidence from the health care facility within five business days after notification.

ARS § 13-1426 (Sexual assault investigations; collected biological evidence testing; definitions): C. The investigating law enforcement agency must submit the sexual assault kit evidence to a public accredited crime laboratory for forensic analysis within fifteen business days after its receipt in all cases in which a victim reports to law enforcement and law enforcement determines that a crime occurred.

ARS § 13-1426 (Sexual assault investigations; collected biological evidence testing; definitions): D. All sexual assault examination kits that are submitted for analysis must be analyzed as soon as practicable if sufficient personnel and resources are available.

ARS § 13-1426 (Sexual assault investigations; collected biological evidence testing; definitions): E. The public accredited crime laboratory shall ensure that all eligible DNA profiles are uploaded into:

ARS § 13-1426 (Sexual assault investigations; collected biological evidence testing; definitions): 1. Databases that are maintained by the state law enforcement agency, if the DNA profile meets the requirements of the state database comparison policies.

ARS § 13-1426 (Sexual assault investigations; collected biological evidence testing; definitions): 2. Databases that are maintained by municipal law enforcement agencies, if the DNA profile meets the requirements of the municipal crime laboratory comparison policies.

ARS § 13-1426 (Sexual assault investigations; collected biological evidence testing; definitions): 3. The combined DNA index system database established by the federal bureau of investigation, if the DNA profile meets the requirements of the bureau's comparison policies.

ARS § 13-1426 (Sexual assault investigations; collected biological evidence testing; definitions): F. A public accredited crime laboratory may contract with a private accredited crime laboratory, as appropriate, to perform the analysis that is required by this section, subject to the necessary quality assurance reviews by the public accredited crime laboratory.

ARS § 13-1426 (Sexual assault investigations; collected biological evidence testing; definitions): G. The failure of a law enforcement agency to submit a request for analysis within the time limits prescribed by this section does not constitute grounds in any criminal or civil proceeding to challenge the validity of a DNA evidence association and a court may not exclude any evidence obtained from the sexual assault examination kit on those grounds.

ARS § 13-1426 (Sexual assault investigations; collected biological evidence testing; definitions): H. A person who is accused or convicted of committing a crime against a victim does not have standing to object to any failure to comply with this section and such failure is not grounds for setting aside a conviction or sentence.

ARS § 13-1426 (Sexual assault investigations; collected biological evidence testing; definitions): I. This section does not establish a private right of action or claim on the part of any individual, entity or agency against any law enforcement agency or any contractor of a law enforcement agency.
ARS § 13-1426 (Sexual assault investigations; collected biological evidence testing; definitions): J. For the purposes of this section:

ARS § 13-1426 (Sexual assault investigations; collected biological evidence testing; definitions): 1. "Law enforcement agency" means the police department of any state, county, municipality or postsecondary educational institution or for any agency that has an agreement in place for evidence analysis.

ARS § 13-1426 (Sexual assault investigations; collected biological evidence testing; definitions): 2. "Public accredited crime laboratory" means a crime laboratory that is established pursuant to section 41-1771 or a municipal crime laboratory.

ARS § 13-1427 (Sexual assault kits; annual report; definitions): A. On or before August 30 of each year, each law enforcement agency shall report to the department of public safety on a form prescribed by the department of public safety:
ARS § 13-1427 (Sexual assault kits; annual report; definitions): 1. The number of sexual assault kits that the agency received.
ARS § 13-1427 (Sexual assault kits; annual report; definitions): 2. The number of sexual assault kits that were submitted to a public accredited crime laboratory for analysis.
ARS § 13-1427 (Sexual assault kits; annual report; definitions): 3. The number of sexual assault kits that were not submitted to a public accredited crime laboratory for analysis.

ARS § 13-1427 (Sexual assault kits; annual report; definitions): 4. The reason or reasons for not submitting evidence from each sexual assault kit to a public accredited crime laboratory for analysis.
ARS § 13-1427 (Sexual assault kits; annual report; definitions): B. On or before August 30 of each year, each public accredited crime laboratory shall report to the department of public safety:
ARS § 13-1427 (Sexual assault kits; annual report; definitions): 1. The number of sexual assault kits that the laboratory received.
ARS § 13-1427 (Sexual assault kits; annual report; definitions): 2. The number of sexual assault kits that were not analyzed and the reason or reasons that the kits were not analyzed.

ARS § 13-1427 (Sexual assault kits; annual report; definitions): C. On or before December 1 of each year, the department of public safety shall report to the governor, the president of the senate and the speaker of the house of representatives on the compilation of the reports that are received from each public accredited crime laboratory and each law enforcement agency pursuant to subsections A and B of this section. The report must include any reconciliation and recommendations for increased compliance if necessary. The department of public safety shall post the reports on the department's website.

ARS § 13-1427 (Sexual assault kits; annual report; definitions): D. For the purposes of this section, "law enforcement agency" and "public accredited crime laboratory" have the same meanings prescribed in section 13-1426.

ARS § 13-1428 (Sexual extortion; classification; definition): A. A person commits sexual extortion by knowingly communicating a threat with the intent to coerce another person to do any of the following:
ARS § 13-1428 (Sexual extortion; classification; definition): 1. Engage in sexual contact or sexual intercourse.
ARS § 13-1428 (Sexual extortion; classification; definition): 2. Allow the other person's genitals, anus or female breast to be photographed, filmed, videotaped or digitally recorded.
ARS § 13-1428 (Sexual extortion; classification; definition): 3. Exhibit the other person's genitals, anus or female breast.

ARS § 13-1428 (Sexual extortion; classification; definition): B. Sexual extortion is a class 3 felony and the person is not eligible for suspension of sentence, probation, pardon or release from confinement on any basis except as specifically authorized by section 31-233, subsection A or B until the sentence imposed by the court has been served or commuted. If the victim is under fifteen years of age, sexual extortion is a class 2 felony and is punishable pursuant to section 13-705.
ARS § 13-1428 (Sexual extortion; classification; definition): C. For the purposes of this section, "communicating a threat" means a threat to do any of the following:
ARS § 13-1428 (Sexual extortion; classification; definition): 1. Damage the property of the other person.
ARS § 13-1428 (Sexual extortion; classification; definition): 2. Harm the reputation of the other person.

ARS § 13-1428 (Sexual extortion; classification; definition): 3. Produce or distribute a photograph, film, videotape or digital recording that depicts the other person engaging in sexual contact or sexual intercourse or the exhibition of the other person's genitals, anus or female breast.

ARS § 13-1429 (Possessing, trafficking or importing a child sex doll; classification; annual report; definition): A. A person commits possessing a child sex doll by intentionally or knowingly possessing a child sex doll.

ARS § 13-1429 (Possessing, trafficking or importing a child sex doll; classification; annual report; definition): B. A person commits trafficking a child sex doll by knowingly manufacturing, distributing, selling, transferring, offering to sell, advertising, providing, shipping, delivering for shipment, offering to deliver for shipment or possessing with the intent to manufacture, distribute, sell, ship or transfer a child sex doll.

ARS § 13-1429 (Possessing, trafficking or importing a child sex doll; classification; annual report; definition): C. A person commits importing a child sex doll by knowingly transporting a child sex doll into this state by any means with the intent to distribute, sell or transfer the child sex doll.

ARS § 13-1429 (Possessing, trafficking or importing a child sex doll; classification; annual report; definition): D. In a prosecution for a violation of subsection B of this section, unless satisfactorily explained, the possession of two or more child sex dolls may give rise to an inference that a person intends to commit trafficking a child sex doll.

ARS § 13-1429 (Possessing, trafficking or importing a child sex doll; classification; annual report; definition): E. This section does not apply to a common carrier transporting a container with a child sex doll if the common carrier does not have knowledge of the container's contents.

ARS § 13-1429 (Possessing, trafficking or importing a child sex doll; classification; annual report; definition): F. On or before December 31, 2024 and each year thereafter, the administrative office of the courts shall submit a report to the president of the senate, the speaker of the house of representatives, the minority leader in the senate and the minority leader in the house of representatives that lists, by county, the total number of persons who have been convicted of a violation of this section.
ARS § 13-1429 (Possessing, trafficking or importing a child sex doll; classification; annual report; definition): G. A violation of this section is a class 4 felony.

ARS § 13-1429 (Possessing, trafficking or importing a child sex doll; classification; annual report; definition): H. For the purposes of this section, "child sex doll" means an anatomically correct doll, mannequin or robot that both:

ARS § 13-1429 (Possessing, trafficking or importing a child sex doll; classification; annual report; definition): 1. Has the features of or features that resemble those of an infant or a child who is under twelve years of age.
ARS § 13-1429 (Possessing, trafficking or importing a child sex doll; classification; annual report; definition): 2. Is intended to be used for sexual stimulation or gratification.
ARS § 13-1430 (Child enticement; classification; definitions): A. A person commits child enticement by knowingly doing either of the following:

ARS § 13-1430 (Child enticement; classification; definitions): 1. Using an electronic communication device, performing an act in person or through a third party or using any written communication to lure or entice or attempt to lure or entice a minor to distribute a visual depiction of a person’s genitals or the female breast.
ARS § 13-1430 (Child enticement; classification; definitions): 2. Committing any act in furtherance of or to facilitate the sexual abuse of the minor.

ARS § 13-1430 (Child enticement; classification; definitions): B. This section does not prohibit the distribution of a visual depiction that taken as a whole has serious literary, artistic, political or scientific value for minors.
ARS § 13-1430 (Child enticement; classification; definitions): C. Child enticement is a class 5 felony, except that child enticement is a class 4 felony if the defendant is in a position of trust.
ARS § 13-1430 (Child enticement; classification; definitions): D. For the purposes of this section:
ARS § 13-1430 (Child enticement; classification; definitions): 1. "Electronic communication device" has the same meaning as in section 13-3561.
ARS § 13-1430 (Child enticement; classification; definitions): 2. "Sexual abuse" includes any offense in chapter 14 or 35.1 of this title or section 13-3212.
ARS § 13-1430 (Child enticement; classification; definitions): 3. "Visual depiction" has the same meaning as in section 13-3551.
ARS § 13-1501 (Definitions): In this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires:
ARS § 13-1501 (Definitions): 1. "Critical public service facility" means:

ARS § 13-1501 (Definitions): (a) A structure or fenced yard that is posted with signage indicating it is a felony to trespass or signage indicating high voltage or high pressure and is used by a rail, bus, air or other mass transit provider, a public or private utility, any municipal corporation, city, town or other political subdivision that is organized under state law and that generates, transmits, distributes or otherwise provides natural gas, liquefied petroleum gas, electricity or a combustible substance for a delivery system that is not a retail-only facility, a telecommunications carrier or telephone company, a municipal provider as defined in section 45-561, a law enforcement agency, a public or private fire department or an emergency medical service provider.

ARS § 13-1501 (Definitions): (b) A structure or fenced yard or any equipment or apparatus that is posted with signage indicating it is a felony to trespass or signage indicating high voltage or high pressure and is used to manufacture, extract, transport, distribute or store gas, including natural gas or liquefied petroleum gas, oil, electricity, water or hazardous materials, unless it is a retail-only facility.

ARS § 13-1501 (Definitions): 2. "Enter or remain unlawfully" means an act of a person who enters or remains on premises when the person's intent for so entering or remaining is not licensed, authorized or otherwise privileged except when the entry is to commit theft of merchandise displayed for sale during normal business hours, when the premises are open to the public and when the person does not enter any unauthorized areas of the premises.
ARS § 13-1501 (Definitions): 3. "Entry" means the intrusion of any part of any instrument or any part of a person's body inside the external boundaries of a structure or unit of real property.

ARS § 13-1501 (Definitions): 4. "Fenced commercial yard" means a unit of real property that is surrounded completely by fences, walls, buildings or similar barriers, or any combination of fences, walls, buildings or similar barriers, and that is zoned for business operations or where livestock, produce or other commercial items are located.

ARS § 13-1501 (Definitions): 5. "Fenced residential yard" means a unit of real property that immediately surrounds or is adjacent to a residential structure and that is enclosed by a fence, wall, building or similar barrier or any combination of fences, walls, buildings or similar barriers.

ARS § 13-1501 (Definitions): 6. "Fenced yard" means a unit of real property that is surrounded by fences, walls, buildings or similar barriers or any combination of fences, walls, buildings or similar barriers.
ARS § 13-1501 (Definitions): 7. "In the course of committing" means any acts that are performed by an intruder from the moment of entry to and including flight from the scene of a crime.

ARS § 13-1501 (Definitions): 8. "Manipulation key" means a key, device or instrument, other than a key that is designed to operate a specific lock, that can be variably positioned and manipulated in a vehicle keyway to operate a lock or cylinder, including a wiggle key, jiggle key or rocker key.
ARS § 13-1501 (Definitions): 9. "Master key" means a key that operates all the keyed locks or cylinders in a similar type or group of locks.
ARS § 13-1501 (Definitions): 10. "Nonresidential structure" means any structure other than a residential structure and includes a retail establishment.

ARS § 13-1501 (Definitions): 11. "Residential structure" means any structure, movable or immovable, permanent or temporary, that is adapted for both human residence and lodging whether occupied or not.

ARS § 13-1501 (Definitions): 12. "Structure" means any device that accepts electronic or physical currency and that is used to conduct commercial transactions, any vending machine or any building, object, vehicle, railroad car or place with sides and a floor that is separately securable from any other structure attached to it and that is used for lodging, business, transportation, recreation or storage.

ARS § 13-1501 (Definitions): 13. "Vending machine" means a machine that dispenses merchandise or service through the means of currency, coin, token, credit card or other nonpersonal means of accepting payment for merchandise or service received.
ARS § 13-1502 (Criminal trespass in the third degree; classification): A. A person commits criminal trespass in the third degree by:

ARS § 13-1502 (Criminal trespass in the third degree; classification): 1. Knowingly entering or remaining unlawfully on any real property after a reasonable request to leave by a law enforcement officer, the owner or any other person having lawful control over such property, or reasonable notice prohibiting entry.

ARS § 13-1502 (Criminal trespass in the third degree; classification): 2. Knowingly entering or remaining unlawfully on the right-of-way for tracks, or the storage or switching yards or rolling stock of a railroad company.

ARS § 13-1502 (Criminal trespass in the third degree; classification): B. Pursuant to subsection A, paragraph 1 of this section, a request to leave by a law enforcement officer acting at the request of the owner of the property or any other person having lawful control over the property has the same legal effect as a request made by the property owner or other person having lawful control of the property.
ARS § 13-1502 (Criminal trespass in the third degree; classification): C. Criminal trespass in the third degree is a class 3 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-1503 (Criminal trespass in the second degree; classification): A. A person commits criminal trespass in the second degree by knowingly entering or remaining unlawfully in or on any nonresidential structure or in any fenced commercial yard.
ARS § 13-1503 (Criminal trespass in the second degree; classification): B. Criminal trespass in the second degree is a class 2 misdemeanor.
ARS § 13-1504 (Criminal trespass in the first degree; classification): A. A person commits criminal trespass in the first degree by knowingly:
ARS § 13-1504 (Criminal trespass in the first degree; classification): 1. Entering or remaining unlawfully in or on a residential structure.
ARS § 13-1504 (Criminal trespass in the first degree; classification): 2. Entering or remaining unlawfully in a fenced residential yard.

ARS § 13-1504 (Criminal trespass in the first degree; classification): 3. Entering any residential yard and, without lawful authority, looking into the residential structure thereon in reckless disregard of infringing on the inhabitant's right of privacy.

ARS § 13-1504 (Criminal trespass in the first degree; classification): 4. Entering unlawfully on real property that is subject to a valid mineral claim or lease with the intent to hold, work, take or explore for minerals on the claim or lease.

ARS § 13-1504 (Criminal trespass in the first degree; classification): 5. Entering or remaining unlawfully on the property of another and burning, defacing, mutilating or otherwise desecrating a religious symbol or other religious property of another without the express permission of the owner of the property.
ARS § 13-1504 (Criminal trespass in the first degree; classification): 6. Entering or remaining unlawfully in or on a critical public service facility.

ARS § 13-1504 (Criminal trespass in the first degree; classification): B. Criminal trespass in the first degree under subsection A, paragraph 6 of this section is a class 5 felony.  Criminal trespass in the first degree under subsection A, paragraph 1 or 5 of this section is a class 6 felony.  Criminal trespass in the first degree under subsection A, paragraph 2, 3 or 4 of this section is a class 1 misdemeanor.
ARS § 13-1505 (Possession of burglary tools; master key; manipulation key; classification): A. A person commits possession of burglary tools by:

ARS § 13-1505 (Possession of burglary tools; master key; manipulation key; classification): 1. Possessing any explosive, tool, instrument or other article adapted or commonly used for committing any form of burglary as defined in sections 13-1506, 13-1507 and 13-1508 and intending to use or permit the use of such an item in the commission of a burglary.
ARS § 13-1505 (Possession of burglary tools; master key; manipulation key; classification): 2. Buying, selling, transferring, possessing or using a motor vehicle manipulation key or master key.
ARS § 13-1505 (Possession of burglary tools; master key; manipulation key; classification): B. Subsection A, paragraph 2 of this section does not apply to a person who either:

ARS § 13-1505 (Possession of burglary tools; master key; manipulation key; classification): 1. Uses a master key in the course of the person's lawful business or occupation, including licensed vehicle dealers and manufacturers, key manufacturers who are engaged in the business of designing, making, altering, duplicating or repairing locks or keys, locksmiths, loan institutions that finance vehicles and law enforcement.

ARS § 13-1505 (Possession of burglary tools; master key; manipulation key; classification): 2. Transfers, possesses or uses no more than one manipulation key, unless the manipulation key is transferred, possessed or used with the intent to commit any theft or felony.
ARS § 13-1505 (Possession of burglary tools; master key; manipulation key; classification): C. Possession of burglary tools is a class 6 felony.
ARS § 13-1506 (Burglary in the third degree; classification): A. A person commits burglary in the third degree by:

ARS § 13-1506 (Burglary in the third degree; classification): 1. Entering or remaining unlawfully in or on a nonresidential structure or in a fenced commercial or residential yard with the intent to commit any theft or any felony therein.

ARS § 13-1506 (Burglary in the third degree; classification): 2. Making entry into any part of a motor vehicle by means of a manipulation key or master key, with the intent to commit any theft or felony in the motor vehicle.
ARS § 13-1506 (Burglary in the third degree; classification): B. Burglary in the third degree is a class 4 felony.

ARS § 13-1507 (Burglary in the second degree; classification): A. A person commits burglary in the second degree by entering or remaining unlawfully in or on a residential structure with the intent to commit any theft or any felony therein.
ARS § 13-1507 (Burglary in the second degree; classification): B. Burglary in the second degree is a class 3 felony.

ARS § 13-1508 (Burglary in the first degree; classification): A. A person commits burglary in the first degree if such person or an accomplice violates the provisions of either section 13-1506 or 13-1507 and knowingly possesses explosives, a deadly weapon or a dangerous instrument in the course of committing any theft or any felony.

ARS § 13-1508 (Burglary in the first degree; classification): B. Burglary in the first degree of a nonresidential structure or a fenced commercial or residential yard is a class 3 felony. It is a class 2 felony if committed in a residential structure.

ARS § 13-1509 (Willful failure to complete or carry an alien registration document; exception; authenticated records;): A. In addition to any violation of federal law, a person is guilty of willful failure to complete or carry an alien registration document if the person is in violation of 8 United States Code section 1304(e) or 1306(a).

ARS § 13-1509 (Willful failure to complete or carry an alien registration document; exception; authenticated records;): B. In the enforcement of this section, an alien's immigration status may be determined by:

ARS § 13-1509 (Willful failure to complete or carry an alien registration document; exception; authenticated records;): 1. A law enforcement officer who is authorized by the federal government to verify or ascertain an alien's immigration status.

ARS § 13-1509 (Willful failure to complete or carry an alien registration document; exception; authenticated records;): 2. The United States immigration and customs enforcement or the United States customs and border protection pursuant to 8 United States Code section 1373(c).

ARS § 13-1509 (Willful failure to complete or carry an alien registration document; exception; authenticated records;): C. A law enforcement official or agency of this state or a county, city, town or other political subdivision of this state may not consider race, color or national origin in the enforcement of this section except to the extent permitted by the United States or Arizona Constitution.

ARS § 13-1509 (Willful failure to complete or carry an alien registration document; exception; authenticated records;): D. A person who is sentenced pursuant to this section is not eligible for suspension of sentence, probation, pardon, commutation of sentence, or release from confinement on any basis except as authorized by section 31-233, subsection A or B until the sentence imposed by the court has been served or the person is eligible for release pursuant to section 41-1604.07.

ARS § 13-1509 (Willful failure to complete or carry an alien registration document; exception; authenticated records;): E. In addition to any other penalty prescribed by law, the court shall order the person to pay jail costs.

ARS § 13-1509 (Willful failure to complete or carry an alien registration document; exception; authenticated records;): F. This section does not apply to a person who maintains authorization from the federal government to remain in the United States.

ARS § 13-1509 (Willful failure to complete or carry an alien registration document; exception; authenticated records;): G. Any record that relates to the immigration status of a person is admissible in any court without further foundation or testimony from a custodian of records if the record is certified as authentic by the government agency that is responsible for maintaining the record.

ARS § 13-1509 (Willful failure to complete or carry an alien registration document; exception; authenticated records;): H. A violation of this section is a class 1 misdemeanor, except that the maximum fine is one hundred dollars and for a first violation of this section the court shall not sentence the person to more than twenty days in jail and for a second or subsequent violation the court shall not sentence the person to more than thirty days in jail.
ARS § 13-1601 (Definitions): In this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires:
ARS § 13-1601 (Definitions): 1. "Damaging" means damage as defined in section 13-1701.

ARS § 13-1601 (Definitions): 2. "Defacing" means any unnecessary act of substantially marring any surface or place, by any means, or any act of putting up, affixing, fastening, printing or painting any notice on any structure, without permission from the owner.

ARS § 13-1601 (Definitions): 3. "Litter" includes any rubbish, refuse, waste material, offal, paper, glass, cans, bottles, organic or inorganic trash, debris, filthy or odoriferous objects, dead animals or any foreign substance of whatever kind or description, including junked or abandoned vehicles, whether or not any of these items are of value.

ARS § 13-1601 (Definitions): 4. "Property of another" means property in which any person other than the defendant has an interest, including community property and other property in which the defendant also has an interest and, for damage caused by theft of scrap metal, the property of other persons damaged directly or indirectly as a result of the acts of the defendant.
ARS § 13-1601 (Definitions): 5. "Tamper" means any act of interference.

ARS § 13-1601 (Definitions): 6. "Tampering with utility property" means any of the following if committed against property that is owned or operated by a utility for the purposes of transmission or distribution:
ARS § 13-1601 (Definitions): (a) Rearranging, damaging, altering, interfering with or otherwise preventing the performance of a normal or customary function of utility property.
ARS § 13-1601 (Definitions): (b) Connecting any wire, conduit or device to any utility property without authorization.
ARS § 13-1601 (Definitions): (c) Defacing, puncturing, removing, reversing or altering any utility property.
ARS § 13-1601 (Definitions): (d) Preventing any meter from properly measuring or registering.
ARS § 13-1601 (Definitions): (e) Taking, receiving, using or converting to personal use or the use of another any utility service that has not been measured or authorized.
ARS § 13-1601 (Definitions): (f) Diverting or changing the intended course or path of the utility service without the authorization or consent of the utility.
ARS § 13-1601 (Definitions): (g) Causing, procuring, permitting, aiding or abetting any person to do any of the acts listed in this paragraph.

ARS § 13-1601 (Definitions): 7. "Utility" means any enterprise, public or private, that provides gas, electric, irrigation, steam, water, water conservation, sewer or communications services, as well as any common carrier on land, rail, sea or air.
ARS § 13-1602 (Criminal damage; classification): A. A person commits criminal damage by:
ARS § 13-1602 (Criminal damage; classification): 1. Recklessly defacing or damaging property of another person.
ARS § 13-1602 (Criminal damage; classification): 2. Recklessly tampering with property of another person so as substantially to impair its function or value.
ARS § 13-1602 (Criminal damage; classification): 3. Recklessly damaging property of a utility.
ARS § 13-1602 (Criminal damage; classification): 4. Recklessly physically obstructing a passageway in such a manner as to deprive livestock of access to the only reasonably available water.

ARS § 13-1602 (Criminal damage; classification): 5. Recklessly drawing or inscribing a message, slogan, sign or symbol that is made on any public or private building, structure or surface, except the ground, and that is made without permission of the owner.
ARS § 13-1602 (Criminal damage; classification): 6. Intentionally tampering with utility property.
ARS § 13-1602 (Criminal damage; classification): B. Criminal damage is punished as follows:
ARS § 13-1602 (Criminal damage; classification): 1. Criminal damage is a class 4 felony if the person recklessly damages property of another in an amount of $10,000 or more.

ARS § 13-1602 (Criminal damage; classification): 2. Criminal damage is a class 4 felony if the person recklessly damages the property of a utility in an amount of $5,000 or more or if the person intentionally tampers with utility property and the damage causes an imminent safety hazard to any person.

ARS § 13-1602 (Criminal damage; classification): 3. Criminal damage is a class 5 felony if the person recklessly damages property of another in an amount of $2,000 or more but less than $10,000 or if the damage is inflicted to promote, further or assist any criminal street gang or criminal syndicate with the intent to intimidate and the person is not subject to paragraph 1 or 2 of this subsection.
ARS § 13-1602 (Criminal damage; classification): 4. Criminal damage is a class 6 felony if the person recklessly damages property of another in an amount of $1,000 or more but less than $2,000.
ARS § 13-1602 (Criminal damage; classification): 5. Criminal damage is a class 1 misdemeanor if the person recklessly damages property of another in an amount of more than $250 but less than $1,000.
ARS § 13-1602 (Criminal damage; classification): 6. In all other cases criminal damage is a class 2 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-1602 (Criminal damage; classification): C. For a violation of subsection A, paragraph 5 of this section, in determining the amount of damage to property, damages include reasonable labor costs of any kind, reasonable material costs of any kind and any reasonable costs that are attributed to equipment that is used to abate or repair the damage to the property.
ARS § 13-1603 (Criminal littering or polluting; classification): A. A person commits criminal littering or polluting if the person without lawful authority does any of the following:

ARS § 13-1603 (Criminal littering or polluting; classification): 1. Throws, places, drops or permits to be dropped on public property or property of another that is not a lawful dump any litter, destructive or injurious material that the person does not immediately remove.

ARS § 13-1603 (Criminal littering or polluting; classification): 2. Discharges or permits to be discharged any sewage, oil products or other harmful substances into any waters or onto any shorelines within this state.
ARS § 13-1603 (Criminal littering or polluting; classification): 3. Dumps any earth, soil, stones, ores or minerals on any land.
ARS § 13-1603 (Criminal littering or polluting; classification): B. Criminal littering or polluting is punishable as follows:

ARS § 13-1603 (Criminal littering or polluting; classification): 1. A class 6 felony if the act is a knowing violation of subsection A in which the amount of litter or other prohibited material or substance exceeds three hundred pounds in weight or one hundred cubic feet in volume or is done in any quantity for a commercial purpose.

ARS § 13-1603 (Criminal littering or polluting; classification): 2. A class 1 misdemeanor if the act is a knowing violation of subsection A, paragraph 1 in which the amount of litter or prohibited material or substance is more than one hundred pounds in weight but less than three hundred pounds in weight or more than thirty-five cubic feet in volume but less than one hundred cubic feet in volume and is not done for a commercial purpose.

ARS § 13-1603 (Criminal littering or polluting; classification): 3. A class 1 misdemeanor if the act is not punishable under paragraph 1 of this subsection and involves placing any destructive or injurious material on or within fifty feet of a highway, beach or shoreline of any body of water used by the public.
ARS § 13-1603 (Criminal littering or polluting; classification): 4. A class 2 misdemeanor if the act is not punishable under paragraph 1, 2 or 3 of this subsection.

ARS § 13-1603 (Criminal littering or polluting; classification): C. If a fine is assessed for a violation of subsection A, paragraph 1 or 2, one hundred per cent of any assessed fine shall be deposited in the general fund of the county in which the fine was assessed. At least fifty per cent of the fine shall be used by the county for the purposes of illegal dumping cleanup.
ARS § 13-1604 (Aggravated criminal damage; classification): A. A person commits aggravated criminal damage by intentionally or recklessly without the express permission of the owner:

ARS § 13-1604 (Aggravated criminal damage; classification): 1. Defacing, damaging or in any way changing the appearance of any building, structure, personal property or place used for worship or any religious purpose.
ARS § 13-1604 (Aggravated criminal damage; classification): 2. Defacing or damaging any building, structure or place used as a school or as an educational facility.

ARS § 13-1604 (Aggravated criminal damage; classification): 3. Defacing, damaging or tampering with any cemetery, mortuary or personal property of the cemetery or mortuary or other facility used for the purpose of burial or memorializing the dead.

ARS § 13-1604 (Aggravated criminal damage; classification): 4. Defacing, damaging or tampering with any utility or agricultural infrastructure or property, construction site or existing structure for the purpose of obtaining nonferrous metals.
ARS § 13-1604 (Aggravated criminal damage; classification): B. Aggravated criminal damage is punishable as follows:

ARS § 13-1604 (Aggravated criminal damage; classification): 1. If the person intentionally or recklessly does any act described in subsection A of this section that causes damage to the property of another in an amount of ten thousand dollars or more, aggravated criminal damage:
ARS § 13-1604 (Aggravated criminal damage; classification): (a) Resulting from actions described in subsection A, paragraph 1, 2 or 3 of this section is a class 4 felony.
ARS § 13-1604 (Aggravated criminal damage; classification): (b) Resulting from actions described in subsection A, paragraph 4 of this section is a class 3 felony.

ARS § 13-1604 (Aggravated criminal damage; classification): 2. If the person intentionally or recklessly damages property of another in an amount of one thousand five hundred dollars or more but less than ten thousand dollars, aggravated criminal damage:
ARS § 13-1604 (Aggravated criminal damage; classification): (a) Resulting from actions described in subsection A, paragraph 1, 2 or 3 of this section is a class 5 felony.
ARS § 13-1604 (Aggravated criminal damage; classification): (b) Resulting from actions described in subsection A, paragraph 4 of this section is a class 4 felony.
ARS § 13-1604 (Aggravated criminal damage; classification): 3. In all other cases aggravated criminal damage is:
ARS § 13-1604 (Aggravated criminal damage; classification): (a) A class 6 felony if it results from actions described in subsection A, paragraph 1, 2 or 3 of this section.
ARS § 13-1604 (Aggravated criminal damage; classification): (b) A class 5 felony if it results from actions described in subsection A, paragraph 4 of this section.

ARS § 13-1604 (Aggravated criminal damage; classification): C. In determining the amount of damage to property, damages include the cost of repair or replacement of the property that was damaged, the cost of the loss of crops and livestock, reasonable labor costs of any kind, reasonable material costs of any kind and any reasonable costs that are attributed to equipment that is used to abate or repair the damage to the property.

ARS § 13-1605 (Aggregation of amounts of damage): Amounts of damage caused pursuant to one scheme or course of conduct, whether to property of one or more persons, may be aggregated in the indictment or information at the discretion of this state in determining the classification of an offense in violation of this chapter.
ARS § 13-1701 (Definitions): In this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires:
ARS § 13-1701 (Definitions): 1. "Damage" means any physical or visual impairment of any surface.

ARS § 13-1701 (Definitions): 2. "Occupied structure" means any structure as defined in paragraph 4 in which one or more human beings either is or is likely to be present or so near as to be in equivalent danger at the time the fire or explosion occurs. The term includes any dwelling house, whether occupied, unoccupied or vacant.

ARS § 13-1701 (Definitions): 3. "Property" means anything other than a structure which has value, tangible or intangible, public or private, real or personal, including documents evidencing value or ownership.

ARS § 13-1701 (Definitions): 4. "Structure" means any building, object, vehicle, watercraft, aircraft or place with sides and a floor, used for lodging, business, transportation, recreation or storage.
ARS § 13-1701 (Definitions): 5. "Wildland" means any brush covered land, cutover land, forest, grassland or woods.

ARS § 13-1702 (Reckless burning; classification): A. A person commits reckless burning by recklessly causing a fire or explosion which results in damage to an occupied structure, a structure, wildland or property.
ARS § 13-1702 (Reckless burning; classification): B. Reckless burning is a class 1 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-1703 (Arson of a structure or property; classification): A. A person commits arson of a structure or property by knowingly and unlawfully damaging a structure or property by knowingly causing a fire or explosion.

ARS § 13-1703 (Arson of a structure or property; classification): B. Arson of a structure is a class 4 felony. Arson of property is a class 4 felony if the property had a value of more than one thousand dollars. Arson of property is a class 5 felony if the property had a value of more than one hundred dollars but not more than one thousand dollars. Arson of property is a class 1 misdemeanor if the property had a value of one hundred dollars or less.

ARS § 13-1704 (Arson of an occupied structure; classification): A. A person commits arson of an occupied structure by knowingly and unlawfully damaging an occupied structure by knowingly causing a fire or explosion.
ARS § 13-1704 (Arson of an occupied structure; classification): B. Arson of an occupied structure is a class 2 felony.

ARS § 13-1705 (Arson of an occupied jail or prison facility; classification.): A. A person commits arson of an occupied jail or prison facility by knowingly causing a fire or explosion which results in physical damage to the jail or prison facility.
ARS § 13-1705 (Arson of an occupied jail or prison facility; classification.): B. Arson of an occupied jail or prison facility is a class 4 felony.

ARS § 13-1706 (Burning of wildlands; exceptions; classification): A. It is unlawful for any person, without lawful authority, to intentionally, knowingly, recklessly or with criminal negligence to set or cause to be set on fire any wildland other than the person's own or to permit a fire that was set or caused to be set by the person to pass from the person's own grounds to the grounds of another person.
ARS § 13-1706 (Burning of wildlands; exceptions; classification): B. This section does not apply to any of the following:
ARS § 13-1706 (Burning of wildlands; exceptions; classification): 1. Open burning that is lawfully conducted in the course of agricultural operations.
ARS § 13-1706 (Burning of wildlands; exceptions; classification): 2. Fire management operations that are conducted by a political subdivision.
ARS § 13-1706 (Burning of wildlands; exceptions; classification): 3. Prescribed or controlled burns that are conducted with written authority from the state forester.

ARS § 13-1706 (Burning of wildlands; exceptions; classification): 4. Lawful activities that are conducted pursuant to any rule, regulation or policy that is adopted by a state, tribal or federal agency.

ARS § 13-1706 (Burning of wildlands; exceptions; classification): 5. In absence of a fire ban or other burn restrictions to a person on public lands, setting a fire for purposes of cooking or warming that does not spread sufficiently from its source to require action by a fire control agency.
ARS § 13-1706 (Burning of wildlands; exceptions; classification): C. A person who violates this section is guilty of an offense as follows:
ARS § 13-1706 (Burning of wildlands; exceptions; classification): 1. If done with criminal negligence, the offense is a class 2 misdemeanor.
ARS § 13-1706 (Burning of wildlands; exceptions; classification): 2. If done recklessly, the offense is a class 1 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-1706 (Burning of wildlands; exceptions; classification): 3. If done intentionally or knowingly and the person knows or reasonably should know that the person's conduct violates any order or rule that is issued by a governmental entity and that prohibits, bans, restricts or otherwise regulates fires during periods of extreme fire hazard, the offense is a class 6 felony.

ARS § 13-1706 (Burning of wildlands; exceptions; classification): 4. If done intentionally and the person's conduct places another person in danger of death or serious bodily injury or places any building or occupied structure of another person in danger of damage, the offense is a class 3 felony.

ARS § 13-1707 (Unlawful cross burning; classification): A. It is unlawful for a person to burn or cause to be burned a cross on the property of another person without that person's permission or on a highway or any other public place with the intent to intimidate any person or group of persons.  The intent to intimidate may not be inferred solely from the act of burning a cross, but shall be proven by independent evidence.
ARS § 13-1707 (Unlawful cross burning; classification): B. A person who violates this section is guilty of a class 1 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-1708 (Unlawful symbol burning; classification): A. It is unlawful for a person to burn or cause to be burned any symbol not addressed by section 13-1707 on the property of another person without that person's permission or on a highway or any other public place with the intent to intimidate any person or group of persons.  The intent to intimidate may not be inferred solely from the act of burning the symbol, but shall be proven by independent evidence.
ARS § 13-1708 (Unlawful symbol burning; classification): B. A person who violates this section is guilty of a class 1 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-1709 (Emergency response and investigation costs; civil liability; definitions): A. A person who commits an act in violation of this chapter that results in an appropriate emergency response or investigation and who is convicted of the violation may be liable for the expenses that are incurred incident to the emergency response and the investigation of the commission of the offense.

ARS § 13-1709 (Emergency response and investigation costs; civil liability; definitions): B. The court may assess and collect the expenses prescribed in subsection A.  The court shall state the amount of these expenses as a separate item in any final judgment, order or decree.

ARS § 13-1709 (Emergency response and investigation costs; civil liability; definitions): C. The expenses are a debt of the person. The public agency, for profit entity or nonprofit entity that incurred the expenses may collect the debt proportionally. The liability that is imposed under this section is in addition to and not in limitation of any other liability that may be imposed. If a person is subject to liability under this section and is married, only the separate property of the person is subject to liability.

ARS § 13-1709 (Emergency response and investigation costs; civil liability; definitions): D. There shall be no duty under a policy of liability insurance to defend or indemnify any person found liable for any expenses under this section.
ARS § 13-1709 (Emergency response and investigation costs; civil liability; definitions): E. For the purposes of this section:

ARS § 13-1709 (Emergency response and investigation costs; civil liability; definitions): 1. "Expenses" means reasonable costs that are directly incurred by a public agency, for profit entity or nonprofit entity that makes an appropriate emergency response to an incident or an investigation of the commission of the offense, including the costs of providing police, fire fighting, rescue and emergency medical services at the scene of the incident and the salaries of the persons who respond to the incident but excluding charges assessed by an ambulance service that is regulated pursuant to title 36, chapter 21.1, article 2.

ARS § 13-1709 (Emergency response and investigation costs; civil liability; definitions): 2. "Public agency" means this state, any city, county, municipal corporation or district, any Arizona federally recognized Native American tribe or any other public authority that is located in whole or in part in this state and that provides police, fire fighting, medical or other emergency services.
ARS § 13-1801 (Definitions): A. In this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires:
ARS § 13-1801 (Definitions): 1. "Check" means any check, draft or other negotiable or nonnegotiable instrument of any kind.
ARS § 13-1801 (Definitions): 2. "Control" or "exercise control" means to act so as to exclude others from using their property except on the defendant's own terms.
ARS § 13-1801 (Definitions): 3. "Credit" means an express agreement with the drawee for the payment of a check.

ARS § 13-1801 (Definitions): 4. "Deprive" means to withhold the property interest of another either permanently or for so long a time period that a substantial portion of its economic value or usefulness or enjoyment is lost, to withhold with the intent to restore it only on payment of any reward or other compensation or to transfer or dispose of it so that it is unlikely to be recovered.
ARS § 13-1801 (Definitions): 5. "Draw" means making, drawing, uttering, preparing, writing or delivering a check.
ARS § 13-1801 (Definitions): 6. "Funds" means money or credit.

ARS § 13-1801 (Definitions): 7. "Issue" means to deliver or cause to be delivered a check to a person who thereby acquires a right against the drawer with respect to the check.  A person who draws a check with the intent that it be so delivered is deemed to have issued it if the delivery occurs.

ARS § 13-1801 (Definitions): 8. "Material misrepresentation" means a pretense, promise, representation or statement of present, past or future fact that is fraudulent and that, when used or communicated, is instrumental in causing the wrongful control or transfer of property or services.  The pretense may be verbal or it may be a physical act.
ARS § 13-1801 (Definitions): 9. "Means of transportation" means any vehicle.

ARS § 13-1801 (Definitions): 10. "Obtain" means to bring about or to receive the transfer of any interest in property, whether to a defendant or to another, or to secure the performance of a service or the possession of a trade secret.

ARS § 13-1801 (Definitions): 11. "Pass" means, for a payee, holder or bearer of a check that previously has been or purports to have been drawn and issued by another, to deliver a check, for a purpose other than collection, to a third person who by delivery acquires a right with respect to the check.
ARS § 13-1801 (Definitions): 12. "Property" means any thing of value, tangible or intangible, including trade secrets.

ARS § 13-1801 (Definitions): 13. "Property of another" means property in which any person other than the defendant has an interest on which the defendant is not privileged to infringe, including property in which the defendant also has an interest, notwithstanding the fact that the other person might be precluded from civil recovery because the property was used in an unlawful transaction or was subject to forfeiture as contraband. Property in possession of the defendant is not deemed property of another person who has only a security interest in the property, even if legal title is in the creditor pursuant to a security agreement.

ARS § 13-1801 (Definitions): 14. "Services" includes labor, professional services, transportation, cable service and video service, computer or communication services, gas or electricity services, accommodation in hotels, restaurants or leased premises or elsewhere, admission to exhibitions and use of vehicles or other movable property.

ARS § 13-1801 (Definitions): 15. "Value" means the fair market value of the property or services at the time of the theft.  The value of ferrous metal, as defined in section 44-1641, or nonferrous metal is the average fair market value of the metal in the local area together with the repair or replacement value of any property from which the metal was removed at the time of the theft.  Written instruments that do not have a readily ascertained market value have as their value either the face amount of indebtedness less the portion satisfied or the amount of economic loss involved in deprivation of the instrument, whichever is greater. When property has an undeterminable value the trier of fact shall determine its value and, in reaching its decision, may consider all relevant evidence, including evidence of the property's value to its owner.

ARS § 13-1801 (Definitions): B. In determining the classification of the offense, the state may aggregate in the indictment or information amounts taken in thefts committed pursuant to one scheme or course of conduct, whether the amounts were taken from one or several persons.
ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): A. A person commits theft if, without lawful authority, the person knowingly:
ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): 1. Controls property of another with the intent to deprive the other person of such property; or

ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): 2. Converts for an unauthorized term or use services or property of another entrusted to the defendant or placed in the defendant's possession for a limited, authorized term or use; or

ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): 3. Obtains services or property of another by means of any material misrepresentation with intent to deprive the other person of such property or services; or

ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): 4. Comes into control of lost, mislaid or misdelivered property of another under circumstances providing means of inquiry as to the true owner and appropriates such property to the person's own or another's use without reasonable efforts to notify the true owner; or
ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): 5. Controls property of another knowing or having reason to know that the property was stolen; or

ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): 6. Obtains services known to the defendant to be available only for compensation without paying or an agreement to pay the compensation or diverts another's services to the person's own or another's benefit without authority to do so; or
ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): 7. Controls the ferrous metal or nonferrous metal of another with the intent to deprive the other person of the metal; or
ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): 8. Controls the ferrous metal or nonferrous metal of another knowing or having reason to know that the metal was stolen; or

ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): 9. Purchases within the scope of the ordinary course of business the ferrous metal or nonferrous metal of another person knowing that the metal was stolen.

ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): B. A person commits theft if, without lawful authority, the person knowingly takes control, title, use or management of a vulnerable adult's property while acting in a position of trust and confidence and with the intent to deprive the vulnerable adult of the property. Proof that a person took control, title, use or management of a vulnerable adult's property without adequate consideration to the vulnerable adult may give rise to an inference that the person intended to deprive the vulnerable adult of the property.
ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): C. It is an affirmative defense to any prosecution under subsection B of this section that either:
ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): 1. The property was given as a gift consistent with a pattern of gift giving to the person that existed before the adult became vulnerable.

ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): 2. The property was given as a gift consistent with a pattern of gift giving to a class of individuals that existed before the adult became vulnerable.
ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): 3. The superior court approved the transaction before the transaction occurred.
ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): D. The inferences set forth in section 13-2305 apply to any prosecution under subsection A, paragraph 5 of this section.

ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): E. At the conclusion of any grand jury proceeding, hearing or trial, the court shall preserve any trade secret that is admitted in evidence or any portion of a transcript that contains information relating to the trade secret pursuant to section 44-405.

ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): F. Subsection B of this section does not apply to an agent who is acting within the scope of the agent's duties as or on behalf of a health care institution that is licensed pursuant to title 36, chapter 4 and that provides services to the vulnerable adult.

ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): G. Theft of property or services with a value of twenty-five thousand dollars or more is a class 2 felony. Theft of property or services with a value of four thousand dollars or more but less than twenty-five thousand dollars is a class 3 felony. Theft of property or services with a value of three thousand dollars or more but less than four thousand dollars is a class 4 felony, except that theft of any vehicle engine or transmission is a class 4 felony regardless of value.  Theft of property or services with a value of two thousand dollars or more but less than three thousand dollars is a class 5 felony.  Theft of property or services with a value of one thousand dollars or more but less than two thousand dollars is a class 6 felony.  Theft of any property or services valued at less than one thousand dollars is a class 1 misdemeanor, unless the property is taken from the person of another, is a firearm or is an animal taken for the purpose of animal fighting in violation of section 13-2910.01, in which case the theft is a class 6 felony.

ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): H. A person who is convicted of a violation of subsection A, paragraph 1 or 3 of this section that involved property with a value of one hundred thousand dollars or more is not eligible for suspension of sentence, probation, pardon or release from confinement on any basis except pursuant to section 31-233, subsection A or B until the sentence imposed by the court has been served, the person is eligible for release pursuant to section 41-1604.07 or the sentence is commuted.

ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): I. For the purposes of this section, the value of ferrous metal or nonferrous metal includes the amount of any damage to the property of another caused as a result of the theft of the metal.
ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): J. In an action for theft of ferrous metal or nonferrous metal:

ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): 1. Unless satisfactorily explained or acquired in the ordinary course of business by an automotive recycler that is licensed pursuant to title 28, chapter 10 or by a scrap metal dealer as defined in section 44-1641, proof of possession of scrap metal that was recently stolen may give rise to an inference that the person in possession of the scrap metal was aware of the risk that it had been stolen or in some way participated in its theft.

ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): 2. Unless satisfactorily explained or sold in the ordinary course of business by an automotive recycler that is licensed pursuant to title 28, chapter 10 or by a scrap metal dealer as defined in section 44-1641, proof of the sale of stolen scrap metal at a price substantially below its fair market value may give rise to an inference that the person selling the scrap metal was aware of the risk that it had been stolen.
ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): K. For the purposes of this section:

ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): 1. "Adequate consideration" means the property was given to the person as payment for bona fide goods or services provided by the person and the payment was at a rate that was customary for similar goods or services in the community that the vulnerable adult resided in at the time of the transaction.
ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): 2. "Ferrous metal" has the same meaning prescribed in section 44-1641.
ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): 3. "Pattern of gift giving" means two or more gifts that are the same or similar in type and monetary value.
ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): 4. "Position of trust and confidence" has the same meaning prescribed in section 46-456.
ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): 5. "Property" includes all forms of real property and personal property.
ARS § 13-1802 (Theft; classification; definitions): 6. "Vulnerable adult" has the same meaning prescribed in section 46-451.
ARS § 13-1803 (Unlawful use of means of transportation; classification): A. A person commits unlawful use of means of transportation if, without intent permanently to deprive, the person either:
ARS § 13-1803 (Unlawful use of means of transportation; classification): 1. Knowingly takes unauthorized control over another person's means of transportation.

ARS § 13-1803 (Unlawful use of means of transportation; classification): 2. Knowingly is transported or physically located in a vehicle that the person knows or has reason to know is in the unlawful possession of another person pursuant to paragraph 1 or section 13-1814.
ARS § 13-1803 (Unlawful use of means of transportation; classification): B. A violation of subsection A, paragraph 1 of this section is a class 5 felony.
ARS § 13-1803 (Unlawful use of means of transportation; classification): C. A violation of subsection A, paragraph 2 of this section is a class 6 felony.

ARS § 13-1804 (Theft by extortion; classification): A. A person commits theft by extortion by knowingly obtaining or seeking to obtain property or services by means of a threat to do in the future any of the following:
ARS § 13-1804 (Theft by extortion; classification): 1. Cause physical injury to anyone by means of a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument or cause death or serious physical injury to anyone.
ARS § 13-1804 (Theft by extortion; classification): 2. Cause physical injury to anyone except as provided in paragraph 1 of this subsection.
ARS § 13-1804 (Theft by extortion; classification): 3. Cause damage to property.
ARS § 13-1804 (Theft by extortion; classification): 4. Engage in other conduct constituting an offense.
ARS § 13-1804 (Theft by extortion; classification): 5. Accuse anyone of a crime or bring criminal charges against anyone.

ARS § 13-1804 (Theft by extortion; classification): 6. Expose a secret or an asserted fact in a social media message as defined in section 16-901 or in any other manner, whether true or false, tending to subject anyone to hatred, contempt or ridicule or to impair the person's credit or business unless the threat is based on a plausible claim of right to the property or services obtained or sought to be obtained.
ARS § 13-1804 (Theft by extortion; classification): 7. Take or withhold action as a public servant or cause a public servant to take or withhold action.
ARS § 13-1804 (Theft by extortion; classification): 8. Cause anyone to part with any property.
ARS § 13-1804 (Theft by extortion; classification): 9. Take or withhold action regarding an alleged claim of easement or other right of access to an adjoining property if both of the following occur:
ARS § 13-1804 (Theft by extortion; classification): (a) The claimant's property interest is the result of a tax lien purchase or foreclosure pursuant to title 42, chapter 18.

ARS § 13-1804 (Theft by extortion; classification): (b) The fair market value of the claimant's property is equal to or less than the amount paid by the claimant for the purchase of the tax lien or foreclosure, including taxes paid after the lien purchase and any costs and attorney fees paid in connection with the lien foreclosure.  For the purposes of this subdivision, "fair market value" means the fair market value as defined in section 33-814, subsection A as of the date of the theft.

ARS § 13-1804 (Theft by extortion; classification): B. It is a defense to a prosecution under subsection A, paragraph 5, 6 or 7 of this section if a reasonable person would believe that the property or services were obtained or sought to be obtained by the threat of a reasonable accusation, exposure, lawsuit or other invocation of official action.
ARS § 13-1804 (Theft by extortion; classification): C. Theft by extortion is a class 4 felony, except that theft by extortion under subsection A, paragraph 1 of this section is a class 2 felony.

ARS § 13-1805 (Shoplifting; detaining suspect; defense to wrongful detention; civil action by merchant; public services; classification): A. A person commits shoplifting if, while in an establishment in which merchandise is displayed for sale, the person knowingly obtains such goods of another with the intent to deprive that person of such goods by:

ARS § 13-1805 (Shoplifting; detaining suspect; defense to wrongful detention; civil action by merchant; public services; classification): 1. Removing any of the goods from the immediate display or from any other place within the establishment without paying the purchase price; or

ARS § 13-1805 (Shoplifting; detaining suspect; defense to wrongful detention; civil action by merchant; public services; classification): 2. Charging the purchase price of the goods to a fictitious person or any person without that person's authority; or

ARS § 13-1805 (Shoplifting; detaining suspect; defense to wrongful detention; civil action by merchant; public services; classification): 3. Paying less than the purchase price of the goods by some trick or artifice such as altering, removing, substituting or otherwise disfiguring any label, price tag or marking; or
ARS § 13-1805 (Shoplifting; detaining suspect; defense to wrongful detention; civil action by merchant; public services; classification): 4. Transferring the goods from one container to another; or
ARS § 13-1805 (Shoplifting; detaining suspect; defense to wrongful detention; civil action by merchant; public services; classification): 5. Concealment.
