ARS § 13-2323 (Participating in a human smuggling organization or operation; classification): 3. Furnishing advice or direction in the conduct, financing or management of a human smuggling organization's or operation's affairs with the intent to promote or further the criminal objectives of a human smuggling organization or operation.

ARS § 13-2323 (Participating in a human smuggling organization or operation; classification): 4. Intentionally promoting or furthering the criminal objectives of a human smuggling organization or operation by inducing or committing any act or omission by a public servant in violation of the public servant's official duty.

ARS § 13-2323 (Participating in a human smuggling organization or operation; classification): 5. Knowingly assisting a human smuggling organization or operation by transporting a person, or procuring the transportation for a person, with the intent to do either of the following:
ARS § 13-2323 (Participating in a human smuggling organization or operation; classification): (a) Conceal the person from a peace officer.

ARS § 13-2323 (Participating in a human smuggling organization or operation; classification): (b) Assist the person with fleeing from a peace officer who is attempting to lawfully arrest or detain the person.
ARS § 13-2323 (Participating in a human smuggling organization or operation; classification): B. Participating in a human smuggling organization or operation is a class 2 felony.

ARS § 13-2323 (Participating in a human smuggling organization or operation; classification): C. A person who is convicted of a violation of this section is not eligible for suspension of sentence, probation, pardon or release from confinement on any basis except as specifically authorized by section 31-233, subsection A or B until the sentence imposed by the court has been served or commuted.

ARS § 13-2401 (Personal information on the internet; exception; classification; definitions): A. It is unlawful for a person to knowingly make available on the internet the personal information of a health professional, election officer, public official, peace officer, justice, judge, commissioner, hearing officer, public defender, member of the commission on appellate court appointments, employee of the department of child safety or employee of adult protective services who has direct contact with families in the course of employment or prosecutor if the dissemination of the personal  information poses an imminent and serious threat to the health professional's, election officer's, public official's, peace officer's, justice's, judge's, commissioner's, hearing officer's, public defender's, member's, department of child safety employee's, adult protective services employee's or prosecutor's safety or the safety of that person's immediate family and the threat is reasonably apparent to the person making the information available on the internet to be serious and imminent.  For the purposes of this subsection, "personal information" includes the address of a property held in trust by a public official.

ARS § 13-2401 (Personal information on the internet; exception; classification; definitions): B. It is not a violation of this section if an employee of a county recorder, county treasurer or county assessor publishes personal information, in good faith, on the website of the county recorder, county treasurer or county assessor in the ordinary course of carrying out public functions.
ARS § 13-2401 (Personal information on the internet; exception; classification; definitions): C. A violation of subsection A of this section is a class 5 felony.
ARS § 13-2401 (Personal information on the internet; exception; classification; definitions): D. For the purposes of this section:
ARS § 13-2401 (Personal information on the internet; exception; classification; definitions): 1. "Commissioner" means a commissioner of the superior court or municipal court.

ARS § 13-2401 (Personal information on the internet; exception; classification; definitions): 2. "Election officer" means a state, county or municipal employee who holds an election officer's certificate issued pursuant to section 16-407.

ARS § 13-2401 (Personal information on the internet; exception; classification; definitions): 3. "Health professional" means an individual who is licensed pursuant to title 32, chapter 13, 15, 17, 19.1, 25 or 33.
ARS § 13-2401 (Personal information on the internet; exception; classification; definitions): 4. "Hearing officer" means a hearing officer who is appointed pursuant to section 28-1553.

ARS § 13-2401 (Personal information on the internet; exception; classification; definitions): 5. "Immediate family" means a health professional's, peace officer's, justice's, judge's, commissioner's, public defender's or prosecutor's spouse, child or parent and any other adult who lives in the same residence as the person.

ARS § 13-2401 (Personal information on the internet; exception; classification; definitions): 6. "Judge" means a judge of the United States district court, the United States court of appeals, the United States magistrate court, the United States bankruptcy court, the Arizona court of appeals, the superior court or a municipal court.
ARS § 13-2401 (Personal information on the internet; exception; classification; definitions): 7. "Justice" means a justice of the United States or Arizona supreme court or a justice of the peace.

ARS § 13-2401 (Personal information on the internet; exception; classification; definitions): 8. "Personal information" means a health professional's, election officer's, public official's, peace officer's, justice's, judge's, commissioner's, hearing officer's, public defender's, commission on appellate court appointments member's or prosecutor's home address, home telephone number, pager number or personal photograph, directions to the person's home or photographs of the person's home or vehicle.

ARS § 13-2401 (Personal information on the internet; exception; classification; definitions): 9. "Prosecutor" means a current or former county attorney, municipal prosecutor, attorney general or United States attorney and includes a current or former assistant or deputy United States attorney, county attorney, municipal prosecutor or attorney general.

ARS § 13-2401 (Personal information on the internet; exception; classification; definitions): 10. "Public defender" means a federal public defender, county public defender, county legal defender or county contract indigent defense counsel and includes an assistant or deputy federal public defender, county public defender or county legal defender.

ARS § 13-2401 (Personal information on the internet; exception; classification; definitions): 11. "Public official" means a person who is duly elected or appointed to Congress, the legislature, a statewide office or a county, city or town office.

ARS § 13-2402 (Obstructing governmental operations; classification): A. A person commits obstructing governmental operations if, by using or threatening to use violence or physical force, such person knowingly obstructs, impairs or hinders:
ARS § 13-2402 (Obstructing governmental operations; classification): 1. The performance of a governmental function by a public servant acting under color of his official authority; or

ARS § 13-2402 (Obstructing governmental operations; classification): 2. The enforcement of the penal law or the preservation of the peace by a peace officer acting under color of his official authority.
ARS § 13-2402 (Obstructing governmental operations; classification): B. This section does not apply to the obstruction, impairment or hinderance of the making of an arrest.
ARS § 13-2402 (Obstructing governmental operations; classification): C. Obstructing governmental operations is a class 1 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2403 (Refusing to aid a peace officer; classification): A. A person commits refusing to aid a peace officer if, upon a reasonable command by a person reasonably known to be a peace officer, such person knowingly refuses or fails to aid such peace officer in:
ARS § 13-2403 (Refusing to aid a peace officer; classification): 1. Effectuating or securing an arrest; or
ARS § 13-2403 (Refusing to aid a peace officer; classification): 2. Preventing the commission by another of any offense.

ARS § 13-2403 (Refusing to aid a peace officer; classification): B. A person who complies with this section by aiding a peace officer shall not be held liable to any person for damages resulting therefrom, provided such person acted reasonably under the circumstances known to him at the time.
ARS § 13-2403 (Refusing to aid a peace officer; classification): C. Refusing to aid a peace officer is a class 1 misdemeanor.
ARS § 13-2404 (Refusing to assist in fire control; classification): A. A person commits refusing to assist in fire control if:

ARS § 13-2404 (Refusing to assist in fire control; classification): 1. Upon a reasonable command by a person reasonably known to be a fireman, such person knowingly refuses to aid in extinguishing a fire or in protecting property at the scene of a fire; or

ARS § 13-2404 (Refusing to assist in fire control; classification): 2. Upon command by a person reasonably known to be a fireman or peace officer, such person knowingly disobeys an order or regulation relating to the conduct of persons in the vicinity of a fire.

ARS § 13-2404 (Refusing to assist in fire control; classification): B. In this section, "fireman" means any officer of the fire department, the state forester or his deputies or any other person vested by law with the duty to extinguish fires.

ARS § 13-2404 (Refusing to assist in fire control; classification): C. A person who complies with this section by assisting in fire control shall not be held liable to any person for damages resulting therefrom, if such person acted reasonably under the circumstances known to him at the time.
ARS § 13-2404 (Refusing to assist in fire control; classification): D. Refusing to assist in fire control is a class 1 misdemeanor.
ARS § 13-2405 (Compounding; classification): A. A person commits compounding if such person knowingly accepts or agrees to accept any pecuniary benefit as consideration for:
ARS § 13-2405 (Compounding; classification): 1. Refraining from seeking prosecution of an offense; or
ARS § 13-2405 (Compounding; classification): 2. Refraining from reporting to law enforcement authorities the commission or suspected commission of any offense or information relating to the offense.
ARS § 13-2405 (Compounding; classification): B. Subsection A shall apply in all cases except those which are compromised by leave of court as provided by law.
ARS § 13-2405 (Compounding; classification): C. Compounding is a class 6 felony if the crime compounded is a felony. If the crime compounded is not a felony, compounding is a class 3 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2406 (Impersonating a public servant; classification; definition): A. A person commits impersonating a public servant if such person pretends to be a public servant and engages in any conduct with the intent to induce another to submit to his pretended official authority or to rely on his pretended official acts.

ARS § 13-2406 (Impersonating a public servant; classification; definition): B. It is no defense to a prosecution under this section that the office the person pretended to hold did not in fact exist or that the pretended office did not in fact possess the authority claimed for it.
ARS § 13-2406 (Impersonating a public servant; classification; definition): C. Impersonating a public servant is a class 1 misdemeanor.
ARS § 13-2406 (Impersonating a public servant; classification; definition): D. For the purposes of this section, "public servant" includes a notary public.
ARS § 13-2407 (Tampering with a public record; classification): A. A person commits tampering with a public record if, with the intent to defraud or deceive, such person knowingly:

ARS § 13-2407 (Tampering with a public record; classification): 1. Makes or completes a written instrument, knowing that it has been falsely made, which purports to be a public record or true copy thereof or alters or makes a false entry in a written instrument which is a public record or a true copy of a public record; or

ARS § 13-2407 (Tampering with a public record; classification): 2. Presents or uses a written instrument which is or purports to be a public record or a copy of such public record, knowing that it has been falsely made, completed or altered or that a false entry has been made, with intent that it be taken as genuine; or

ARS § 13-2407 (Tampering with a public record; classification): 3. Records, registers or files or offers for recordation, registration or filing in a governmental office or agency a written statement which has been falsely made, completed or altered or in which a false entry has been made or which contains a false statement or false information; or
ARS § 13-2407 (Tampering with a public record; classification): 4. Destroys, mutilates, conceals, removes or otherwise impairs the availability of any public record; or

ARS § 13-2407 (Tampering with a public record; classification): 5. Refuses to deliver a public record in such person's possession upon proper request of a public servant entitled to receive such record for examination or other purposes.

ARS § 13-2407 (Tampering with a public record; classification): B. In this section "public record" means all official books, papers, written instruments or records created, issued, received or kept by any governmental office or agency or required by law to be kept by others for the information of the government.
ARS § 13-2407 (Tampering with a public record; classification): C. Tampering with a public record is a class 6 felony.

ARS § 13-2408 (Securing the proceeds of an offense; classification): A. A person commits securing the proceeds of an offense if, with intent to assist another in profiting or benefiting from the commission of an offense, such person aids the person in securing the proceeds of the offense.

ARS § 13-2408 (Securing the proceeds of an offense; classification): B. Securing the proceeds of an offense is a class 6 felony if the person assisted committed a felony. Securing the proceeds of an offense is a class 2 misdemeanor if the person assisted committed a misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2409 (Obstructing criminal investigations or prosecutions; classification): A person who knowingly attempts by means of bribery, misrepresentation, intimidation or force or threats of force to obstruct, delay or prevent the communication of information or testimony relating to a violation of any criminal statute to a peace officer, magistrate, prosecutor or grand jury or who knowingly injures another in his person or property on account of the giving by the latter or by any other person of any such information or testimony to a peace officer, magistrate, prosecutor or grand jury is guilty of a class 5 felony, except that it is a class 3 felony if the person commits the offense with the intent to promote, further or assist a criminal street gang.

ARS § 13-2410 (Obstructing officer from collecting public money; classification): A person who knowingly obstructs or hinders a public officer from collecting revenue, taxes or other money in which this state or a county, city or town has an interest and that the officer is authorized to collect by law is guilty of a class 2 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): A. A person commits impersonating a peace officer if the person, without lawful authority, pretends to be a peace officer and engages in any conduct with the intent to induce another to submit to the person's pretended authority or to rely on the person's pretended acts.

ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): B. It is not a defense to a prosecution under this section that the law enforcement agency the person pretended to represent did not in fact exist or that the law enforcement agency the person pretended to represent did not in fact possess the authority claimed for it.

ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): C. Impersonating a peace officer is a class 6 felony, except that impersonating a peace officer during the commission of any of the following felonies is a class 4 felony:
ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): 1. Negligent homicide.
ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): 2. Manslaughter.
ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): 3. First degree murder.
ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): 4. Second degree murder.
ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): 5. Assault.
ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): 6. Aggravated assault.
ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): 7. Sexual assault.
ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): 8. Violent sexual assault.
ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): 9. Sexual abuse.
ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): 10. Unlawfully administering intoxicating liquors, narcotic drugs or dangerous drugs.
ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): 11. Attack by a person's vicious animal as prescribed in section 13-1208.
ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): 12. Drive by shooting.
ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): 13. Discharging a firearm at a structure.
ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): 14. Aggravated criminal damage.
ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): 15. Theft.
ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): 16. Theft by extortion.
ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): 17. Theft of a credit card or obtaining a credit card by fraudulent means.
ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): 18. Misconduct involving weapons.
ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): 19. Misconduct involving explosives.
ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): 20. Depositing explosives.
ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): 21. Procuring or placing persons in a house of prostitution.
ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): 22. Dangerous crimes against children as prescribed in section 13-705.
ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): 23. Burglary.
ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): 24. Arson.
ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): 25. Kidnapping.
ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): 26. Robbery.

ARS § 13-2411 (Impersonating a peace officer; classification; definition): D. For the purposes of this section, "peace officer" has the same meaning prescribed in section 1-215 and includes any federal law enforcement officer or agent who has the power to make arrests pursuant to federal law.

ARS § 13-2412 (Refusing to provide truthful name when lawfully detained; classification): A. It is unlawful for a person, after being advised that the person’s refusal to answer is unlawful, to fail or refuse to state the person's true full name on request of a peace officer who has lawfully detained the person based on reasonable suspicion that the person has committed, is committing or is about to commit a crime.  A person detained under this section shall state the person's true full name, but shall not be compelled to answer any other inquiry of a peace officer.
ARS § 13-2412 (Refusing to provide truthful name when lawfully detained; classification): B. A person who violates this section is guilty of a class 2 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2413 (Interfering with a crime scene investigation; classification; definition): A. A person commits interfering with a crime scene investigation if the person knowingly disobeys a peace officer's reasonable verbal order to remain off the premises of a possible crime scene or otherwise interferes with a peace officer's crime scene investigation.

ARS § 13-2413 (Interfering with a crime scene investigation; classification; definition): B. This section does not prevent a person from peaceably observing a police proceeding if the person does not interfere with or obstruct the peace officer's crime scene investigation.
ARS § 13-2413 (Interfering with a crime scene investigation; classification; definition): C. Interfering with a crime scene investigation is a class 2 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2413 (Interfering with a crime scene investigation; classification; definition): D. For the purposes of this section, "crime scene" means an area where a crime has possibly occurred and a peace officer who is on-site has determined that it is necessary to restrict the public's access to the area until any potential evidence of the crime at the scene is identified and preserved, victims and suspects are identified and, if necessary, any emergency medical care and ambulance transportation is requested.

ARS § 13-2414 (Impersonating a veteran; classification; definitions): A. A person commits impersonating a veteran of the United States armed forces if the person knowingly misrepresents themselves to be a veteran and engages in any of the following conduct with the intent to obtain money, property or any tangible benefit:

ARS § 13-2414 (Impersonating a veteran; classification; definitions): 1. The person knowingly misrepresents themselves to be a veteran of any branch of the uniformed services of the United States without having served in that branch as an enlisted service member, warrant officer or commissioned officer.

ARS § 13-2414 (Impersonating a veteran; classification; definitions): 2. The person knowingly misrepresents themselves to be a recipient of a decoration, medal, badge or tab that was not lawfully earned through military service.

ARS § 13-2414 (Impersonating a veteran; classification; definitions): 3. The person knowingly misrepresents themselves to have graduated from a military school from which the person did not graduate or to have obtained a rating or military occupational specialty that the person did not obtain.
ARS § 13-2414 (Impersonating a veteran; classification; definitions): 4. The person falsely claims attendance at any of the following academies or schools:
ARS § 13-2414 (Impersonating a veteran; classification; definitions): (a) United States military academy.
ARS § 13-2414 (Impersonating a veteran; classification; definitions): (b) United States naval academy.
ARS § 13-2414 (Impersonating a veteran; classification; definitions): (c) United States air force academy.
ARS § 13-2414 (Impersonating a veteran; classification; definitions): (d) United States coast guard academy.
ARS § 13-2414 (Impersonating a veteran; classification; definitions): (e) United States merchant marine academy.
ARS § 13-2414 (Impersonating a veteran; classification; definitions): (f) United States marine corps and United States army sergeant majors academy.
ARS § 13-2414 (Impersonating a veteran; classification; definitions): (g) United States air force chiefs course.
ARS § 13-2414 (Impersonating a veteran; classification; definitions): (h) United States navy senior enlisted academy.

ARS § 13-2414 (Impersonating a veteran; classification; definitions): (i) All other military branch schools that produce an additional skills identifier qualification, including ranger, seal, recon or special forces.
ARS § 13-2414 (Impersonating a veteran; classification; definitions): 5. The person knowingly misrepresents themselves to be a combat veteran.
ARS § 13-2414 (Impersonating a veteran; classification; definitions): 6. The person falsifies or alters military documents or records.

ARS § 13-2414 (Impersonating a veteran; classification; definitions): 7. The person knowingly misrepresents themselves to have received a characterization of discharge that the person did not receive.

ARS § 13-2414 (Impersonating a veteran; classification; definitions): 8. The person knowingly misrepresents themselves to be a veteran pursuant to this subsection in the furtherance of a campaign for political office.

ARS § 13-2414 (Impersonating a veteran; classification; definitions): B. Certified separation documents from the applicable uniformed service or the national archives and record administration that support the person's claims constitute a complete defense to prosecution. Before filing a complaint or seeking an indictment, a prosecuting agency shall obtain from the applicable uniformed service or the national archives and record administration a certified copy of the person's separation documents or shall receive notice that such documents do not exist.

ARS § 13-2414 (Impersonating a veteran; classification; definitions): C. This section does not apply to actors or actresses who play a veteran in conjunction with a role in a production intended for entertainment or to individuals experiencing homelessness.

ARS § 13-2414 (Impersonating a veteran; classification; definitions): D. Impersonating a veteran is a class 1 misdemeanor, except that impersonating a veteran is a class 6 felony if the benefit obtained has a value of at least $50,000.
ARS § 13-2414 (Impersonating a veteran; classification; definitions): E. If a person is convicted of a class 6 felony pursuant to this section, section 13-604 does not apply.
ARS § 13-2414 (Impersonating a veteran; classification; definitions): F. For the purposes of this section:

ARS § 13-2414 (Impersonating a veteran; classification; definitions): 1. "Combat veteran" means a current or former member of the uniformed services who served in a location where the receipt of imminent danger pay or hostile fire pay was authorized.

ARS § 13-2414 (Impersonating a veteran; classification; definitions): 2. "Tangible benefit" means financial remuneration, an effect on the outcome of a criminal or civil court proceeding, or any benefit relating to service in the military that is provided by a federal, state or local governmental entity.
ARS § 13-2501 (Definitions): In this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires:

ARS § 13-2501 (Definitions): 1. "Contraband" means any dangerous drug, narcotic drug, marijuana, intoxicating liquor of any kind, deadly weapon, dangerous instrument, explosive, wireless communication device, multimedia storage device or other article whose use or possession would endanger the safety, security or preservation of order in a correctional facility or a juvenile secure care facility as defined in section 41-2801, or of any person within a correctional or juvenile secure care facility.
ARS § 13-2501 (Definitions): 2. "Correctional facility" means any place used for the confinement or control of a person:
ARS § 13-2501 (Definitions): (a) Charged with or convicted of an offense; or
ARS § 13-2501 (Definitions): (b) Held for extradition; or
ARS § 13-2501 (Definitions): (c) Pursuant to an order of court for law enforcement purposes.

ARS § 13-2501 (Definitions): Lawful transportation or movement incident to correctional facility confinement pursuant to this paragraph is within the control of a correctional facility. For the purposes of this chapter, being within the control of a correctional facility does not include release on parole, on community supervision, on probation or by other lawful authority on the condition of subsequent personal appearance at a designated place and time.

ARS § 13-2501 (Definitions): 3. "Custody" means the imposition of actual or constructive restraint pursuant to an on-site arrest or court order but does not include detention in a correctional facility, juvenile detention center or state hospital.

ARS § 13-2501 (Definitions): 4. "Escape" means departure from custody or from a juvenile secure care facility as described in section 41-2816, a juvenile detention facility or an adult correctional facility in which a person is held or detained with knowledge that such departure is unpermitted or failure to return to custody or detention following a temporary leave granted for a specific purpose or for a limited period.

ARS § 13-2502 (Escape in the third degree; classification): A. A person commits escape in the third degree if, having been arrested for, charged with or found guilty of a misdemeanor or petty offense, such person knowingly escapes or attempts to escape from custody.
ARS § 13-2502 (Escape in the third degree; classification): B. Escape in the third degree is a class 6 felony.
ARS § 13-2503 (Escape in the second degree; classification): A. A person commits escape in the second degree by knowingly:
ARS § 13-2503 (Escape in the second degree; classification): 1. Escaping or attempting to escape from a juvenile secure care facility or a juvenile detention facility; or

ARS § 13-2503 (Escape in the second degree; classification): 2. Escaping or attempting to escape from custody imposed as a result of having been arrested for, charged with or found guilty of a felony; or

ARS § 13-2503 (Escape in the second degree; classification): 3. Escaping or attempting to escape from the Arizona state hospital if the person was committed to the hospital for treatment pursuant to section 8-291.09, 13-502, 13-3992, 13-4507, 13-4512 or 31-226 or rule 11 of the Arizona rules of criminal procedure; or

ARS § 13-2503 (Escape in the second degree; classification): 4. Escaping or attempting to escape from the Arizona state hospital if the person was committed to the hospital for treatment pursuant to title 36, chapter 37.
ARS § 13-2503 (Escape in the second degree; classification): 5. Attempting to escape from an adult correctional facility.

ARS § 13-2503 (Escape in the second degree; classification): B. Escape in the second degree pursuant to subsection A, paragraph 1, 2, 4 or 5 of this section is a class 5 felony, and the sentence imposed for a violation of this section shall run consecutively to any sentence of imprisonment for which the person was confined or to any term of community supervision for the sentence including probation, parole, work furlough or any other release.  Escape in the second degree pursuant to subsection A, paragraph 3 of this section is a class 2 misdemeanor.
ARS § 13-2504 (Escape in the first degree; classification): A. A person commits escape in the first degree by knowingly:

ARS § 13-2504 (Escape in the first degree; classification): 1. Escaping or attempting to escape from custody or a juvenile secure care facility, a juvenile detention facility or an adult correctional facility by either of the following:
ARS § 13-2504 (Escape in the first degree; classification): (a) Using or threatening the use of physical force against another person.
ARS § 13-2504 (Escape in the first degree; classification): (b) Using or threatening to use a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument against another person.
ARS § 13-2504 (Escape in the first degree; classification): 2. Escaping from an adult correctional facility.

ARS § 13-2504 (Escape in the first degree; classification): B. Escape in the first degree is a class 4 felony, and the sentence imposed for a violation of this section shall run consecutively to any sentence of imprisonment for which the person was confined, to any confinement in a secure care facility or to any term of community supervision for the sentence including probation, parole, work furlough or any other release.
ARS § 13-2505 (Promoting prison contraband; exceptions; x-radiation; body scans; classification): A. A person, not otherwise authorized by law, commits promoting prison contraband:

ARS § 13-2505 (Promoting prison contraband; exceptions; x-radiation; body scans; classification): 1. By knowingly taking contraband into a correctional facility or the grounds of a correctional facility; or
ARS § 13-2505 (Promoting prison contraband; exceptions; x-radiation; body scans; classification): 2. By knowingly conveying contraband to any person confined in a correctional facility; or

ARS § 13-2505 (Promoting prison contraband; exceptions; x-radiation; body scans; classification): 3. By knowingly making, obtaining or possessing contraband while being confined in a correctional facility or while being lawfully transported or moved incident to correctional facility confinement.

ARS § 13-2505 (Promoting prison contraband; exceptions; x-radiation; body scans; classification): B. A person who has reasonable grounds to believe there has been a violation or attempted violation of this section shall immediately report the violation or attempted violation to the official in charge of the facility or to a peace officer.

ARS § 13-2505 (Promoting prison contraband; exceptions; x-radiation; body scans; classification): C. Notwithstanding any law to the contrary, any person who is convicted of a violation of this section is prohibited from being employed by this state or any of its agencies or political subdivisions until the person's civil rights have been restored pursuant to chapter 9 of this title.
ARS § 13-2505 (Promoting prison contraband; exceptions; x-radiation; body scans; classification): D. This section does not apply to any of the following:

ARS § 13-2505 (Promoting prison contraband; exceptions; x-radiation; body scans; classification): 1. A prisoner who possesses or carries any tool, instrument or implement used by him at the direction or with the permission of prison officials.
ARS § 13-2505 (Promoting prison contraband; exceptions; x-radiation; body scans; classification): 2. Contraband located at the place where a person is on home arrest.

ARS § 13-2505 (Promoting prison contraband; exceptions; x-radiation; body scans; classification): 3. Contraband authorized by the correctional facility policies and used at the direction or with the permission of prison officials.

ARS § 13-2505 (Promoting prison contraband; exceptions; x-radiation; body scans; classification): E. The state department of corrections, a county jail or a city or town correctional facility may request a licensed practitioner as defined in section 32-2801 to order that x-radiation be performed on any inmate if there is reason to believe the inmate is in possession of any contraband.

ARS § 13-2505 (Promoting prison contraband; exceptions; x-radiation; body scans; classification): F. The state department of corrections, a county jail or a city or town correctional facility, in compliance with generally accepted health and safety standards, may perform a body scan of an inmate by using low-dose ionizing radiation without an order from a licensed practitioner to prevent any contraband from entering into a correctional facility.

ARS § 13-2505 (Promoting prison contraband; exceptions; x-radiation; body scans; classification): G. Promoting prison contraband if the contraband is a deadly weapon, dangerous instrument or explosive is a class 2 felony. Promoting prison contraband if the contraband is a dangerous drug, narcotic drug or marijuana is a class 2 felony. In all other cases promoting prison contraband is a class 5 felony. Failure to report a violation or attempted violation of this section is a class 5 felony.
ARS § 13-2506 (Failure to appear in the second degree; classification): A. A person commits failure to appear in the second degree if, having either:

ARS § 13-2506 (Failure to appear in the second degree; classification): 1. Been required by law to appear in connection with any misdemeanor or petty offense, the person knowingly fails to appear as required, regardless of the disposition of the charge requiring the appearance.

ARS § 13-2506 (Failure to appear in the second degree; classification): 2. Given a written promise to appear in court or been personally served with a written notice to appear on a designated date pursuant to section 13-3903, the person thereafter fails to appear, personally or by counsel.

ARS § 13-2506 (Failure to appear in the second degree; classification): B. Failure to appear in the second degree pursuant to subsection A, paragraph 1 of this section is a class 1 misdemeanor.  Failure to appear in the second degree pursuant to subsection A, paragraph 2 of this section is a class 2 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2507 (Failure to appear in the first degree; classification): A. A person commits failure to appear in the first degree if, having been required by law to appear in connection with any felony, such person knowingly fails to appear as required, regardless of the disposition of the charge requiring the appearance.
ARS § 13-2507 (Failure to appear in the first degree; classification): B. Failure to appear in the first degree is a class 5 felony.

ARS § 13-2508 (Resisting arrest; classification; definition): A. A person commits resisting arrest by intentionally preventing or attempting to prevent a person reasonably known to him to be a peace officer, acting under color of such peace officer's official authority, from effecting an arrest by:
ARS § 13-2508 (Resisting arrest; classification; definition): 1. Using or threatening to use physical force against the peace officer or another.
ARS § 13-2508 (Resisting arrest; classification; definition): 2. Using any other means creating a substantial risk of causing physical injury to the peace officer or another.
ARS § 13-2508 (Resisting arrest; classification; definition): 3. Engaging in passive resistance.

ARS § 13-2508 (Resisting arrest; classification; definition): B. Resisting arrest pursuant to subsection A, paragraph 1 or 2 of this section is a class 6 felony.  Resisting arrest pursuant to subsection A, paragraph 3 of this section is a class 1 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2508 (Resisting arrest; classification; definition): C. For the purposes of this section, "passive resistance" means a nonviolent physical act or failure to act that is intended to impede, hinder or delay the effecting of an arrest.

ARS § 13-2509 (Resisting an order directing, regulating or controlling motor vehicle; classification): A. A person commits resisting an order directing, regulating or controlling a motor vehicle by knowingly failing to obey an order of a person reasonably known to him to be a peace officer, acting under color of such officer's official authority, directing, regulating or controlling his vehicle.

ARS § 13-2509 (Resisting an order directing, regulating or controlling motor vehicle; classification): B. Resisting an order directing, regulating or controlling a motor vehicle is a class 2 misdemeanor.
ARS § 13-2510 (Hindering prosecution; definition): For purposes of sections 13-2511 and 13-2512 a person renders assistance to another person by knowingly:
ARS § 13-2510 (Hindering prosecution; definition): 1. Harboring or concealing the other person; or

ARS § 13-2510 (Hindering prosecution; definition): 2. Warning the other person of impending discovery, apprehension, prosecution or conviction. This does not apply to a warning given in connection with an effort to bring another into compliance with the law; or

ARS § 13-2510 (Hindering prosecution; definition): 3. Providing the other person with money, transportation, a weapon, a disguise or other similar means of avoiding discovery, apprehension, prosecution or conviction; or

ARS § 13-2510 (Hindering prosecution; definition): 4. Preventing or obstructing by means of force, deception or intimidation anyone from performing an act that might aid in the discovery, apprehension, prosecution or conviction of the other person; or

ARS § 13-2510 (Hindering prosecution; definition): 5. Suppressing by an act of concealment, alteration or destruction any physical evidence that might aid in the discovery, apprehension, prosecution or conviction of the other person; or
ARS § 13-2510 (Hindering prosecution; definition): 6. Concealing the identity of the other person.

ARS § 13-2511 (Hindering prosecution in the second degree; classification): A. A person commits hindering prosecution in the second degree if, with the intent to hinder the apprehension, prosecution, conviction or punishment of another for any misdemeanor or petty offense, such person renders assistance to such person.
ARS § 13-2511 (Hindering prosecution in the second degree; classification): B. Hindering prosecution in the second degree is a class 1 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2512 (Hindering prosecution in the first degree; classification): A. A person commits hindering prosecution in the first degree if, with the intent to hinder the apprehension, prosecution, conviction or punishment of another for any felony, the person renders assistance to the other person.
ARS § 13-2512 (Hindering prosecution in the first degree; classification): B. Hindering prosecution in the first degree is a class 5 felony, except that it is a class 3 felony if either:
ARS § 13-2512 (Hindering prosecution in the first degree; classification): 1. The person knows or has reason to know that the offense involves terrorism or murder.
ARS § 13-2512 (Hindering prosecution in the first degree; classification): 2. The person commits the offense with the intent to promote, further or assist a criminal street gang.

ARS § 13-2513 (Failure to discharge duties; classification; definition): A. A person who has custodial responsibility and who intentionally fails to discharge those duties is guilty of a class 1 misdemeanor if that failure results in any of the following:
ARS § 13-2513 (Failure to discharge duties; classification; definition): 1. The escape of a prisoner.
ARS § 13-2513 (Failure to discharge duties; classification; definition): 2. Serious physical injury to or the death of any other person or prisoner.

ARS § 13-2513 (Failure to discharge duties; classification; definition): B. For the purposes of this section, "custodial responsibility" means having responsibility for the care, management or control of a prisoner who is committed to the state department of corrections.

ARS § 13-2514 (Promoting secure care facility contraband; classifications): A. A person, not otherwise authorized by law, commits promoting secure care facility contraband by knowingly doing any of the following:

ARS § 13-2514 (Promoting secure care facility contraband; classifications): 1. Taking contraband onto the grounds of or into a secure care facility under the jurisdiction of the department of juvenile corrections.

ARS § 13-2514 (Promoting secure care facility contraband; classifications): 2. Conveying contraband to any person confined in a secure care facility under the jurisdiction of the department of juvenile corrections.

ARS § 13-2514 (Promoting secure care facility contraband; classifications): 3. Making, obtaining or possessing contraband while being confined in a secure care facility under the jurisdiction of the department of juvenile corrections.

ARS § 13-2514 (Promoting secure care facility contraband; classifications): B. Except for information protected under attorney client privilege, any person who has reasonable grounds to believe there has been a violation or attempted violation of this section shall immediately report the violation or attempted violation to the official in charge of the facility or to a peace officer.

ARS § 13-2514 (Promoting secure care facility contraband; classifications): C. Promoting secure care facility contraband if the contraband is a deadly weapon, dangerous instrument or explosive is a class 2 felony. Promoting secure care facility contraband if the contraband is a dangerous drug, narcotic drug or marijuana is a class 2 felony. In all other cases promoting secure care facility contraband is a class 5 felony. Failure to report a violation or attempted violation of this section is a class 5 felony.

ARS § 13-2514 (Promoting secure care facility contraband; classifications): D. Notwithstanding any law to the contrary, any person convicted of a violation of this section shall be prohibited from employment by this state or any of its agencies or political subdivisions until the person's civil rights have been restored pursuant to chapter 9 of this title.
ARS § 13-2601 (Definition): In this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires:
ARS § 13-2601 (Definition): 1. "Employee" includes a person employed by an enterprise or an agent or fiduciary of a principal.
ARS § 13-2601 (Definition): 2. "Employer" includes an enterprise or principal.
ARS § 13-2601 (Definition): 3. "Party officer" means a person who holds any position or office in a political party, whether by election, appointment or otherwise.
ARS § 13-2602 (Bribery of a public servant or party officer; classification): A. A person commits bribery of a public servant or party officer if with corrupt intent:

ARS § 13-2602 (Bribery of a public servant or party officer; classification): 1. Such person offers, confers or agrees to confer any benefit upon a public servant or party officer with the intent to influence the public servant's or party officer's vote, opinion, judgment, exercise of discretion or other action in his official capacity as a public servant or party officer; or

ARS § 13-2602 (Bribery of a public servant or party officer; classification): 2. While a public servant or party officer, such person solicits, accepts or agrees to accept any benefit upon an agreement or understanding that his vote, opinion, judgment, exercise of discretion or other action as a public servant or party officer may thereby be influenced.

ARS § 13-2602 (Bribery of a public servant or party officer; classification): B. It is no defense to a prosecution under this section that a person sought to be influenced was not qualified to act in the desired way because such person had not yet assumed office, lacked jurisdiction or for any other reason.
ARS § 13-2602 (Bribery of a public servant or party officer; classification): C. Bribery of a public servant or party officer is a class 4 felony.
ARS § 13-2603 (Trading in public office; classification): A. A person commits trading in public office if with corrupt intent:

ARS § 13-2603 (Trading in public office; classification): 1. Such person offers, confers or agrees to confer any benefit upon a public servant or party officer upon an agreement or understanding that he will or may be appointed to a public office or designated or nominated as a candidate for public office; or

ARS § 13-2603 (Trading in public office; classification): 2. While a public servant or party officer, such person solicits, accepts or agrees to accept any benefit from another upon an agreement or understanding that that person will or may be appointed to a public office or designated or nominated as a candidate for public office.

ARS § 13-2603 (Trading in public office; classification): B. This section does not apply to contributions to political campaign funds or other similar political contributions made without corrupt intent.
ARS § 13-2603 (Trading in public office; classification): C. Trading in public office is a class 6 felony.

ARS § 13-2604 (Forfeiture and disqualification from office): Notwithstanding sections 13-904 and 13-907, a person who is convicted of violating section 13-2602 or 13-2603 shall forever be disqualified from becoming a public servant and, if such person is a public servant at the time of his conviction, shall forfeit his office.
ARS § 13-2605 (Commercial bribery; classification; exception): A. A person commits commercial bribery if:

ARS § 13-2605 (Commercial bribery; classification; exception): 1. Such person confers any benefit on an employee without the consent of such employee's employer, corruptly intending that such benefit will influence the conduct of the employee in relation to the employer's commercial affairs, and the conduct of the employee causes economic loss to the employer.

ARS § 13-2605 (Commercial bribery; classification; exception): 2. While an employee of an employer such employee accepts any benefit from another person, corruptly intending that such benefit will influence his conduct in relation to the employer's commercial affairs, and such conduct causes economic loss to the employer or principal.

ARS § 13-2605 (Commercial bribery; classification; exception): B. Commercial bribery is a class 5 felony if the value of the benefit is more than one thousand dollars. Commercial bribery is a class 6 felony if the value of the benefit is not more than one thousand dollars but not less than one hundred dollars. Commercial bribery is a class 1 misdemeanor if the value of the benefit is less than one hundred dollars.

ARS § 13-2605 (Commercial bribery; classification; exception): C. This section shall not be construed to prohibit a person from recruiting an employee of another employer unless, pursuant to an agreement between such person and the employee that such employee engage in conduct which will cause economic loss to his employer, such employee engages in conduct while an employee of his original employer and such conduct causes economic loss to the employer.

ARS § 13-2606 (Offer to exert improper influence on public officer or employee for consideration; classification): A person who intentionally or knowingly obtains or seeks to obtain any benefit from another person upon a claim or representation that he can or will improperly influence the action of a public servant is guilty of a class 4 felony.
ARS § 13-2701 (Definitions): In this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires:

ARS § 13-2701 (Definitions): 1. "Material" means that which could have affected the course or outcome of any proceeding or transaction. Whether a statement is material in any given factual situation is a question of law.

ARS § 13-2701 (Definitions): 2. "Statement" means any representation of fact and includes a representation of opinion, belief or other state of mind where the representation clearly relates to state of mind apart from or in addition to any facts which are the subject of the representation.

ARS § 13-2701 (Definitions): 3. "Sworn statement" means any statement knowingly given under oath or affirmation attesting to the truth of what is stated, including a notarized statement whether or not given in connection with an official proceeding.
ARS § 13-2702 (Perjury; classification): A. A person commits perjury by making either:
ARS § 13-2702 (Perjury; classification): 1. A false sworn statement in regard to a material issue, believing it to be false.

ARS § 13-2702 (Perjury; classification): 2. A false unsworn declaration, certificate, verification or statement in regard to a material issue that the person subscribes as true under penalty of perjury, believing it to be false.
ARS § 13-2702 (Perjury; classification): B. Perjury is a class 4 felony.
ARS § 13-2703 (False swearing; classification): A. A person commits false swearing by making a false sworn statement, believing it to be false.
ARS § 13-2703 (False swearing; classification): B. False swearing is a class 6 felony.
ARS § 13-2704 (Unsworn falsification; classification): A. A person commits unsworn falsification by knowingly:

ARS § 13-2704 (Unsworn falsification; classification): 1. Making any statement that he believes to be false, in regard to a material issue, to a public servant in connection with an application for any benefit, privilege or license.

ARS § 13-2704 (Unsworn falsification; classification): 2. Making any statement that he believes to be false in regard to a material issue to a public servant in connection with any official proceeding as defined in section 13-2801.

ARS § 13-2704 (Unsworn falsification; classification): B. Unsworn falsification pursuant to paragraph 1, subsection A, is a class 2 misdemeanor. Unsworn falsification pursuant to subsection A, paragraph 2 is a class 1 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2705 (Perjury by inconsistent statements): When a person has made inconsistent statements under oath, both having been made within the period of the statute of limitations, the prosecution may proceed by setting forth the inconsistent statements in a single charge alleging in the alternative that one or the other was false and not believed by the defendant. In such case it shall not be necessary for the prosecution to prove which statement was false but only that one or the other was false and not believed by the defendant to be true.
ARS § 13-2706 (Limitation on defenses): A. It is no defense to a prosecution under this chapter that:
ARS § 13-2706 (Limitation on defenses): 1. The statement was inadmissible under the rules of evidence; or
ARS § 13-2706 (Limitation on defenses): 2. The oath or affirmation was taken or administered in an irregular manner; or
ARS § 13-2706 (Limitation on defenses): 3. The defendant mistakenly believed the false statement to be immaterial.

ARS § 13-2706 (Limitation on defenses): B. The provisions of law which declare that evidence obtained upon examination of a person as a witness cannot be received against him in a criminal proceeding do not forbid giving such evidence against the person upon any proceedings founded upon a charge of perjury committed in such examination.

ARS § 13-2707 (Proof of guilt): Proof of guilt beyond a reasonable doubt is sufficient for perjury or false swearing and it shall not be necessary that proof be made by a particular number of witnesses or by documentary or other type of evidence.
ARS § 13-2801 (Definitions): In this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires:
ARS § 13-2801 (Definitions): 1. "Juror" means any person who is a member of any impaneled jury or grand jury, and includes any person who has been drawn or summoned to attend as a prospective juror.

ARS § 13-2801 (Definitions): 2. "Official proceeding" means a proceeding heard before any legislative, judicial, administrative or other governmental agency or official authorized to hear evidence under oath.
ARS § 13-2801 (Definitions): 3. "Physical evidence" means any article, object, document, record or other thing of physical substance.
ARS § 13-2801 (Definitions): 4. "Testimony" means oral or written statements, documents or any other material that may be offered by a witness in an official proceeding.
ARS § 13-2801 (Definitions): 5. "Threat" means a threat proscribed by section 13-1804, subsection A.

ARS § 13-2802 (Influencing a witness; classification): A. A person commits influencing a witness if such person threatens a witness or offers, confers or agrees to confer any benefit upon a witness in any official proceeding or a person he believes may be called as a witness with intent to:
ARS § 13-2802 (Influencing a witness; classification): 1. Influence the testimony of that person; or
ARS § 13-2802 (Influencing a witness; classification): 2. Induce that person to avoid legal process summoning him to testify; or
ARS § 13-2802 (Influencing a witness; classification): 3. Induce that person to absent himself from any official proceeding to which he has been legally summoned.
ARS § 13-2802 (Influencing a witness; classification): B. Influencing a witness is a class 5 felony.

ARS § 13-2803 (Receiving a bribe by a witness; classification): A. A witness in an official proceeding or a person who believes he may be called as a witness commits receiving a bribe by a witness if such person knowingly solicits, accepts or agrees to accept any benefit upon an agreement or understanding that:
ARS § 13-2803 (Receiving a bribe by a witness; classification): 1. His testimony will thereby be influenced; or
ARS § 13-2803 (Receiving a bribe by a witness; classification): 2. He will attempt to avoid legal process summoning him to testify; or
ARS § 13-2803 (Receiving a bribe by a witness; classification): 3. He will absent himself from any official proceeding to which he has been legally summoned.
ARS § 13-2803 (Receiving a bribe by a witness; classification): B. Receiving a bribe by a witness is a class 5 felony.

ARS § 13-2804 (Tampering with a witness; classification): A. A person commits tampering with a witness if the person knowingly communicates, directly or indirectly, with a witness in any official proceeding or a person he believes may be called as a witness to do any of the following:
ARS § 13-2804 (Tampering with a witness; classification): 1. Unlawfully withhold any testimony.
ARS § 13-2804 (Tampering with a witness; classification): 2. Testify falsely.
ARS § 13-2804 (Tampering with a witness; classification): 3. Absent himself from any official proceeding to which he has been legally summoned.
ARS § 13-2804 (Tampering with a witness; classification): 4. Evade a summons or subpoena.
ARS § 13-2804 (Tampering with a witness; classification): B. Tampering with a witness is a class 6 felony.

ARS § 13-2805 (Influencing a juror; classification): A. A person commits influencing a juror if such person threatens a juror or offers, confers or agrees to confer a benefit upon a juror with the intent to influence the juror's vote, opinion, decision or other action as a juror.
ARS § 13-2805 (Influencing a juror; classification): B. Influencing a juror is a class 4 felony.

ARS § 13-2806 (Receiving a bribe by a juror; classification): A. A juror commits receiving a bribe by a juror if such person knowingly solicits, accepts or agrees to accept any benefit upon an agreement or understanding that his vote, opinion, decision or other action as a juror may be influenced.
ARS § 13-2806 (Receiving a bribe by a juror; classification): B. Receiving a bribe by a juror is a class 5 felony.

ARS § 13-2807 (Jury tampering; classification): A. A person commits jury tampering if, with intent to influence a juror's vote, opinion, decision or other action in a case, such person directly or indirectly, communicates with a juror other than as part of the normal proceedings of the case.
ARS § 13-2807 (Jury tampering; classification): B. Jury tampering is a class 6 felony.

ARS § 13-2808 (Misconduct by a juror; classification): A. A juror commits misconduct by a juror if, in relation to an action or proceeding pending or about to be brought before him, such person knowingly:
ARS § 13-2808 (Misconduct by a juror; classification): 1. Allows an unauthorized communication to be made to him; or
ARS § 13-2808 (Misconduct by a juror; classification): 2. Makes a promise or agreement to decide for or against any party to the proceeding other than as part of jury deliberation.
ARS § 13-2808 (Misconduct by a juror; classification): B. Misconduct by a juror is a class 6 felony.

ARS § 13-2809 (Tampering with physical evidence; classification): A. A person commits tampering with physical evidence if, with intent that it be used, introduced, rejected or unavailable in an official proceeding which is then pending or which such person knows is about to be instituted, such person:
ARS § 13-2809 (Tampering with physical evidence; classification): 1. Destroys, mutilates, alters, conceals or removes physical evidence with the intent to impair its verity or availability; or
ARS § 13-2809 (Tampering with physical evidence; classification): 2. Knowingly makes, produces or offers any false physical evidence; or
ARS § 13-2809 (Tampering with physical evidence; classification): 3. Prevents the production of physical evidence by an act of force, intimidation or deception against any person.
ARS § 13-2809 (Tampering with physical evidence; classification): B. Inadmissibility of the evidence in question is not a defense.
ARS § 13-2809 (Tampering with physical evidence; classification): C. Tampering with physical evidence is a class 6 felony.
ARS § 13-2810 (Interfering with judicial proceedings; classification): A. A person commits interfering with judicial proceedings if such person knowingly:

ARS § 13-2810 (Interfering with judicial proceedings; classification): 1. Engages in disorderly, disrespectful or insolent behavior during the session of a court which directly tends to interrupt its proceedings or impairs the respect due to its authority; or
ARS § 13-2810 (Interfering with judicial proceedings; classification): 2. Disobeys or resists the lawful order, process or other mandate of a court; or
ARS § 13-2810 (Interfering with judicial proceedings; classification): 3. Refuses to be sworn or affirmed as a witness in any court proceeding; or
ARS § 13-2810 (Interfering with judicial proceedings; classification): 4. Publishes a false or grossly inaccurate report of a court proceeding; or
ARS § 13-2810 (Interfering with judicial proceedings; classification): 5. Refuses to serve as a juror unless exempted by law; or
ARS § 13-2810 (Interfering with judicial proceedings; classification): 6. Fails inexcusably to attend a trial at which he has been chosen to serve as a juror.
ARS § 13-2810 (Interfering with judicial proceedings; classification): B. Interfering with judicial proceedings is a class 1 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2812 (Unlawful grand jury disclosure; classification): A. A person commits unlawful grand jury disclosure if the person knowingly discloses to another the nature or substance of any grand jury testimony or any decision, result or other matter attending a grand jury proceeding, except in the proper discharge of official duties, at the discretion of the prosecutor to inform a victim of the status of the case or when permitted by the court in furtherance of justice.
ARS § 13-2812 (Unlawful grand jury disclosure; classification): B. Unlawful grand jury disclosure is a class 1 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2813 (Unlawful disclosure of an indictment, information or complaint; classification): A. A person commits unlawful disclosure of an indictment, information or complaint if the person knowingly discloses the fact that an indictment, information or complaint has been found or filed before the accused person is in custody or has been served with a summons, except in the proper discharge of official duties, at the discretion of the prosecutor to inform a victim of the status of the case or as authorized by the court in furtherance of justice.
ARS § 13-2813 (Unlawful disclosure of an indictment, information or complaint; classification): B. This section does not apply to offenses that are created by city or county ordinance.
ARS § 13-2813 (Unlawful disclosure of an indictment, information or complaint; classification): C. Unlawful disclosure of an indictment, information or complaint is a class 1 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2814 (Simulating legal process; classification): A. A person commits simulating legal process if such person knowingly sends or delivers to another any document falsely purporting to be an order or other document that simulates civil or criminal process.
ARS § 13-2814 (Simulating legal process; classification): B. Simulating legal process is a class 2 misdemeanor.
ARS § 13-2901 (Definitions): In this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires:

ARS § 13-2901 (Definitions): 1. "Marijuana" means all parts of any plant of the genus cannabis, from which the resin has not been extracted, whether growing or not, and the seeds of such plant. Marijuana does not include the mature stalks of such plant, or the sterilized seed of such plant which is incapable of germination.
ARS § 13-2901 (Definitions): 2. "Public" means affecting or likely to affect a substantial group of persons.
ARS § 13-2902 (Unlawful assembly; classification): A. A person commits unlawful assembly by:
ARS § 13-2902 (Unlawful assembly; classification): 1. Assembling with two or more other persons with the intent to engage in conduct constituting a riot as defined in section 13-2903; or

ARS § 13-2902 (Unlawful assembly; classification): 2. Being present at an assembly of two or more other persons who are engaged in or who have the readily apparent intent to engage in conduct constituting a riot as defined in section 13-2903 and knowingly remaining there and refusing to obey an official order to disperse.
ARS § 13-2902 (Unlawful assembly; classification): B. Unlawful assembly is a class 1 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2903 (Riot; classification): A. A person commits riot if, with two or more other persons acting together, such person recklessly uses force or violence or threatens to use force or violence, if such threat is accompanied by immediate power of execution, which disturbs the public peace.
ARS § 13-2903 (Riot; classification): B. Riot is a class 5 felony.

ARS § 13-2904 (Disorderly conduct; classification): A. A person commits disorderly conduct if, with intent to disturb the peace or quiet of a neighborhood, family or person, or with knowledge of doing so, such person:
ARS § 13-2904 (Disorderly conduct; classification): 1. Engages in fighting, violent or seriously disruptive behavior; or
ARS § 13-2904 (Disorderly conduct; classification): 2. Makes unreasonable noise; or

ARS § 13-2904 (Disorderly conduct; classification): 3. Uses abusive or offensive language or gestures to any person present in a manner likely to provoke immediate physical retaliation by such person; or

ARS § 13-2904 (Disorderly conduct; classification): 4. Makes any protracted commotion, utterance or display with the intent to prevent the transaction of the business of a lawful meeting, gathering or procession; or

ARS § 13-2904 (Disorderly conduct; classification): 5. Refuses to obey a lawful order to disperse issued to maintain public safety in dangerous proximity to a fire, a hazard or any other emergency; or
ARS § 13-2904 (Disorderly conduct; classification): 6. Recklessly handles, displays or discharges a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument.

ARS § 13-2904 (Disorderly conduct; classification): B. Disorderly conduct under subsection A, paragraph 6 is a class 6 felony. Disorderly conduct under subsection A, paragraph 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 is a class 1 misdemeanor.
ARS § 13-2905 (Loitering; classification): A. A person commits loitering if such person intentionally:

ARS § 13-2905 (Loitering; classification): 1. Is present in a public place and in an offensive manner or in a manner likely to disturb the public peace solicits another person to engage in any sexual offense.

ARS § 13-2905 (Loitering; classification): 2. Is present in a transportation facility and after a reasonable request to cease or unless specifically authorized to do so solicits or engages in any business, trade or commercial transactions involving the sale of merchandise or services.
ARS § 13-2905 (Loitering; classification): 3. Is present in a public place, unless specifically authorized by law, to gamble with any cards, dice or other similar gambling devices.

ARS § 13-2905 (Loitering; classification): 4. Is present in or about a school, college or university building or grounds after a reasonable request to leave and either does not have any reason or relationship involving custody of or responsibility for a pupil or student or any other specific legitimate reason for being there or does not have written permission to be there from anyone authorized to grant permission.

ARS § 13-2905 (Loitering; classification): 5. Except as provided in section 13-3969, subsection A, solicits bail bond business inside a court building or immediately around or near the entrance of a county or city jail.  For the purposes of this paragraph, "solicit" includes handing out business cards or any printed material or displaying any electronic devices related to bail bonds, verbally asking a person if the person needs a bail bond and recruiting another person to solicit bail bond business.
ARS § 13-2905 (Loitering; classification): B. Loitering under subsection A, paragraph 4 is a class 1 misdemeanor. Loitering under subsection A, paragraphs 1, 2, 3 and 5 is a class 3 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2906 (Obstructing a highway or other public thoroughfare; classification; definition): A. A person commits obstructing a highway or other public thoroughfare if the person, alone or with other persons, does any of the following:

ARS § 13-2906 (Obstructing a highway or other public thoroughfare; classification; definition): 1. Having no legal privilege to do so, recklessly interferes with the passage of any highway or public thoroughfare by creating an unreasonable inconvenience or hazard.

ARS § 13-2906 (Obstructing a highway or other public thoroughfare; classification; definition): 2. Intentionally activates a pedestrian signal on a highway or public thoroughfare if the person's reason for activating the signal is not to cross the highway or public thoroughfare but to do both of the following:
ARS § 13-2906 (Obstructing a highway or other public thoroughfare; classification; definition): (a) Stop the passage of traffic on the highway or public thoroughfare.
ARS § 13-2906 (Obstructing a highway or other public thoroughfare; classification; definition): (b) Solicit a driver for a donation or business.

ARS § 13-2906 (Obstructing a highway or other public thoroughfare; classification; definition): 3. After receiving a verbal warning to desist, intentionally interferes with passage on a highway or other public thoroughfare or entrance into a public forum that results in preventing other persons from gaining access to a governmental meeting, a governmental hearing or a political campaign event.
ARS § 13-2906 (Obstructing a highway or other public thoroughfare; classification; definition): B. Obstructing a highway or other public thoroughfare under:
ARS § 13-2906 (Obstructing a highway or other public thoroughfare; classification; definition): 1. Subsection A, paragraph 3 of this section is a class 1 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2906 (Obstructing a highway or other public thoroughfare; classification; definition): 2. Subsection A, paragraph 1 of this section is a class 2 misdemeanor, except that a second or subsequent violation within a period of twenty-four months is a class 1 misdemeanor.
ARS § 13-2906 (Obstructing a highway or other public thoroughfare; classification; definition): 3. Subsection A, paragraph 2 of this section is a class 3 misdemeanor.
ARS § 13-2906 (Obstructing a highway or other public thoroughfare; classification; definition): C. For the purposes of this section, "public forum" has the same meaning prescribed in section 15-1861.

ARS § 13-2907 (False reporting; emergency response costs; classification; definitions): A. A person commits false reporting by initiating or circulating a report of a bombing, fire or other emergency knowing that such report is false and intending:

ARS § 13-2907 (False reporting; emergency response costs; classification; definitions): 1. That it will cause action of any sort by an official or volunteer agency organized to deal with emergencies; or
ARS § 13-2907 (False reporting; emergency response costs; classification; definitions): 2. That it will place a person in fear of imminent serious physical injury; or

ARS § 13-2907 (False reporting; emergency response costs; classification; definitions): 3. That it will prevent or interrupt the occupation of any building, room, place of assembly, public place or means of transportation.

ARS § 13-2907 (False reporting; emergency response costs; classification; definitions): B. A person commits false reporting by initiating a report of a serious offense involving an educational institution or any place used for worship or for religious services knowing that such report is false and intending that it will cause an emergency response.

ARS § 13-2907 (False reporting; emergency response costs; classification; definitions): C. A person who commits a violation of this section that results in an emergency response or investigation of false reporting and who is convicted of a violation of this section is liable for the expenses that are incurred incident to the emergency response or the investigation of the commission of false reporting, except that if the person is a juvenile who is adjudicated delinquent of a violation of this section, the court may order the juvenile to pay the expenses incurred under this subsection as restitution.  The expenses are a debt of the person.  The public agency, for profit entity or not-for-profit entity that incurred the expenses may collect the debt proportionally.  The liability that is imposed under this subsection is in addition to any other liability that may be imposed.

ARS § 13-2907 (False reporting; emergency response costs; classification; definitions): D. A violation of subsection A of this section is a class 1 misdemeanor, except that a second or subsequent violation is a class 6 felony. A violation of subsection B of this section is a class 6 felony.
ARS § 13-2907 (False reporting; emergency response costs; classification; definitions): E. For the purposes of this section:
ARS § 13-2907 (False reporting; emergency response costs; classification; definitions): 1. "Educational institution" means any of the following:
ARS § 13-2907 (False reporting; emergency response costs; classification; definitions): (a) A public school as defined in section 15-101.

ARS § 13-2907 (False reporting; emergency response costs; classification; definitions): (b) A private school that provides instruction to pupils in any combination of kindergarten programs and grades one through twelve.
ARS § 13-2907 (False reporting; emergency response costs; classification; definitions): (c) A community college as defined in section 15-1401.
ARS § 13-2907 (False reporting; emergency response costs; classification; definitions): (d) A university that is under the jurisdiction of the Arizona board of regents.
ARS § 13-2907 (False reporting; emergency response costs; classification; definitions): (e) A private postsecondary institution that is licensed under title 32, chapter 30, article 2.

ARS § 13-2907 (False reporting; emergency response costs; classification; definitions): (f) A college in this state that is owned, operated or chartered by a federally recognized Native American tribe on the tribe's own Indian reservation.
ARS § 13-2907 (False reporting; emergency response costs; classification; definitions): 2. "Emergency response" means an immediate response by a law enforcement agency.

ARS § 13-2907 (False reporting; emergency response costs; classification; definitions): 3. "Expenses" means any reasonable costs that are directly incurred by a public agency, for profit entity or not-for-profit entity that makes an appropriate emergency response to an incident or an investigation of the commission of false reporting.  Expenses includes the costs of providing police, fire fighting, rescue and emergency medical services at the scene of an incident and the salaries of the persons who respond to the incident. Expenses does not include any charges that are assessed by an ambulance service that is regulated pursuant to title 36, chapter 21.1, article 2.

ARS § 13-2907 (False reporting; emergency response costs; classification; definitions): 4. "Public agency" means this state, any city, county, municipal corporation or district, any Arizona federally recognized Native American tribe or any other public authority that is located in whole or in part in this state and that provides police, fire fighting, medical or other emergency services.
ARS § 13-2907 (False reporting; emergency response costs; classification; definitions): 5. "Serious offense" has the same meaning as provided in section 13-706.

ARS § 13-2907.01 (False reporting to law enforcement agencies; classification): A. It is unlawful for a person to knowingly make to a law enforcement agency of either this state or a political subdivision of this state a false, fraudulent or unfounded report or statement or to knowingly misrepresent a fact for the purpose of interfering with the orderly operation of a law enforcement agency or misleading a peace officer.
ARS § 13-2907.01 (False reporting to law enforcement agencies; classification): B. Violation of this section is a class 1 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2907.02 (False reporting of child abuse or neglect; classification): A person who knowingly and intentionally makes a false report of child abuse or neglect knowing the report is false or a person who coerces another person to make a false report of child abuse or neglect knowing the report is false is guilty of a class 1 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2907.03 (False reporting of sexual assault involving a spouse; classification): A person who intentionally makes a false report of sexual assault involving a spouse knowing the report is false or a person who coerces another person to make a false report of sexual assault involving a spouse knowing the report is false is guilty of a class 1 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2907.04 (False reporting of vulnerable adult abuse; classification): A. It is unlawful for a person to intentionally make a false report of vulnerable adult abuse or neglect to a law enforcement agency or to another person who is required by law to report the information to a law enforcement agency.
ARS § 13-2907.04 (False reporting of vulnerable adult abuse; classification): B. A violation of this section is a class 1 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2907.05 (False reporting of an offense involving corrections or probation employees; classification): A person who intentionally makes a false report of an offense listed in section 13-1409 or 13-1419 knowing the report is false or a person who coerces another person to make a false report of an offense listed in section 13-1409 or 13-1419 knowing the report is false is guilty of a class 1 misdemeanor.
ARS § 13-2908 (Criminal nuisance; classification): A. A person commits criminal nuisance:

ARS § 13-2908 (Criminal nuisance; classification): 1. If, by conduct either unlawful in itself or unreasonable under the circumstances, such person recklessly creates or maintains a condition which endangers the safety or health of others.
ARS § 13-2908 (Criminal nuisance; classification): 2. By knowingly conducting or maintaining any premises, place or resort where persons gather for purposes of engaging in unlawful conduct.
ARS § 13-2908 (Criminal nuisance; classification): B. Criminal nuisance is a class 3 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2909 (Residential picketing; classification): A. A person commits residential picketing if the person intentionally engages in picketing or otherwise demonstrates before or about an individual's residence or dwelling place and both of the following apply:
ARS § 13-2909 (Residential picketing; classification): 1. The picketing or demonstrating is intentionally directed at a person who resides in the residence or dwelling place.

ARS § 13-2909 (Residential picketing; classification): 2. A reasonable person would find the person's picketing or demonstrating to be harassing, threatening or alarming to a person in the residence or dwelling place.
ARS § 13-2909 (Residential picketing; classification): B. This section does not apply to a residence or dwelling place that is also used as the individual's principal place of business.
ARS § 13-2909 (Residential picketing; classification): C. Residential picketing is a class 3 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): A. A person commits cruelty to animals if the person does any of the following:

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 1. Intentionally, knowingly or recklessly subjects any animal under the person's custody or control to cruel neglect or abandonment.
