ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 2. Intentionally, knowingly or recklessly fails to provide medical attention necessary to prevent protracted suffering to any animal under the person's custody or control.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 3. Intentionally, knowingly or recklessly inflicts unnecessary physical injury to any animal.
ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 4. Recklessly subjects any animal to cruel mistreatment.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 5. Intentionally, knowingly or recklessly kills any animal under the custody or control of another person without either legal privilege or consent of the owner.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 6. Recklessly interferes with, kills or harms a working or service animal without either legal privilege or consent of the owner.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 7. Intentionally, knowingly or recklessly leaves an animal unattended and confined in a motor vehicle and physical injury to or death of the animal is likely to result.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 8. Intentionally or knowingly subjects any animal under the person's custody or control to cruel neglect or abandonment that results in serious physical injury to the animal.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 9. Intentionally or knowingly subjects any animal to cruel mistreatment.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 10. Intentionally or knowingly interferes with a working or service animal without either legal privilege or consent of the owner.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 11. Intentionally or knowingly kills or seriously harms a service animal without either legal privilege or consent of the owner.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 12. Intentionally or knowingly allows any dog that is under the person's custody or control to interfere with, kill or cause physical injury to a service animal.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 13. Recklessly allows any dog that is under the person's custody or control to interfere with, kill or cause physical injury to a service animal.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 14. Intentionally or knowingly obtains or exerts unauthorized control over a service animal with the intent to deprive the service animal handler of the service animal.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 15. Intentionally or knowingly subjects a domestic animal to cruel mistreatment.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 16. Intentionally or knowingly kills a domestic animal without either legal privilege or consent of the domestic animal's owner or handler.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 17. Intentionally or knowingly harasses a working animal that is in a law enforcement vehicle or trailer without either legal privilege or consent of the owner.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 18. Intentionally, knowingly or recklessly fails to provide medical attention necessary to prevent unreasonable suffering to any domestic animal under the person's custody or control.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 19. Intentionally or knowingly kills or causes serious harm to a working animal without either legal privilege or consent of the owner.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): B. In addition to any justification defense that is applicable pursuant to chapter 4 of this title, it is a defense to subsection A of this section if:

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 1. Any person exposes poison to be taken by a dog that has killed or wounded livestock or poison to be taken by predatory animals on premises owned, leased or controlled by the person for the purpose of protecting the person or the person's livestock or poultry, the treated property is kept posted by the person who authorized or performed the treatment until the poison has been removed and the poison is removed by the person exposing the poison after the threat to the person or the person's livestock or poultry has ceased to exist. The posting required shall provide adequate warning to persons who enter the property by the point or points of normal entry. The warning notice that is posted shall be readable at a distance of fifty feet, shall contain a poison statement and symbol and shall state the word "danger" or "warning".

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 2. Any person uses poisons in and immediately around buildings owned, leased or controlled by the person for the purpose of controlling wild and domestic rodents as otherwise allowed by the laws of the state, excluding any fur-bearing animals as defined in section 17-101.
ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): C. This section does not prohibit or restrict:

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 1. The taking of wildlife or other activities permitted by or pursuant to title 17.
ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 2. Activities permitted by or pursuant to title 3.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 3. Activities regulated by the Arizona game and fish department or the Arizona department of agriculture.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): D. A peace officer, animal control enforcement agent or animal control enforcement deputy may use reasonable force to open a vehicle to rescue an animal if the animal is left in the vehicle as prescribed in subsection A, paragraph 7 of this section.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): E. A person who is convicted of a violation of subsection A, paragraph 6, 10, 11 or 19 of this section is liable as follows:

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 1. If the working or service animal was injured, killed or disabled, to the owner or agency that owns the working or service animal and that employs the handler or to the owner or handler for the replacement and training costs of the working or service animal and for any veterinary bills.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 2. To the owner or agency that owns a working or service animal for the salary of the handler for the period of time that the handler's services are lost to the owner or agency.
ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 3. To the owner for the owner's contractual losses with the agency.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): F. An incorporated city or town or a county may adopt an ordinance with misdemeanor provisions at least as stringent as the misdemeanor provisions of this section, except that any ordinance adopted shall not prohibit or restrict any activity involving a dog, whether the dog is restrained or not, if the activity is directly related to the business of shepherding or herding livestock and the activity is necessary for the safety of a human, the dog or livestock or is permitted by or pursuant to title 3.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): G. If a judicial officer orders the release of a person who is currently serving a term of probation for a violation of this section and who is charged with a new violation of this section on the person's own recognizance or on the execution of bail, the judicial officer shall impose a condition of release that prohibits the person from possessing or having contact with any animal.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): H. A person who violates subsection A, paragraph 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 13, 17 or 18 of this section is guilty of a class 1 misdemeanor.  A person who violates subsection A, paragraph 8, 9, 10, 12 or 14 of this section is guilty of a class 6 felony. A person who violates subsection A, paragraph 11, 15, 16 or 19 of this section is guilty of a class 5 felony.
ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): I. For the purposes of this section:
ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 1. "Animal" means a mammal, bird, reptile or amphibian.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 2. "Cruel mistreatment" means to torture or otherwise inflict unnecessary serious physical injury on an animal or to kill an animal in a manner that causes protracted suffering to the animal.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 3. "Cruel neglect" means to fail to provide an animal with necessary food, water or shelter or to fail to provide a domestic animal with any of the following:

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): (a) Except for a dog that primarily resides outdoors, access to shelter that is necessary and adequate.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): (b) For a dog that primarily resides outdoors, except while a dog is engaged in or training for lawful hunting, police, military or patrol work, search and rescue, herding or livestock guarding, trials and other lawful competitions, service and assistance work and other working, sporting and competitive functions or is under the custody or control of a person who has no permanent place of residence, access to shelter that meets all of the following requirements:

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): (i) Has a natural or artificial cover that is accessible throughout the year.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): (ii) Is maintained in good repair, is of sufficient size to protect the dog from injury and allows the dog to stand, turn around, lie down in a natural manner and maintain normal body temperature.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): (iii) Is maintained in a manner that minimizes the risk of disease, infestation or parasites.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 4. "Domestic animal" means a mammal, bird, reptile or amphibian, not regulated by title 3, that is kept primarily as a pet or companion or that is bred to be a pet or companion.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 5. "Handler" means a law enforcement officer or any other person who has successfully completed a course of training prescribed by the person's agency or the service animal owner and who used a specially trained animal under the direction of the person's agency or the service animal owner.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 6. "Harass" means to engage in conduct that a reasonable person would expect to impede or interfere with a working animal's performance of its duties.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 7. "Service animal" means an animal that has completed a formal training program, that assists its owner in one or more daily living tasks that are associated with a productive lifestyle and that is trained to not pose a danger to the health and safety of the general public.

ARS § 13-2910 (Cruelty to animals; interference with working or service animal; release conditions; classification; definitions): 8. "Working animal" means a horse or dog that is used by a law enforcement agency, that is specially trained for law enforcement work and that is under the control of a handler.
ARS § 13-2910.01 (Animal fighting; classification): A. A person commits animal fighting by knowingly:

ARS § 13-2910.01 (Animal fighting; classification): 1. Owning, possessing, keeping or training any animal if the person knows or has reason to know that the animal will engage in an exhibition of fighting with another animal.
ARS § 13-2910.01 (Animal fighting; classification): 2. For amusement or gain, causing any animal to fight with another animal, or causing any animals to injure each other.
ARS § 13-2910.01 (Animal fighting; classification): 3. Permitting any act in violation of paragraph 1 or 2 to be done on any premises under the person’s charge or control.
ARS § 13-2910.01 (Animal fighting; classification): B. This section does not:
ARS § 13-2910.01 (Animal fighting; classification): 1. Prohibit or restrict activities permitted by or pursuant to title 3.
ARS § 13-2910.01 (Animal fighting; classification): 2. Apply to animals that are trained to protect livestock from predation and that engage in actions to protect livestock.
ARS § 13-2910.01 (Animal fighting; classification): C. Animal fighting is a class 5 felony.

ARS § 13-2910.02 (Presence at animal fight; classification): Any person who is knowingly present at any place or building where preparations are being made for an exhibition of the fighting of animals, or who is present at such exhibition, is guilty of a class 6 felony.
ARS § 13-2910.03 (Cockfighting; classification): (Caution: 1998 Prop. 105 applies)
ARS § 13-2910.03 (Cockfighting; classification): A. A person commits cockfighting by knowingly:
ARS § 13-2910.03 (Cockfighting; classification): 1. Owning, possessing, keeping or training any cock with the intent that such cock engage in an exhibition of fighting with another cock.
ARS § 13-2910.03 (Cockfighting; classification): 2. For amusement or gain, causing any cock to fight with another cock or causing any cocks to injure each other.
ARS § 13-2910.03 (Cockfighting; classification): 3. Permitting any act in violation of paragraph 1 or 2 to be done on any premises under his charge or control.
ARS § 13-2910.03 (Cockfighting; classification): B. Cockfighting is a class 5 felony.

ARS § 13-2910.03 (Cockfighting; classification): C. For purposes of this section and section 13-2910.04, cock means any male chicken, including game fowl except wildlife as defined in Arizona Revised Statutes section 17-101.
ARS § 13-2910.04 (Presence at cockfight; classification): (Caution: 1998 Prop. 105 applies)

ARS § 13-2910.04 (Presence at cockfight; classification): Any person who is knowingly present at any place or building where preparations are being made for an exhibition of the fighting of cocks, or is present at such exhibition, is guilty of a class 1 misdemeanor.
ARS § 13-2910.05 (Exempt activities): (Caution:  1998 Prop. 105 applies)

ARS § 13-2910.05 (Exempt activities): Activity involving the possession, training, exhibition or use of an animal in the otherwise lawful pursuits of hunting, ranching, farming, rodeos, shows and security services shall be exempt from the provisions of sections 13-2910.01, 13-2910.02, 13-2910.03 and 13-2910.04 and 13-2910.10.
ARS § 13-2910.06 (Defense to cruelty to animals and bird fighting): (Caution: 1998 Prop. 105 applies)

ARS § 13-2910.06 (Defense to cruelty to animals and bird fighting): It is a defense to sections 13-2910, 13-2910.01, 13-2910.02, 13-2910.03 and 13-2910.04 that the activity charged involves the possession, training, exhibition or use of a bird or animal in the otherwise lawful sports of falconry, animal hunting, rodeos, ranching or the training or use of hunting dogs.
ARS § 13-2910.07 (Cruel and inhumane confinement of a pig during pregnancy or of a calf raised for veal): (Caution:  1998 Prop. 105 applies)

ARS § 13-2910.07 (Cruel and inhumane confinement of a pig during pregnancy or of a calf raised for veal): A. Notwithstanding any other provision of title 3 or title 13, a person shall not tether or confine any pig during pregnancy or any calf raised for veal, on a farm, for all or the majority of any day, in a manner that prevents such animal from:
ARS § 13-2910.07 (Cruel and inhumane confinement of a pig during pregnancy or of a calf raised for veal): 1. Lying down and fully extending his or her limbs; or
ARS § 13-2910.07 (Cruel and inhumane confinement of a pig during pregnancy or of a calf raised for veal): 2. Turning around freely.
ARS § 13-2910.07 (Cruel and inhumane confinement of a pig during pregnancy or of a calf raised for veal): B. This section shall not apply to:
ARS § 13-2910.07 (Cruel and inhumane confinement of a pig during pregnancy or of a calf raised for veal): 1. Pigs or calves during transportation.

ARS § 13-2910.07 (Cruel and inhumane confinement of a pig during pregnancy or of a calf raised for veal): 2. Pigs or calves in rodeo exhibitions, state or county fair exhibitions, or other similar exhibitions.

ARS § 13-2910.07 (Cruel and inhumane confinement of a pig during pregnancy or of a calf raised for veal): 3. The killing of pigs or calves according to the provisions of chapter 13, title 3 and other applicable law and regulations.
ARS § 13-2910.07 (Cruel and inhumane confinement of a pig during pregnancy or of a calf raised for veal): 4. Pigs or calves involved in lawful scientific or agricultural research.

ARS § 13-2910.07 (Cruel and inhumane confinement of a pig during pregnancy or of a calf raised for veal): 5. Pigs or calves while undergoing an examination, test, treatment or operation for veterinary purposes.
ARS § 13-2910.07 (Cruel and inhumane confinement of a pig during pregnancy or of a calf raised for veal): 6. A pig during the seven day period prior to the pig's expected date of giving birth.
ARS § 13-2910.07 (Cruel and inhumane confinement of a pig during pregnancy or of a calf raised for veal): C. A person who violates this section is guilty of a class 1 misdemeanor.
ARS § 13-2910.07 (Cruel and inhumane confinement of a pig during pregnancy or of a calf raised for veal): D. The following definitions shall govern this section:
ARS § 13-2910.07 (Cruel and inhumane confinement of a pig during pregnancy or of a calf raised for veal): 1. "Calf" means a calf of the bovine species.

ARS § 13-2910.07 (Cruel and inhumane confinement of a pig during pregnancy or of a calf raised for veal): 2. "Calf raised for veal" means a calf raised with the intent of selling, marketing or distributing the meat, organs or any part of such calf as a food product described as "veal."

ARS § 13-2910.07 (Cruel and inhumane confinement of a pig during pregnancy or of a calf raised for veal): 3. "Farm" means the land, buildings, support facilities, and other equipment that is wholly or partially used for the production of animals for food or fiber.
ARS § 13-2910.07 (Cruel and inhumane confinement of a pig during pregnancy or of a calf raised for veal): 4. "Pig" means any animal of the porcine species.

ARS § 13-2910.07 (Cruel and inhumane confinement of a pig during pregnancy or of a calf raised for veal): 5. "Turning around freely" means having the ability to turn around in a complete circle without any impediment, including a tether, or, in the case of an enclosure (including what is commonly described as a "gestation crate" for pigs and a "veal crate" for calves) without touching any side of the enclosure.
ARS § 13-2910.08 (The humane treatment of farm animals fund): (Conditionally Eff.  Caution: 1998 Prop. 105 applies)

ARS § 13-2910.08 (The humane treatment of farm animals fund): The "humane treatment of farm animals fund" is hereby established to be administered by the attorney general under the conditions and for the purposes provided by this section.  Upon receipt, the attorney general shall deposit in the fund any monies received for the state as a result of enforcement of the humane treatment of farm animals act and any monies received by the attorney general as a money donation to the fund from any public or private group, society, association or individual.  The monies in the fund shall be used only for mandatory expenditures, if any, required by the humane treatment of farm animals act and administration of the fund. Monies in the fund are not subject to legislative appropriation.  The fund is exempt from statutory provisions relating to lapsing of appropriations and shall not revert to the general fund.
ARS § 13-2910.09 (Equine tripping; classification; definitions): A. A person who knowingly or intentionally trips an equine for entertainment or sport is guilty of a class 1 misdemeanor.
ARS § 13-2910.09 (Equine tripping; classification; definitions): B. A person who is convicted of a first violation of this section:

ARS § 13-2910.09 (Equine tripping; classification; definitions): 1. Shall be sentenced to serve not less than forty-eight consecutive hours in jail and is not eligible for probation or suspension of execution of sentence unless the entire sentence is served.
ARS § 13-2910.09 (Equine tripping; classification; definitions): 2. Shall pay a fine of not less than one thousand dollars.
ARS § 13-2910.09 (Equine tripping; classification; definitions): C. A person who is convicted of a second violation of this section:

ARS § 13-2910.09 (Equine tripping; classification; definitions): 1. Shall be sentenced to serve not less than thirty consecutive days in jail and is not eligible for probation or suspension of execution of sentence unless the entire sentence is served.
ARS § 13-2910.09 (Equine tripping; classification; definitions): 2. Shall pay a fine of not less than two thousand dollars.
ARS § 13-2910.09 (Equine tripping; classification; definitions): D. A person who is convicted of a third or subsequent violation of this section:

ARS § 13-2910.09 (Equine tripping; classification; definitions): 1. Shall be sentenced to serve not less than ninety consecutive days in jail and is not eligible for probation or suspension of execution of sentence unless the entire sentence is served.
ARS § 13-2910.09 (Equine tripping; classification; definitions): 2. Shall pay a fine of not less than two thousand dollars.

ARS § 13-2910.09 (Equine tripping; classification; definitions): E. This section does not apply to any jumping or steeplechase events, racing, training, branding, show events, calf or steer roping events, bulldogging or steer wrestling events or any other traditional western rodeo events, including barrel racing, bareback or saddled bronc riding or other similar activities or events.
ARS § 13-2910.09 (Equine tripping; classification; definitions): F. For the purposes of this section:
ARS § 13-2910.09 (Equine tripping; classification; definitions): 1. "Equine" means a horse, pony, mule, donkey or hinny.

ARS § 13-2910.09 (Equine tripping; classification; definitions): 2. "Trips" means knowingly or intentionally causing an equine to lose its balance or fall by use of a wire, pole, stick or rope or any other object or by any other means.

ARS § 13-2910.10 (Ownership, possession, purchase, sale, transfer or manufacture of animal fighting paraphernalia; classification; definition): A. It is unlawful for a person to knowingly own, possess, purchase, sell, transfer or manufacture animal fighting paraphernalia for the purpose of engaging in, promoting or facilitating animal fighting pursuant to section 13-2910.01 or cockfighting pursuant to section 13-2910.03.

ARS § 13-2910.10 (Ownership, possession, purchase, sale, transfer or manufacture of animal fighting paraphernalia; classification; definition): B. A person who violates this section is guilty of a class 1 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2910.10 (Ownership, possession, purchase, sale, transfer or manufacture of animal fighting paraphernalia; classification; definition): C. For the purposes of this section, "animal fighting paraphernalia":

ARS § 13-2910.10 (Ownership, possession, purchase, sale, transfer or manufacture of animal fighting paraphernalia; classification; definition): 1. Means equipment, products, implements or materials of any kind that are used, intended for use or designed solely for use in animal fighting or cockfighting or training, preparing, conditioning or furthering animal fighting or cockfighting.

ARS § 13-2910.10 (Ownership, possession, purchase, sale, transfer or manufacture of animal fighting paraphernalia; classification; definition): 2. Includes breaking sticks, cat mills, treadmills, fighting pits, springpoles, gaffs, slashers and heels and other sharp implements that are designed to be attached in place of the natural spur of a cock or game fowl.

ARS § 13-2910.11 (Unlawful animal ownership or possession; transfer of animals; restoration of right to possess animals; classification; good cause exception; definitions): A. It is unlawful for a person who has been convicted of any of the following offenses to own, possess, adopt, foster, reside with or otherwise intentionally contact, care for or have custody of any animal in the person's household:

ARS § 13-2910.11 (Unlawful animal ownership or possession; transfer of animals; restoration of right to possess animals; classification; good cause exception; definitions): 1. An intentional or knowing violation of cruelty to animals pursuant to section 13-2910, subsection A, paragraph 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 9, 12, 15 or 16.

ARS § 13-2910.11 (Unlawful animal ownership or possession; transfer of animals; restoration of right to possess animals; classification; good cause exception; definitions): 2. Cruelty to animals pursuant to section 13-2910, subsection A, paragraph 4.

ARS § 13-2910.11 (Unlawful animal ownership or possession; transfer of animals; restoration of right to possess animals; classification; good cause exception; definitions): 3. Animal fighting pursuant to section 13-2910.01.

ARS § 13-2910.11 (Unlawful animal ownership or possession; transfer of animals; restoration of right to possess animals; classification; good cause exception; definitions): 4. Bestiality pursuant to section 13-1411.

ARS § 13-2910.11 (Unlawful animal ownership or possession; transfer of animals; restoration of right to possess animals; classification; good cause exception; definitions): B. Except as provided in subsection D of this section, the prohibitions listed in subsection A of this section shall remain in place for the following amount of time:

ARS § 13-2910.11 (Unlawful animal ownership or possession; transfer of animals; restoration of right to possess animals; classification; good cause exception; definitions): 1. For a first misdemeanor conviction, at least five years.

ARS § 13-2910.11 (Unlawful animal ownership or possession; transfer of animals; restoration of right to possess animals; classification; good cause exception; definitions): 2. For a first felony conviction or a second or subsequent misdemeanor conviction, at least ten years.

ARS § 13-2910.11 (Unlawful animal ownership or possession; transfer of animals; restoration of right to possess animals; classification; good cause exception; definitions): 3. For a second or subsequent felony conviction, for the person's lifetime.

ARS § 13-2910.11 (Unlawful animal ownership or possession; transfer of animals; restoration of right to possess animals; classification; good cause exception; definitions): C. Within thirty days after a person is prohibited from possessing an animal pursuant to this section, the person shall transfer all animals in the person's care or custody to another person who is not in the person's household.

ARS § 13-2910.11 (Unlawful animal ownership or possession; transfer of animals; restoration of right to possess animals; classification; good cause exception; definitions): D. On proper application and not less than one year after the person is convicted of a misdemeanor violation of an offense listed in subsection A of this section or two and one-half years after the person is convicted of a felony violation of an offense listed in subsection A of this section, the person may apply to have the person's right to possess an animal restored. Any time spent on absconder status while on probation, on escape status or incarcerated is excluded in calculating the minimum time requirement. The person may apply to the judge, justice of the peace or magistrate who pronounced sentence or imposed probation or the successor in office of the judge, justice of the peace or magistrate. The applicant shall serve a copy of the application on the prosecutor. The court shall conduct a hearing on the request within sixty days after the application is filed. The defendant bears the burden by a preponderance of evidence at the hearing. To assist the court in making a determination, the court shall require the person to complete a psychiatric or psychological examination and undergo counseling, if necessary, before restoring the person's right to possess an animal. The court may terminate or reduce the time period required by subsection B of this section on a finding that:

ARS § 13-2910.11 (Unlawful animal ownership or possession; transfer of animals; restoration of right to possess animals; classification; good cause exception; definitions): 1. The applicant does not present a danger to self, the animal's immediate family and the public.

ARS § 13-2910.11 (Unlawful animal ownership or possession; transfer of animals; restoration of right to possess animals; classification; good cause exception; definitions): 2. The applicant has the ability to properly care for all animals in the applicant's possession.

ARS § 13-2910.11 (Unlawful animal ownership or possession; transfer of animals; restoration of right to possess animals; classification; good cause exception; definitions): 3. The applicant has successfully completed all classes or counseling that was ordered by the sentencing court.

ARS § 13-2910.11 (Unlawful animal ownership or possession; transfer of animals; restoration of right to possess animals; classification; good cause exception; definitions): E. A convicted person who lives in a household with an animal that is owned, possessed, adopted or fostered by another person in the household may apply to the court for a good cause exception. A good cause exception is valid for one year and allows the convicted person to reside in the same household as an animal. The convicted person may request the court to renew a good cause exception sixty days before the good cause exception expires. The court may grant a good cause exception or renew a good cause exception if all of the following apply:

ARS § 13-2910.11 (Unlawful animal ownership or possession; transfer of animals; restoration of right to possess animals; classification; good cause exception; definitions): 1. The convicted person is on supervised or unsupervised probation, community supervision or parole or agrees to be subject to the court's jurisdiction and supervision while living in the household.

ARS § 13-2910.11 (Unlawful animal ownership or possession; transfer of animals; restoration of right to possess animals; classification; good cause exception; definitions): 2. The court determines that it is in the best interests of the animal and the person who owns, possesses, adopts or fosters the animal to allow the convicted person to remain in the same household and reside with the animal.

ARS § 13-2910.11 (Unlawful animal ownership or possession; transfer of animals; restoration of right to possess animals; classification; good cause exception; definitions): 3. The convicted person agrees to not intentionally contact, care for or have custody of the animal.

ARS § 13-2910.11 (Unlawful animal ownership or possession; transfer of animals; restoration of right to possess animals; classification; good cause exception; definitions): F. A person who violates this section is guilty of a class 1 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2910.11 (Unlawful animal ownership or possession; transfer of animals; restoration of right to possess animals; classification; good cause exception; definitions): G. For the purposes of this section:
ARS § 13-2910.11 (Unlawful animal ownership or possession; transfer of animals; restoration of right to possess animals; classification; good cause exception; definitions): 1. "Animal":

ARS § 13-2910.11 (Unlawful animal ownership or possession; transfer of animals; restoration of right to possess animals; classification; good cause exception; definitions): (a) Means any domesticated dog or cat.

ARS § 13-2910.11 (Unlawful animal ownership or possession; transfer of animals; restoration of right to possess animals; classification; good cause exception; definitions): (b) Does not include livestock as defined in section 3-1201 or wildlife as defined in section 17-101.

ARS § 13-2910.11 (Unlawful animal ownership or possession; transfer of animals; restoration of right to possess animals; classification; good cause exception; definitions): 2. "Household" includes all of the persons who occupy a housing unit as the person's usual place of residence, including all of the following:

ARS § 13-2910.11 (Unlawful animal ownership or possession; transfer of animals; restoration of right to possess animals; classification; good cause exception; definitions): (a) The related family members and all unrelated persons, if any, such as lodgers, foster children, wards or employees who share the housing unit.

ARS § 13-2910.11 (Unlawful animal ownership or possession; transfer of animals; restoration of right to possess animals; classification; good cause exception; definitions): (b) A person who lives alone in a housing unit or a group of unrelated persons sharing a housing unit such as partners or roomers.

ARS § 13-2910.11 (Unlawful animal ownership or possession; transfer of animals; restoration of right to possess animals; classification; good cause exception; definitions): 3. "Housing unit" means a house, an apartment, a mobile home or trailer, a group of rooms or a single room occupied as separate living quarters for a household and includes any front, side or rear yards and any garages and detached garages that are under the control of the household.

ARS § 13-2910.12 (Presence of minor at animal fight or cockfight; classification): A. A person who knowingly causes, allows or assists a minor to attend an animal fight or cockfight or to be present at any place or building where preparations are being made for an exhibition of animal fighting or cockfighting in violation of section 13-2910.01, 13-2910.02, 13-2910.03 or 13-2910.04 is guilty of a class 1 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2910.12 (Presence of minor at animal fight or cockfight; classification): B. This section does not preclude the prosecution of the person for any offense based on any act not covered by this section.

ARS § 13-2911 (Interference with or disruption of an educational institution; violation; classification; definitions): A. A person commits interference with or disruption of an educational institution by doing any of the following:

ARS § 13-2911 (Interference with or disruption of an educational institution; violation; classification; definitions): 1. Intentionally, knowingly or recklessly interfering with or disrupting the normal operations of an educational institution by either:

ARS § 13-2911 (Interference with or disruption of an educational institution; violation; classification; definitions): (a) Threatening to cause physical injury to any employee or student of an educational institution or any person on the property of an educational institution.

ARS § 13-2911 (Interference with or disruption of an educational institution; violation; classification; definitions): (b) Threatening to cause damage to any educational institution, the property of any educational institution or the property of any employee or student of an educational institution.

ARS § 13-2911 (Interference with or disruption of an educational institution; violation; classification; definitions): 2. Intentionally or knowingly entering or remaining on the property of any educational institution for the purpose of interfering with the lawful use of the property or in any manner as to deny or interfere with the lawful use of the property by others.

ARS § 13-2911 (Interference with or disruption of an educational institution; violation; classification; definitions): 3. Intentionally or knowingly refusing to obey a lawful order given pursuant to subsection C of this section.

ARS § 13-2911 (Interference with or disruption of an educational institution; violation; classification; definitions): B. To constitute a violation of this section, the acts that are prohibited by subsection A, paragraph 1 of this section are not required to be directed at a specific individual, a specific educational institution or any specific property of an educational institution.

ARS § 13-2911 (Interference with or disruption of an educational institution; violation; classification; definitions): C. The chief administrative officer of an educational institution or an officer or employee designated by the chief administrative officer to maintain order may order a person to leave the property of the educational institution if the officer or employee has reasonable grounds to believe either that:

ARS § 13-2911 (Interference with or disruption of an educational institution; violation; classification; definitions): 1. Any person or persons are committing any act that interferes with or disrupts the lawful use of the property by others at the educational institution.

ARS § 13-2911 (Interference with or disruption of an educational institution; violation; classification; definitions): 2. Any person has entered on the property of an educational institution for the purpose of committing any act that interferes with or disrupts the lawful use of the property by others at the educational institution.

ARS § 13-2911 (Interference with or disruption of an educational institution; violation; classification; definitions): D. The appropriate governing board of every educational institution shall adopt rules pursuant to title 41, chapter 6 for the maintenance of public order on all property of any educational institution under its jurisdiction that is used for educational purposes and shall provide a program for the enforcement of its rules.  The rules shall govern the conduct of students, faculty and other staff and all members of the public while on the property of the educational institution.  Penalties for violations of the rules shall be clearly set forth and enforced.  Penalties shall include provisions for the ejection of a violator from the property and, in the case of a student, faculty member or other staff violator, the violator's suspension or expulsion or any other appropriate disciplinary action.  A governing board shall amend its rules as necessary to ensure the maintenance of public order.  Any deadly weapon, dangerous instrument or explosive that is used, displayed or possessed by a person in violation of a rule adopted pursuant to this subsection shall be forfeited and sold or otherwise disposed of pursuant to section 13-3105 and chapter 39 of this title.  This subsection does not do either of the following:

ARS § 13-2911 (Interference with or disruption of an educational institution; violation; classification; definitions): 1. Preclude school districts from conducting approved gun safety programs on school campuses.

ARS § 13-2911 (Interference with or disruption of an educational institution; violation; classification; definitions): 2. Apply to private universities, colleges, high schools or common schools or other private educational institutions.

ARS § 13-2911 (Interference with or disruption of an educational institution; violation; classification; definitions): E. An educational institution is not eligible to receive any state aid or assistance unless rules are adopted in accordance with this section.

ARS § 13-2911 (Interference with or disruption of an educational institution; violation; classification; definitions): F. This section does not prevent or limit the authority of the governing board of any educational institution to discharge any employee or expel, suspend or otherwise punish any student for any violation of its rules, even though the violation is unlawful under this chapter or is otherwise an offense.

ARS § 13-2911 (Interference with or disruption of an educational institution; violation; classification; definitions): G. This section may be enforced by any peace officer in this state wherever and whenever a violation occurs.

ARS § 13-2911 (Interference with or disruption of an educational institution; violation; classification; definitions): H. Restitution under sections 8-341, 8-345 and 13-603 applies to any financial loss that is suffered by a person or educational institution as a result of a violation of this section.

ARS § 13-2911 (Interference with or disruption of an educational institution; violation; classification; definitions): I. Notwithstanding section 15-341 and subsection D of this section, the governing board of an educational institution may not adopt or enforce any policy or rule that prohibits the lawful possession or carrying of a deadly weapon on a public right-of-way by a person or on or within a person's means of transportation.

ARS § 13-2911 (Interference with or disruption of an educational institution; violation; classification; definitions): J. Interference with or disruption of an educational institution pursuant to subsection A, paragraph 1 of this section is a class 6 felony. Interference with or disruption of an educational institution pursuant to subsection A, paragraph 2 or 3 of this section is a class 1 misdemeanor.
ARS § 13-2911 (Interference with or disruption of an educational institution; violation; classification; definitions): K. For the purposes of this section:

ARS § 13-2911 (Interference with or disruption of an educational institution; violation; classification; definitions): 1. "Educational institution" means, except as otherwise provided, any university, college, community college, high school or common school in this state.

ARS § 13-2911 (Interference with or disruption of an educational institution; violation; classification; definitions): 2. "Governing board" means the body, whether appointed or elected, that has responsibility for the maintenance and government of an educational institution.

ARS § 13-2911 (Interference with or disruption of an educational institution; violation; classification; definitions): 3. "Interference with or disruption of" includes any act that might reasonably lead to the evacuation or closure of any property of the educational institution or the postponement, cancellation or suspension of any class or other school activity.  For the purposes of this paragraph, an actual evacuation, closure, postponement, cancellation or suspension is not required for the act to be considered an interference or disruption.

ARS § 13-2911 (Interference with or disruption of an educational institution; violation; classification; definitions): 4. "Property of an educational institution" means all land, buildings and other facilities that are owned, operated or controlled by the governing board of an educational institution and that are devoted to educational purposes.

ARS § 13-2911 (Interference with or disruption of an educational institution; violation; classification; definitions): 5. "Public right-of-way" means any highway, street, road, thoroughfare, path, alley or other right-of-way that is publicly accessible and that is established and maintained by this state or a political subdivision of this state. Public right-of-way does not include property of an educational institution.

ARS § 13-2912 (Unlawful introduction of disease or parasite; classification): A. It is unlawful for a person to knowingly introduce into this state a disease or parasite of animals or poultry that constitutes a threat to:
ARS § 13-2912 (Unlawful introduction of disease or parasite; classification): 1. Livestock or poultry industry in this state.
ARS § 13-2912 (Unlawful introduction of disease or parasite; classification): 2. Human health.
ARS § 13-2912 (Unlawful introduction of disease or parasite; classification): 3. Human life.
ARS § 13-2912 (Unlawful introduction of disease or parasite; classification): B. This section does not apply to research conducted by government or educational institutions.
ARS § 13-2912 (Unlawful introduction of disease or parasite; classification): C. A violation of subsection A:
ARS § 13-2912 (Unlawful introduction of disease or parasite; classification): 1. Paragraph 1 is a class 5 felony.
ARS § 13-2912 (Unlawful introduction of disease or parasite; classification): 2. Paragraph 2 is a class 4 felony.
ARS § 13-2912 (Unlawful introduction of disease or parasite; classification): 3. Paragraph 3 is a class 2 felony.

ARS § 13-2913 (Unlawful violation of fire ban; classification): A. It is unlawful for a person to enter or remain in any public building or on any public property in violation of any order or rule that is issued by any officer or agency having the power of control, management or supervision of the building or property and that relates to the control and limitation of fires, including any prohibition, restriction or ban on fires, any provision to avert the start of or lessen the likelihood of wildfire and the designation of any place where fires are permitted, restricted, prohibited or banned.
ARS § 13-2913 (Unlawful violation of fire ban; classification): B. A person who violates this section is guilty of a class 2 misdemeanor.
ARS § 13-2914 (Aggressive solicitation; classification; definitions): A. It is unlawful for a person to solicit any money or other thing of value or solicit the sale of goods or services:

ARS § 13-2914 (Aggressive solicitation; classification; definitions): 1. Within fifteen feet of any bank entrance or exit or any automated teller machine if the person does not have permission to be there from the bank or the owner of the property on which the automated teller machine is located.
ARS § 13-2914 (Aggressive solicitation; classification; definitions): 2. In a public area by:

ARS § 13-2914 (Aggressive solicitation; classification; definitions): (a) Intentionally, knowingly or recklessly making any physical contact with or touching another person in the course of the solicitation without the person's consent.

ARS § 13-2914 (Aggressive solicitation; classification; definitions): (b) Approaching or following the person being solicited in a manner that is intended or is likely to cause a reasonable person to fear imminent bodily harm to oneself or another or damage to or loss of property or that is reasonably likely to intimidate the person being solicited into responding affirmatively to the solicitation.

ARS § 13-2914 (Aggressive solicitation; classification; definitions): (c) Continuing to solicit the person after the person being solicited has clearly communicated a request that the solicitation stop.

ARS § 13-2914 (Aggressive solicitation; classification; definitions): (d) Intentionally, knowingly or recklessly obstructing the safe or free passage of the person being solicited or requiring the person to take evasive action to avoid physical contact with the person making the solicitation.  This subdivision does not apply to acts that are authorized as an exercise of one's constitutional right to picket or protest.

ARS § 13-2914 (Aggressive solicitation; classification; definitions): (e) Intentionally, knowingly or recklessly using obscene or abusive language or gestures that are intended or likely to cause a reasonable person to fear imminent bodily harm or that are reasonably likely to intimidate the person being solicited into responding affirmatively to the solicitation.
ARS § 13-2914 (Aggressive solicitation; classification; definitions): B. A violation of this section is a petty offense.
ARS § 13-2914 (Aggressive solicitation; classification; definitions): C. For the purposes of this section:
ARS § 13-2914 (Aggressive solicitation; classification; definitions): 1. "Automated teller machine" has the same meaning prescribed in section 6-101.
ARS § 13-2914 (Aggressive solicitation; classification; definitions): 2. "Bank" means a bank, credit union or other similar financial institution.

ARS § 13-2914 (Aggressive solicitation; classification; definitions): 3. "Public area" means an area that the public or a substantial group of persons has access to and includes alleys, bridges, buildings, driveways, parking lots, parks, playgrounds, plazas, sidewalks and streets open to the general public, and the doorways and entrances to buildings and dwellings and the grounds enclosing them.

ARS § 13-2914 (Aggressive solicitation; classification; definitions): 4. "Solicit" means using any means of communication, including by spoken, written or printed word, to request an immediate donation or exchange of money or other thing of value from another person regardless of the solicitor's purpose or intended use of the money or other thing of value.
ARS § 13-2915 (Preventing use of telephone in emergency; false representation of emergency; classification; definitions): A. It is unlawful for a person to do any of the following:

ARS § 13-2915 (Preventing use of telephone in emergency; false representation of emergency; classification; definitions): 1. Knowingly refuse to yield or surrender the use of a party line to another person to report a fire or summon police or medical or other aid in case of emergency.

ARS § 13-2915 (Preventing use of telephone in emergency; false representation of emergency; classification; definitions): 2.  Ask for or request the use of a party line on the pretext that an emergency exists, knowing that no emergency in fact exists.

ARS § 13-2915 (Preventing use of telephone in emergency; false representation of emergency; classification; definitions): 3. Intentionally prevent or interfere with the use of a telephone by another person in an emergency situation.

ARS § 13-2915 (Preventing use of telephone in emergency; false representation of emergency; classification; definitions): B. Every telephone directory that is compiled and distributed to subscribers shall contain a notice explaining this section.  The notice shall be printed in type that is no smaller than any other type on the same page, other than headings, and shall be preceded by the word "warning".  This subsection does not apply to directories that are distributed solely for business advertising purposes, commonly known as classified directories.

ARS § 13-2915 (Preventing use of telephone in emergency; false representation of emergency; classification; definitions): C. This section does not require a person to allow another person to enter the person's home or place of residence for the purpose of using a telephone in an emergency situation.
ARS § 13-2915 (Preventing use of telephone in emergency; false representation of emergency; classification; definitions): D. A person who violates this section is guilty of a class 2 misdemeanor.
ARS § 13-2915 (Preventing use of telephone in emergency; false representation of emergency; classification; definitions): E. For the purposes of this section:

ARS § 13-2915 (Preventing use of telephone in emergency; false representation of emergency; classification; definitions): 1. "Emergency" means a situation in which property or human life is in jeopardy and the prompt summoning of aid is essential.

ARS § 13-2915 (Preventing use of telephone in emergency; false representation of emergency; classification; definitions): 2. "Emergency situation" means a situation in which both of the following apply:

ARS § 13-2915 (Preventing use of telephone in emergency; false representation of emergency; classification; definitions): (a) Human health, life or safety is in jeopardy and the prompt summoning of aid is essential.

ARS § 13-2915 (Preventing use of telephone in emergency; false representation of emergency; classification; definitions): (b) It is reasonable to believe that a domestic violence offense pursuant to section 13-3601 is being, has been or is about to be committed.

ARS § 13-2915 (Preventing use of telephone in emergency; false representation of emergency; classification; definitions): 3. "Party line" means a subscriber's line telephone circuit, consisting of two or more main telephone stations connected therewith, each station with a distinctive ring or telephone number.

ARS § 13-2916 (Use of an electronic communication to terrify, intimidate, threaten or harass; unlawful use of electronic communication device; applicability; classification; definitions): A. It is unlawful for a person to knowingly terrify, intimidate, threaten or harass a specific person or persons by doing any of the following:

ARS § 13-2916 (Use of an electronic communication to terrify, intimidate, threaten or harass; unlawful use of electronic communication device; applicability; classification; definitions): 1. Directing any obscene, lewd or profane language or suggesting any lewd or lascivious act to the person in an electronic communication.

ARS § 13-2916 (Use of an electronic communication to terrify, intimidate, threaten or harass; unlawful use of electronic communication device; applicability; classification; definitions): 2. Threatening to inflict physical harm on any person or to property in any electronic communication.

ARS § 13-2916 (Use of an electronic communication to terrify, intimidate, threaten or harass; unlawful use of electronic communication device; applicability; classification; definitions): 3. Otherwise disturbing by repeated anonymous, unwanted or unsolicited electronic communications the peace, quiet or right of privacy of the person at the place where the communications were received.

ARS § 13-2916 (Use of an electronic communication to terrify, intimidate, threaten or harass; unlawful use of electronic communication device; applicability; classification; definitions): 4. Without the person's consent and for the purpose of imminently causing the person unwanted physical contact, injury or harassment by a third party, use an electronic communication device to electronically distribute, publish, email, hyperlink or make available for downloading the person's personal identifying information, including a digital image of the person, and the use does in fact incite or produce that unwanted physical contact, injury or harassment.  This paragraph also applies to a person who intends to terrify, intimidate, threaten or harass an immediate family member of the person whose personal identifying information is used.

ARS § 13-2916 (Use of an electronic communication to terrify, intimidate, threaten or harass; unlawful use of electronic communication device; applicability; classification; definitions): B. Any offense committed by use of an electronic communication in violation of this section is deemed to have been committed at either the place where the communications originated or at the place where the communications were received.

ARS § 13-2916 (Use of an electronic communication to terrify, intimidate, threaten or harass; unlawful use of electronic communication device; applicability; classification; definitions): C. This section does not apply to:

ARS § 13-2916 (Use of an electronic communication to terrify, intimidate, threaten or harass; unlawful use of electronic communication device; applicability; classification; definitions): 1. Constitutionally protected speech or activity or to any other activity authorized by law.

ARS § 13-2916 (Use of an electronic communication to terrify, intimidate, threaten or harass; unlawful use of electronic communication device; applicability; classification; definitions): 2. An interactive computer service, as defined in 47 United States Code section 230(f)(2), or to an information service or telecommunications service, as defined in 47 United States Code section 153, for content that is provided by another person.

ARS § 13-2916 (Use of an electronic communication to terrify, intimidate, threaten or harass; unlawful use of electronic communication device; applicability; classification; definitions): D. A person who violates this section is guilty of a class 1 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2916 (Use of an electronic communication to terrify, intimidate, threaten or harass; unlawful use of electronic communication device; applicability; classification; definitions): E. For the purposes of this section:

ARS § 13-2916 (Use of an electronic communication to terrify, intimidate, threaten or harass; unlawful use of electronic communication device; applicability; classification; definitions): 1. "Electronic communication" means a social media post, a wire line, cable, wireless or cellular telephone call, a text message, an instant message or electronic mail.

ARS § 13-2916 (Use of an electronic communication to terrify, intimidate, threaten or harass; unlawful use of electronic communication device; applicability; classification; definitions): 2. "Electronic communication device" includes a telephone, mobile telephone, computer, internet website, internet telephone, hybrid cellular, internet or wireless device, personal digital assistant, video recorder, fax machine or pager.

ARS § 13-2916 (Use of an electronic communication to terrify, intimidate, threaten or harass; unlawful use of electronic communication device; applicability; classification; definitions): 3. "Harassment" means a knowing and wilful course of conduct that is directed at a specific person, that a reasonable person would consider as seriously alarming, seriously disruptive, seriously tormenting or seriously terrorizing the person and that serves no legitimate purpose.

ARS § 13-2916 (Use of an electronic communication to terrify, intimidate, threaten or harass; unlawful use of electronic communication device; applicability; classification; definitions): 4. "Personal identifying information":

ARS § 13-2916 (Use of an electronic communication to terrify, intimidate, threaten or harass; unlawful use of electronic communication device; applicability; classification; definitions): (a) Means information that would allow the identified person to be located, contacted or harassed.

ARS § 13-2916 (Use of an electronic communication to terrify, intimidate, threaten or harass; unlawful use of electronic communication device; applicability; classification; definitions): (b) Includes the person's home address, work address, phone number, email address or other contact information that would allow the identified person to be located, contacted or harassed.

ARS § 13-2916 (Use of an electronic communication to terrify, intimidate, threaten or harass; unlawful use of electronic communication device; applicability; classification; definitions): 5. "Social media post" means a social media communication that is knowingly intended to communicate to a specific person or persons in violation of subsection A of this section.
ARS § 13-2917 (Public nuisance; abatement; classification): A. It is a public nuisance, and is no less a nuisance because the extent of the annoyance or damage inflicted is unequal, for anything:

ARS § 13-2917 (Public nuisance; abatement; classification): 1. To be injurious to health, indecent, offensive to the senses or an obstruction to the free use of property that interferes with the comfortable enjoyment of life or property by an entire community or neighborhood or by a considerable number of persons.

ARS § 13-2917 (Public nuisance; abatement; classification): 2. To unlawfully obstruct the free passage or use, in the customary manner, of any navigable lake, river, bay, stream, canal or basin, or any public park, square, street or highway.

ARS § 13-2917 (Public nuisance; abatement; classification): B. It is a public nuisance for any person to sell, offer to sell, transfer, trade or disseminate any item which is obscene as defined in section 13-3501, within two thousand feet, measured in a straight line, of the nearest boundary line of any of the following:
ARS § 13-2917 (Public nuisance; abatement; classification): 1. Any building used as a private or public elementary or high school.
ARS § 13-2917 (Public nuisance; abatement; classification): 2. Any public park.
ARS § 13-2917 (Public nuisance; abatement; classification): 3. Any residence district as defined in section 28-101.

ARS § 13-2917 (Public nuisance; abatement; classification): C. The county attorney, the attorney general or the city attorney may bring an action in superior court to abate, enjoin and prevent the activity described in subsections A and B of this section.

ARS § 13-2917 (Public nuisance; abatement; classification): D. Any person who knowingly maintains or commits a public nuisance or who knowingly fails or refuses to perform any legal duty relating to the removal of a public nuisance is guilty of a class 2 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2918 (Interference with emergency transmission on citizens' band radio frequency; presumption; definition; classification): A. It is unlawful for a person to recklessly interrupt, impede or otherwise interfere with the transmission of an emergency communication over a citizens' band radio frequency.

ARS § 13-2918 (Interference with emergency transmission on citizens' band radio frequency; presumption; definition; classification): B. A person is presumed to have acted recklessly if he interrupts, impedes or interferes with the transmission of a communication on a channel dedicated to use for emergency communications.

ARS § 13-2918 (Interference with emergency transmission on citizens' band radio frequency; presumption; definition; classification): C. As used in this section "emergency" means a situation in which a person is or is reasonably believed by the person transmitting the communication to be in imminent danger of serious physical injury or in which property is or is reasonably believed by the person transmitting the communication to be in imminent danger of damage or destruction.

ARS § 13-2918 (Interference with emergency transmission on citizens' band radio frequency; presumption; definition; classification): D. A person who violates this section is guilty of a class 1 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2919 (Automated telephone solicitation; violation; classification): A. A person shall not use an automated system for the selection and dialing of telephone numbers and the playing of a recorded message or sending a text message for the purpose of soliciting persons to purchase goods or services or requesting survey information if the results are to be used directly for the purpose of soliciting persons to purchase goods or services.
ARS § 13-2919 (Automated telephone solicitation; violation; classification): B. This section does not apply if a recorded message or text message is received under any of the following circumstances:
ARS § 13-2919 (Automated telephone solicitation; violation; classification): 1. With prior express invitation or permission by the recipient.
ARS § 13-2919 (Automated telephone solicitation; violation; classification): 2. By a recipient who has an existing business relationship with the sender.
ARS § 13-2919 (Automated telephone solicitation; violation; classification): C. A person who violates this section is guilty of a class 2 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2920 (Advertisements and required preamble message for telephone information services; telecommunications corporation compensation; definitions; classification): A. An information access telephone service provider shall not provide or sponsor an advertisement, publication or other communication regarding information access telephone service that does not clearly and conspicuously display the price for each call or for each minute of the call or provide or sponsor a television or radio advertisement that does not include a clearly audible voice announcement of the price for each call or for each minute of the call.

ARS § 13-2920 (Advertisements and required preamble message for telephone information services; telecommunications corporation compensation; definitions; classification): B. Information access telephone service providers shall begin each information access telephone service call with a clear statement, without charge, of whether the call is billed on a per minute or a per call basis and the price for the call or for each minute of the call.

ARS § 13-2920 (Advertisements and required preamble message for telephone information services; telecommunications corporation compensation; definitions; classification): C. Information access telephone service providers shall compensate any telecommunications corporation transporting the provider's service for all charges associated with blocking information access telephone services, and shall make arrangements with the telecommunications corporation for a one time adjustment per residential customer account for an information access telephone service charge if the adjustments involve calls made by minors without authorization or involve claims of fraud, theft or misrepresentation. An adjustment pursuant to this subsection, except for billing and transport charges, shall be charged to the information access telephone service provider who shall not attempt private collection of any adjustments to customers' accounts made by a telecommunications corporation.

ARS § 13-2920 (Advertisements and required preamble message for telephone information services; telecommunications corporation compensation; definitions; classification): D. An information access telephone service provider shall not provide an information access telephone service which describes or depicts, directly or indirectly, sexual conduct or activity or which contains sexually suggestive content unless access to such service is restricted to persons eighteen years of age or older and requires that the service is provided by subscription through the information access telephone service provider.

ARS § 13-2920 (Advertisements and required preamble message for telephone information services; telecommunications corporation compensation; definitions; classification): E. An information access telephone service provider shall not provide recorded announcements or live programs which forward or refer callers to telephone numbers which are not 976 service or 676 service for the purpose of the type of services provided by 976 service or 676 service.
ARS § 13-2920 (Advertisements and required preamble message for telephone information services; telecommunications corporation compensation; definitions; classification): F. In this section:

ARS § 13-2920 (Advertisements and required preamble message for telephone information services; telecommunications corporation compensation; definitions; classification): 1. "Information access telephone service" means telephone service and facilities which provide access to a provider-sponsored prerecorded or live announcement or program and which is commonly referred to as "976 service" or "676 service".

ARS § 13-2920 (Advertisements and required preamble message for telephone information services; telecommunications corporation compensation; definitions; classification): 2. "Provider" means a person, partnership, corporation or organization that contracts with a telecommunications corporation to transport telephone calls, bill customers or collect charges for a prerecorded or live announcement or program.

ARS § 13-2920 (Advertisements and required preamble message for telephone information services; telecommunications corporation compensation; definitions; classification): 3. "Adjustment" means a waiver of all unpaid charges incurred by the residential customer for information access telephone services up to the time the customer contacts the telecommunications corporation and requests the adjustment.

ARS § 13-2920 (Advertisements and required preamble message for telephone information services; telecommunications corporation compensation; definitions; classification): G. A person who violates this section is guilty of a class 3 misdemeanor.

ARS § 13-2921 (Harassment; classification; definition): A. A person commits harassment if the person knowingly and repeatedly commits an act or acts that harass another person or the person knowingly commits any one of the following acts in a manner that harasses:
ARS § 13-2921 (Harassment; classification; definition): 1. Contacts or causes a communication with another person by verbal, electronic, mechanical, telegraphic, telephonic or written means.
ARS § 13-2921 (Harassment; classification; definition): 2. Continues to follow another person in or about a public place after being asked by that person to desist.
ARS § 13-2921 (Harassment; classification; definition): 3. Surveils or causes a person to surveil another person.
ARS § 13-2921 (Harassment; classification; definition): 4. Makes a false report to a law enforcement, credit or social service agency against another person.
ARS § 13-2921 (Harassment; classification; definition): 5. Interferes with the delivery of any public or regulated utility to another person.

ARS § 13-2921 (Harassment; classification; definition): B. A person commits harassment against a public officer or employee if the person, with intent to harass, files a nonconsensual lien against any public officer or employee that is not accompanied by an order or a judgment from a court of competent jurisdiction authorizing the filing of the lien or is not issued by a governmental entity or political subdivision or agency pursuant to its statutory authority, a validly licensed utility or water delivery company, a mechanics' lien claimant or an entity created under covenants, conditions, restrictions or declarations affecting real property.
ARS § 13-2921 (Harassment; classification; definition): C. Harassment under subsection A is a class 1 misdemeanor. Harassment under subsection B is a class 5 felony.
ARS § 13-2921 (Harassment; classification; definition): D. This section does not apply to any of the following:
ARS § 13-2921 (Harassment; classification; definition): 1. A lawful demonstration, assembly or picketing.

ARS § 13-2921 (Harassment; classification; definition): 2. A professional investigator or peace officer who is licensed by this state and who is acting within the scope of the investigator's or officer's duties in connection with any criminal or civil investigation.

ARS § 13-2921 (Harassment; classification; definition): 3. A certified and duly authorized process server who is acting within the scope of the process server's duties in connection with any judicial or administrative action or proceeding.

ARS § 13-2921 (Harassment; classification; definition): E. For the purposes of this section, "harass" means conduct that is directed at a specific person and that would cause a reasonable person to be seriously alarmed, annoyed, humiliated or mentally distressed and the conduct in fact seriously alarms, annoys, humiliates or mentally distresses the person.

ARS § 13-2921.01 (Aggravated harassment; classification; definition): A. A person commits aggravated harassment if the person commits harassment as provided in section 13-2921 and, at the time of the offense, any of the following applies:

ARS § 13-2921.01 (Aggravated harassment; classification; definition): 1. A court has issued any of the following orders in favor of the victim of harassment, the order was served on the person and the order was valid at the time of the offense:
ARS § 13-2921.01 (Aggravated harassment; classification; definition): (a) An order of protection issued pursuant to section 13-3602.
ARS § 13-2921.01 (Aggravated harassment; classification; definition): (b) An injunction against harassment issued pursuant to section 12-1809.
ARS § 13-2921.01 (Aggravated harassment; classification; definition): (c) Any other criminal-related injunction issued under the laws of this state.

ARS § 13-2921.01 (Aggravated harassment; classification; definition): 2. A court has issued an order of protection on an emergency basis pursuant to section 13-3624 against the person in favor of the victim of harassment and the order was still in effect on the date of the offense.
ARS § 13-2921.01 (Aggravated harassment; classification; definition): 3. The person has previously been convicted of an offense included in section 13-3601 committed against the victim of harassment.

ARS § 13-2921.01 (Aggravated harassment; classification; definition): 4. A court has imposed a condition of release on the person that prohibits any contact with the victim of harassment and the court order was still in effect on the date of the offense.

ARS § 13-2921.01 (Aggravated harassment; classification; definition): B. A person who violates subsection A, paragraph 1, 2 or 4 of this section is guilty of a class 6 felony. A person who commits a second or subsequent violation of subsection A, paragraph 1, 2 or 4 of this section is guilty of a class 5 felony. A person who violates subsection A, paragraph 3 of this section is guilty of a class 5 felony.

ARS § 13-2921.01 (Aggravated harassment; classification; definition): C. For the purposes of this section, "convicted" means a person who was convicted of an offense included in section 13-3601 or who was adjudicated delinquent for conduct that would constitute a historical prior felony conviction if the juvenile had been tried as an adult for an offense included in section 13-3601.

ARS § 13-2922 (Interference with transmissions on public safety land mobile radio frequencies; classification; definitions): A. It is unlawful for a person to recklessly interrupt, impede or otherwise directly interfere with emergency communications over a public safety land mobile radio frequency communications network or system created for emergency communications.

ARS § 13-2922 (Interference with transmissions on public safety land mobile radio frequencies; classification; definitions): B. It is unlawful for a person to recklessly interrupt, impede or otherwise interfere with the transmission of a nonemergency communication over a public safety land mobile radio frequency that is dedicated to the dispatch of police, fire or emergency medical response personnel to the scene of an emergency or dedicated to use for emergency communications.

ARS § 13-2922 (Interference with transmissions on public safety land mobile radio frequencies; classification; definitions): C. A person who violates subsection A is guilty of a class 6 felony. A person who violates subsection B is guilty of a class 1 misdemeanor.
ARS § 13-2922 (Interference with transmissions on public safety land mobile radio frequencies; classification; definitions): D. As used in this section:

ARS § 13-2922 (Interference with transmissions on public safety land mobile radio frequencies; classification; definitions): 1. "Emergency" means a situation in which a person is or is reasonably believed by the person transmitting the communication to be in imminent danger of serious physical injury or in which property is or is reasonably believed by the person transmitting the communication to be in imminent danger of damage or destruction.

ARS § 13-2922 (Interference with transmissions on public safety land mobile radio frequencies; classification; definitions): 2. "Public safety land mobile radio frequency" means a frequency prescribed in 47 Code of Federal Regulations part 90, subpart B and part 97, subpart A.

ARS § 13-2922 (Interference with transmissions on public safety land mobile radio frequencies; classification; definitions): 3. "Public safety land mobile radio frequency communications network or system" means those radio services and emergency communications systems that are prescribed in 47 Code of Federal Regulations part 90, subpart B and part 97, subpart A.

ARS § 13-2923 (Stalking; classification; exceptions; definitions): A. A person commits stalking if the person intentionally or knowingly engages in a course of conduct that is directed toward another person and if that conduct causes the victim to:
ARS § 13-2923 (Stalking; classification; exceptions; definitions): 1. Suffer emotional distress or reasonably fear that either:
ARS § 13-2923 (Stalking; classification; exceptions; definitions): (a) The victim's property will be damaged or destroyed.
ARS § 13-2923 (Stalking; classification; exceptions; definitions): (b) Any of the following will be physically injured:
ARS § 13-2923 (Stalking; classification; exceptions; definitions): (i) The victim.
ARS § 13-2923 (Stalking; classification; exceptions; definitions): (ii) The victim's family member, domestic animal or livestock.
ARS § 13-2923 (Stalking; classification; exceptions; definitions): (iii) A person with whom the victim has or has previously had a romantic or sexual relationship.
