ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): 18. "Know" means to have actual knowledge.
ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): 19. "Minor" means an individual who is under eighteen years of age.

ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): 20. "Nontransplant anatomical donation organization" means a tissue bank or other organization that facilitates nontransplant anatomical donations, including facilitation through referrals, obtaining informed consent or authorization and assessing donor acceptability and through the acquisition, traceability, transporting, preparation, packaging, labeling, storage, release, evaluating intended use, distribution and final disposition of nontransplant anatomical donations.

ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): 21. "Organ procurement organization" means a qualified organ procurement organization under 42 United States Code section 273 that is currently certified or recertified in accordance with that federal law.
ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): 22. "Parent" means a parent whose parental rights have not been terminated.
ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): 23. "Part" means an organ, eye or tissue of a human being.  Part does not include the whole body.

ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): 24. "Person" means an individual, corporation, business trust, estate, trust, partnership, limited liability company, association, joint venture, public corporation, government or governmental subdivision, agency or instrumentality, or any other legal or commercial entity.
ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): 25. "Physician" means an individual who is licensed as a physician pursuant to title 32, chapter 13 or 17.
ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): 26. "Principal" means a person who is the subject of a health care power of attorney.
ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): 27. "Procurement organization" means any of the following:
ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): (a) An organ procurement organization.
ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): (b) A tissue bank.
ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): (c) An eye bank.

ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): (d) A storage facility that is licensed, accredited or approved under federal law or the laws of any state to engage in the recovery, screening, testing, processing or storage of human bodies or parts.
ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): (e) A nontransplant anatomical donation organization.

ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): 28. "Prospective donor" means an individual who is dead or near death and who has been determined by a procurement organization to have a part that could be medically suitable for transplantation, therapy, research or education.  Prospective donor does not include an individual who has made a refusal.

ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): 29. "Reasonably available" means able to be contacted by a procurement organization without undue effort and willing and able to act in a timely manner consistent with existing medical criteria necessary for the making of an anatomical gift.
ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): 30. "Recipient" means an individual into whose body a decedent's part has been or is intended to be transplanted.
ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): 31. "Record" means information that is inscribed on a tangible medium or that is stored in an electronic or other medium and is retrievable in perceivable form.

ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): 32. "Refusal" means a record created pursuant to section 36-846 that expressly states an intent to bar other persons from making an anatomical gift of an individual's body or part.
ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): 33. "Sign", with respect to the present intent to authenticate or adopt a record, means either:
ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): (a) To execute or adopt a tangible symbol.
ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): (b) To attach to or logically associate with the record an electronic symbol, sound or process.

ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): 34. "State" means a state of the United States, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, the United States Virgin Islands or any territory or insular possession subject to the jurisdiction of the United States.

ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): 35. "Technician" means an individual who is determined to be qualified to remove or process parts by an appropriate organization that is licensed or regulated under federal or state law or is accredited by a nationally recognized accrediting agency. Technician includes an enucleator.

ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): 36. "Tissue" means all or a portion of the human body other than blood, an organ or an eye unless the blood, organ or eye is donated for the purpose of research or education.

ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): 37. "Tissue bank" means a person that is licensed or regulated under federal or state law or is accredited as a tissue bank by a nationally recognized accrediting agency to engage in the recovery, screening, testing, processing, storage or distribution of tissue.
ARS § 36-841 (Definitions): 38. "Transplant hospital" means a hospital that furnishes organ transplants and other medical and surgical specialty services required for the care of transplant patients.
ARS § 36-842 (Applicability): This article applies to an anatomical gift or amendment to, revocation of or refusal to make an anatomical gift, whenever made.

ARS § 36-843 (Who may make an anatomical gift before donor's death): Subject to the requirements of section 36-847, an anatomical gift may be made during the life of the donor for the purpose of transplantation, therapy, research or education in the manner provided in section 36-844 by:
ARS § 36-843 (Who may make an anatomical gift before donor's death): 1. The donor, if the donor is an adult or is a minor who is either:
ARS § 36-843 (Who may make an anatomical gift before donor's death): (a) Emancipated.

ARS § 36-843 (Who may make an anatomical gift before donor's death): (b) Authorized under state law to apply for a driver license because the donor is at least the youngest age at which an individual may apply for any type of driver license.

ARS § 36-843 (Who may make an anatomical gift before donor's death): 2. An agent of the donor, unless the power of attorney for health care or other record prohibits the agent from making an anatomical gift.
ARS § 36-843 (Who may make an anatomical gift before donor's death): 3. If the donor is an unemancipated minor, a parent of the donor.
ARS § 36-843 (Who may make an anatomical gift before donor's death): 4. The donor's guardian.
ARS § 36-844 (Manner of making anatomical gift before donor's death): A. A donor may make an anatomical gift:
ARS § 36-844 (Manner of making anatomical gift before donor's death): 1. By registering to be a donor on the donor registry established by section 36-858.
ARS § 36-844 (Manner of making anatomical gift before donor's death): 2. In a will.

ARS § 36-844 (Manner of making anatomical gift before donor's death): 3. During a terminal illness or injury of the donor by any form of communication that is addressed to at least two adults, at least one of whom is a disinterested witness.
ARS § 36-844 (Manner of making anatomical gift before donor's death): 4. As provided in subsection B of this section.

ARS § 36-844 (Manner of making anatomical gift before donor's death): B. A donor or other person authorized to make an anatomical gift pursuant to section 36-843 may make a gift by a donor card or other record signed by the donor or other person making the gift or by authorizing that a statement or symbol indicating that the donor has made an anatomical gift be included on a donor registry.  If the donor or other person is physically unable to sign a record, the record may be signed by another individual at the direction of the donor or the other person and must:

ARS § 36-844 (Manner of making anatomical gift before donor's death): 1. Be witnessed by at least two adults, at least one of whom is a disinterested witness, who have signed at the request of the donor or the other person.
ARS § 36-844 (Manner of making anatomical gift before donor's death): 2. State that it has been signed and witnessed as provided in paragraph 1 of this subsection.

ARS § 36-844 (Manner of making anatomical gift before donor's death): C. Revocation, suspension, expiration or cancellation of a driver license or an identification card on which an anatomical gift is indicated does not invalidate the gift.

ARS § 36-844 (Manner of making anatomical gift before donor's death): D. An anatomical gift made by will takes effect on the donor's death whether or not the will is probated.  Invalidation of the will after the donor's death does not invalidate the gift.

ARS § 36-845 (Amending or revoking anatomical gift before donor's death): A. Subject to the requirements of section 36-847, a donor or other person authorized to make an anatomical gift pursuant to section 36-843 may amend or revoke an anatomical gift by:
ARS § 36-845 (Amending or revoking anatomical gift before donor's death): 1. A record signed by either:
ARS § 36-845 (Amending or revoking anatomical gift before donor's death): (a) The donor.
ARS § 36-845 (Amending or revoking anatomical gift before donor's death): (b) The other person.

ARS § 36-845 (Amending or revoking anatomical gift before donor's death): (c) Subject to the requirements of subsection B of this section, another individual acting at the direction of the donor or the other person if the donor or other person is physically unable to sign.

ARS § 36-845 (Amending or revoking anatomical gift before donor's death): 2. A later-executed document of gift that amends or revokes a previous anatomical gift or portion of an anatomical gift, either expressly or by inconsistency.
ARS § 36-845 (Amending or revoking anatomical gift before donor's death): B. A record signed pursuant to subsection A, paragraph 1, subdivision (c) must:

ARS § 36-845 (Amending or revoking anatomical gift before donor's death): 1. Be witnessed by at least two adults, at least one of whom is a disinterested witness, who have signed at the request of the donor or the other person.
ARS § 36-845 (Amending or revoking anatomical gift before donor's death): 2. State that it has been signed and witnessed as prescribed in paragraph 1 of this subsection.

ARS § 36-845 (Amending or revoking anatomical gift before donor's death): C. Subject to the requirements of section 36-847, a donor or other person authorized to make an anatomical gift pursuant to section 36-843 may revoke an anatomical gift by the destruction or cancellation of the document of gift, or the portion of the document of gift used to make the gift, with the intent to revoke the gift.

ARS § 36-845 (Amending or revoking anatomical gift before donor's death): D. A donor may amend or revoke an anatomical gift that was not made in a will by any form of communication during a terminal illness or injury that is addressed to at least two adults, at least one of whom is a disinterested witness.

ARS § 36-845 (Amending or revoking anatomical gift before donor's death): E. A donor who makes an anatomical gift in a will may amend or revoke the gift in the manner provided for amendment or revocation of wills or as prescribed in subsection A of this section.
ARS § 36-846 (Refusal to make anatomical gift; effect of refusal): A. An individual may refuse to make an anatomical gift of the individual's body or part by:
ARS § 36-846 (Refusal to make anatomical gift; effect of refusal): 1. A record signed by either:
ARS § 36-846 (Refusal to make anatomical gift; effect of refusal): (a) The individual.

ARS § 36-846 (Refusal to make anatomical gift; effect of refusal): (b) Subject to the requirements of subsection B of this section, another individual acting at the direction of the individual if the individual is physically unable to sign.
ARS § 36-846 (Refusal to make anatomical gift; effect of refusal): 2. The individual's will, whether or not the will is admitted to probate or invalidated after the individual's death.

ARS § 36-846 (Refusal to make anatomical gift; effect of refusal): 3. Any form of communication made by the individual during the individual's terminal illness or injury that is addressed to at least two adults, at least one of whom is a disinterested witness.
ARS § 36-846 (Refusal to make anatomical gift; effect of refusal): B. A record signed pursuant to subsection A, paragraph 1, subdivision (b) of this section must:

ARS § 36-846 (Refusal to make anatomical gift; effect of refusal): 1. Be witnessed by at least two adults, at least one of whom is a disinterested witness, who have signed at the request of the individual.
ARS § 36-846 (Refusal to make anatomical gift; effect of refusal): 2. State that it has been signed and witnessed as prescribed in paragraph 1 of this subsection.
ARS § 36-846 (Refusal to make anatomical gift; effect of refusal): C. An individual who has made a refusal may amend or revoke the refusal:
ARS § 36-846 (Refusal to make anatomical gift; effect of refusal): 1. In the manner prescribed in subsection A of this section for making a refusal.
ARS § 36-846 (Refusal to make anatomical gift; effect of refusal): 2. By subsequently making an anatomical gift pursuant to section 36-844 that is inconsistent with the refusal.

ARS § 36-846 (Refusal to make anatomical gift; effect of refusal): 3. By destroying or canceling the record evidencing the refusal, or the portion of the record used to make the refusal, with the intent to revoke the refusal.

ARS § 36-846 (Refusal to make anatomical gift; effect of refusal): D. Except as otherwise prescribed in section 36-847, subsection H, in the absence of an express, contrary indication by the individual set forth in the refusal, an individual's unrevoked refusal to make an anatomical gift of the individual's body or part bars all other persons from making an anatomical gift of the individual's body or part.

ARS § 36-847 (Preclusive effect of anatomical gift, amendment or revocation): A. Except as otherwise prescribed in subsections G and H of this section and subject to the requirements of subsection F of this section, in the absence of an express, contrary indication by the donor, a person other than the donor is barred from making, amending or revoking an anatomical gift if the donor made an anatomical gift pursuant to section 36-844 or an amendment to an anatomical gift pursuant to section 36-845.

ARS § 36-847 (Preclusive effect of anatomical gift, amendment or revocation): B. A donor's revocation of an anatomical gift pursuant to section 36-845 is not a refusal and does not bar another person specified in section 36-843 or 36-848 from making an anatomical gift pursuant to section 36-844 or 36-849.

ARS § 36-847 (Preclusive effect of anatomical gift, amendment or revocation): C. If a person other than the donor makes an unrevoked anatomical gift pursuant to section 36-844 or an amendment to an anatomical gift pursuant to section 36-845, another person may not make, amend or revoke the gift pursuant to section 36-849.

ARS § 36-847 (Preclusive effect of anatomical gift, amendment or revocation): D. A revocation of an anatomical gift pursuant to section 36-845 by a person other than the donor does not bar another person from making an anatomical gift pursuant to section 36-844 or 36-849.

ARS § 36-847 (Preclusive effect of anatomical gift, amendment or revocation): E. In the absence of an express contrary indication by the donor or other person authorized to make an anatomical gift pursuant to section 36-843, an anatomical gift of a part is neither a refusal to give another part nor a limitation on the making of an anatomical gift of another part at a later time by the donor or another person.

ARS § 36-847 (Preclusive effect of anatomical gift, amendment or revocation): F. In the absence of an express, contrary indication by the donor or other person authorized to make an anatomical gift pursuant to section 36-843, an anatomical gift of a part for one or more of the purposes described in section 36-843 is not a limitation on the making of an anatomical gift of the part for any of the other purposes by the donor or any other person pursuant to section 36-844 or 36-849.

ARS § 36-847 (Preclusive effect of anatomical gift, amendment or revocation): G. If a donor who is an unemancipated minor dies, a parent of the donor who is reasonably available may revoke or amend an anatomical gift.

ARS § 36-847 (Preclusive effect of anatomical gift, amendment or revocation): H. If an unemancipated minor who signed a refusal dies, a parent of the minor who is reasonably available may revoke the minor's refusal.

ARS § 36-848 (Who may make anatomical gift of decedent's body or part): A. Subject to the requirements of subsections B and C of this section, and unless barred pursuant to section 36-846 or 36-847, an anatomical gift for transplantation, therapy, research or education may be made by any member of the following classes of persons who is reasonably available, in the order of priority listed:

ARS § 36-848 (Who may make anatomical gift of decedent's body or part): 1. An agent of the decedent at the time of death who could have made an anatomical gift pursuant to section 36-843 immediately before the decedent's death.
ARS § 36-848 (Who may make anatomical gift of decedent's body or part): 2. The decedent's spouse.
ARS § 36-848 (Who may make anatomical gift of decedent's body or part): 3. The decedent's adult children.
ARS § 36-848 (Who may make anatomical gift of decedent's body or part): 4. The decedent's parents.

ARS § 36-848 (Who may make anatomical gift of decedent's body or part): 5. If the decedent is unmarried, the decedent's domestic partner, if another person had not assumed financial responsibility for the decedent.
ARS § 36-848 (Who may make anatomical gift of decedent's body or part): 6. The decedent's adult siblings.
ARS § 36-848 (Who may make anatomical gift of decedent's body or part): 7. The decedent's adult grandchildren.
ARS § 36-848 (Who may make anatomical gift of decedent's body or part): 8. The decedent's grandparents.
ARS § 36-848 (Who may make anatomical gift of decedent's body or part): 9. An adult who exhibited special care and concern for the decedent.
ARS § 36-848 (Who may make anatomical gift of decedent's body or part): 10. The persons who were acting as the guardians of the person of the decedent at the time of death.
ARS § 36-848 (Who may make anatomical gift of decedent's body or part): 11. Any other person who has the authority to dispose of the decedent's body.

ARS § 36-848 (Who may make anatomical gift of decedent's body or part): B. If there is more than one member of a class that is listed in subsection A, paragraph 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 or 10 of this section who is entitled to make an anatomical gift, an anatomical gift may be made by a member of the class unless that member or a person to which the gift may pass pursuant to section 36-850 knows of an objection by another member of the class.  If an objection is known, the gift may be made only by a majority of the members of the class who are reasonably available.

ARS § 36-848 (Who may make anatomical gift of decedent's body or part): C. A person may not make an anatomical gift if, at the time of the decedent's death, a person in a prior class pursuant to subsection A of this section is reasonably available to make or to object to the making of an anatomical gift.

ARS § 36-848 (Who may make anatomical gift of decedent's body or part): D. If the decedent's body is not within the custody of the county medical examiner, the county health officer may release and permit the removal of any part from the body in the county health officer's custody for transplantation, therapy, education or research if the requirements of section 36-860, subsection A, are met.

ARS § 36-849 (Manner of making, amending or revoking anatomical gift of decedent's body or part): A. A person who is authorized to make an anatomical gift pursuant to section 36-848 may make an anatomical gift by a document of gift signed by the person making the gift or by that person's oral communication that is electronically recorded or that is contemporaneously reduced to a record and that is signed by the individual receiving the oral communication.

ARS § 36-849 (Manner of making, amending or revoking anatomical gift of decedent's body or part): B. Subject to the requirements of subsection C of this section, an anatomical gift by a person who is authorized pursuant to section 36-848 may be amended or revoked orally or in a record by any member of a prior class who is reasonably available.  If more than one member of the prior class is reasonably available, the gift made by a person authorized pursuant to section 36-848 may be either:
ARS § 36-849 (Manner of making, amending or revoking anatomical gift of decedent's body or part): 1. Amended only if a majority of the reasonably available members agree to the amending of the gift.

ARS § 36-849 (Manner of making, amending or revoking anatomical gift of decedent's body or part): 2. Revoked only if a majority of the reasonably available members agree to the revoking of the gift or if they are equally divided as to whether to revoke the gift.

ARS § 36-849 (Manner of making, amending or revoking anatomical gift of decedent's body or part): C. A revocation pursuant to subsection B of this section is effective only if, before an incision has been made to remove a part from the donor's body or before invasive procedures have begun to prepare the recipient, the procurement organization, transplant hospital, physician or technician knows of the revocation.
ARS § 36-850 (Persons who may receive anatomical gifts; purpose of anatomical gift): A. An anatomical gift may be made to the following named in the document of gift:
ARS § 36-850 (Persons who may receive anatomical gifts; purpose of anatomical gift): 1. An organ procurement organization.

ARS § 36-850 (Persons who may receive anatomical gifts; purpose of anatomical gift): 2. A hospital, accredited medical school, dental school, college, university, procurement organization or any other appropriate person, for research or education.

ARS § 36-850 (Persons who may receive anatomical gifts; purpose of anatomical gift): 3. A search and rescue unit established or recognized by any federal, state, county or local governmental entity to train search and rescue canines.

ARS § 36-850 (Persons who may receive anatomical gifts; purpose of anatomical gift): 4. Subject to the requirements of subsection B of this section, an individual designated by the person making the anatomical gift if the individual is the recipient of the part.
ARS § 36-850 (Persons who may receive anatomical gifts; purpose of anatomical gift): 5. An eye bank or a tissue bank.

ARS § 36-850 (Persons who may receive anatomical gifts; purpose of anatomical gift): B. If an anatomical gift to an individual pursuant to subsection A, paragraph 4 of this section cannot be transplanted into the individual, the part passes pursuant to subsection G of this section in the absence of an express contrary indication by the person making the anatomical gift.

ARS § 36-850 (Persons who may receive anatomical gifts; purpose of anatomical gift): C. If an anatomical gift of one or more specific parts or of all parts is made in a document of gift that does not name a person described in subsection A of this section but that identifies the purpose for which an anatomical gift may be used, the gift passes:

ARS § 36-850 (Persons who may receive anatomical gifts; purpose of anatomical gift): 1. To the appropriate eye bank if the part is an eye and the gift is for the purpose of transplantation or therapy.

ARS § 36-850 (Persons who may receive anatomical gifts; purpose of anatomical gift): 2. To the appropriate tissue bank if the part is tissue and the gift is for the purpose of transplantation or therapy.

ARS § 36-850 (Persons who may receive anatomical gifts; purpose of anatomical gift): 3. To the organ procurement organization as custodian of the organ if the part is an organ and the gift is for the purpose of transplantation or therapy.

ARS § 36-850 (Persons who may receive anatomical gifts; purpose of anatomical gift): 4. To the appropriate procurement organization if the part is an organ, an eye or tissue and the gift is for the purpose of research or education.

ARS § 36-850 (Persons who may receive anatomical gifts; purpose of anatomical gift): 5. To the sheriff of the county in which the gift was made, who may transfer the gift to any canine search and rescue unit established or recognized by any federal, state, county or local governmental entity, and the gift is for the purpose of training search and rescue canines.

ARS § 36-850 (Persons who may receive anatomical gifts; purpose of anatomical gift): D. For the purposes of subsection C of this section, if there is more than one purpose of an anatomical gift stated in the document of gift but the purposes are not stated in any priority, the gift must be used for transplantation or therapy, if suitable. If the gift cannot be used for transplantation or therapy, the gift may be used for research or education or for training search and rescue canines.

ARS § 36-850 (Persons who may receive anatomical gifts; purpose of anatomical gift): E. If an anatomical gift of one or more specific parts is made in a document of gift that does not name a person described in subsection A of this section and does not identify the purpose of the gift, the gift may be used only for transplantation or therapy and the gift passes pursuant to subsection G of this section.

ARS § 36-850 (Persons who may receive anatomical gifts; purpose of anatomical gift): F. If a document of gift specifies only a general intent to make an anatomical gift by words such as "donor", "organ donor" or "body donor", or by a symbol or statement of similar import, the gift may be used only for transplantation or therapy and the gift passes pursuant to subsection G of this section.
ARS § 36-850 (Persons who may receive anatomical gifts; purpose of anatomical gift): G. For the purposes of subsections B, E and F of this section:
ARS § 36-850 (Persons who may receive anatomical gifts; purpose of anatomical gift): 1. If the part is an eye, the gift passes to the appropriate eye bank.
ARS § 36-850 (Persons who may receive anatomical gifts; purpose of anatomical gift): 2. If the part is tissue, the gift passes to the appropriate tissue bank.
ARS § 36-850 (Persons who may receive anatomical gifts; purpose of anatomical gift): 3. If the part is an organ, the gift passes to the organ procurement organization as custodian of the organ.

ARS § 36-850 (Persons who may receive anatomical gifts; purpose of anatomical gift): H. An anatomical gift of an organ for transplantation or therapy, other than an anatomical gift pursuant to subsection A, paragraph 4 of this section, passes to the organ procurement organization as custodian of the organ.

ARS § 36-850 (Persons who may receive anatomical gifts; purpose of anatomical gift): I. If an anatomical gift does not pass pursuant to subsection A, B, C, D, E, F, G or H of this section or the decedent's body or part is not used for transplantation, therapy, research or education or for training search and rescue canines, custody of the body or part passes to the person who is under an obligation to dispose of the body or part pursuant to section 36-831.

ARS § 36-850 (Persons who may receive anatomical gifts; purpose of anatomical gift): J. A person may not accept an anatomical gift if the person knows that the gift was not effectively made pursuant to section 36-844 or 36-849 or if the person knows that the decedent made a refusal pursuant to section 36-846 that was not revoked. For the purposes of this subsection, if a person knows that an anatomical gift was made in a document of gift, the person is deemed to know of any amendment of the gift, revocation of the gift or refusal to make an anatomical gift in the same document of gift.

ARS § 36-850 (Persons who may receive anatomical gifts; purpose of anatomical gift): K. Except as otherwise provided in subsection A, paragraph 4 of this section, this article does not affect the allocation of organs for transplantation or therapy.

ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): A. A health care provider may not, solely on the basis of an individual's disability, do any of the following:
ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): 1. Determine that the individual is ineligible to receive an organ transplant.

ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): 2. Deny the individual medical or other services related to an organ transplant, including evaluation, surgery, counseling and postoperative treatment.

ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): 3. Refuse to refer the individual to a transplant hospital or other related specialist for evaluation or receipt of an organ transplant.

ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): 4. Refuse to place the individual on an organ transplant waiting list or place the individual at a position lower in priority on the list than the position the individual would be placed if not for the individual's disability.

ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): 5. Decline insurance coverage for the individual for any procedure associated with the receipt of an organ transplant or for related services if the procedure or services would be covered under such insurance for the individual if not for the individual's disability.

ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): B. Notwithstanding subsection A of this section, a health care provider may consider an individual's disability when making a treatment recommendation or decision solely to the extent that a physician, following an individualized evaluation of the potential transplant recipient, determines that the disability is medically significant to the organ transplant. This subsection does not require a referral or recommendation for, or the performance of, a medically inappropriate organ transplant.

ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): C. A health care provider may not consider an individual's inability to independently comply with posttransplant medical requirements as medically significant for the purposes of subsection B of this section if the individual has a known disability and the necessary support system to assist the individual in reasonably complying with the requirements.

ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): D. A health care facility shall make reasonable modifications in its policies, practices or procedures as necessary to allow individuals with a disability access to organ transplant-related services, including transplant-related counseling, information or treatment, unless the health care facility can demonstrate that making the modifications would fundamentally alter the nature of the services or would impose an undue hardship on the health care facility. Reasonable modifications in policies, practices and procedures may include:

ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): 1. Communicating with persons supporting or assisting with the individual's postsurgical and posttransplant care, including medication.

ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): 2. Considering the support available to the individual in determining whether the individual is able to reasonably comply with posttransplant medical requirements, including support provided by any of the following:
ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): (a) Family.
ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): (b) Friends.

ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): (c) Home and community-based services, including home and community-based services funded by any of the following:
ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): (i) Medicaid.
ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): (ii) Medicare.
ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): (iii) A health plan in which the individual is enrolled.
ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): (iv) Any other program or source of funding available to the individual.

ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): E. A health care provider shall make reasonable efforts to comply with the policies, practices and procedures, as applicable, developed by a health care facility under subsection D of this section as necessary to allow an individual with a known disability access to organ transplant-related services, including transplant-related counseling, information or treatment, unless the health care provider can demonstrate that compliance would fundamentally alter the nature of the services or would impose an undue hardship on the health care provider.

ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): F. A health care provider shall make reasonable efforts to provide auxiliary aids and services to an individual with a known disability seeking organ transplant-related services, including organ transplant-related counseling, information or treatment, as necessary to allow the individual access to those services, unless the health care provider can demonstrate that providing the transplant-related services with auxiliary aids and services would fundamentally alter the transplant-related services provided or would impose an undue hardship on the health care provider.

ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): G. A health care provider shall comply with the requirements of the Americans with disabilities act of 1990 (42 United States Code sections 12101 through 12213) to the extent that act applies to the health care provider. This subsection does not require a health care provider to comply with that act if the act does not otherwise require compliance by the health care provider.

ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): H. This section applies to each stage of the organ transplant process and related services to an organ transplant, including all of the following:
ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): 1. Evaluation.
ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): 2. Counseling.
ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): 3. Treatment, including postoperative treatment and care.
ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): 4. Providing information.
ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): 5. Any other service recommended or required by a physician.

ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): I. A violation of this section by a health care provider is grounds for disciplinary action by the regulatory agency or board that issued the license, certificate or other authority to the health care provider.  Before a regulatory agency or board may take disciplinary action against a health care provider for a violation, the applicable regulatory agency or board shall both:

ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): 1. Notify the health care provider of the agency's or board's finding that the health care provider violated or is violating this section or a rule adopted pursuant to this section.

ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): 2. Provide the health care provider with an opportunity to correct the violation without penalty or reprimand.

ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): J. A physician who in good faith determines that an individual's disability is medically significant, as described in subsection B of this section, to the organ transplant does not violate this section.

ARS § 36-850.01 (Organ transplant eligibility; individuals with disabilities; discrimination prohibited): K. A health care provider who in good faith makes a treatment recommendation or decision on the basis of a physician's determination that an individual's disability is medically significant, as described in subsection B of this section, to the organ transplant does not violate this section.

ARS § 36-850.02 (Organ transplant; discrimination; violation; civil action): A. If an individual believes that a health care provider or health care facility has violated or is violating section 36-850.01, the affected individual may commence a civil action for injunctive and other equitable relief against the health care provider or health care facility for the purposes of enforcing compliance with that section. The action may be brought in the superior court in the county where the affected individual resides or resided or was denied the organ transplant or referral.

ARS § 36-850.02 (Organ transplant; discrimination; violation; civil action): B. In an action brought under this section, the court shall give the action priority on its docket and expedited review, and may grant injunctive or other equitable relief, including any of the following:
ARS § 36-850.02 (Organ transplant; discrimination; violation; civil action): 1. Requiring auxiliary aids or services to be made available for a qualified recipient.
ARS § 36-850.02 (Organ transplant; discrimination; violation; civil action): 2. Requiring the modification of a policy, practice or procedure of the health care provider or health care facility.
ARS § 36-850.02 (Organ transplant; discrimination; violation; civil action): 3. Requiring that health care facilities be made readily accessible to and usable by a qualified recipient.

ARS § 36-850.02 (Organ transplant; discrimination; violation; civil action): C. This section does not limit or replace available remedies under the Americans with disabilities act of 1990, as amended (42 United States Code sections 12101 through 12213), or any other applicable law.

ARS § 36-850.02 (Organ transplant; discrimination; violation; civil action): D. This section does not create a right to compensatory or punitive damages against a health care provider or health care facility.
ARS § 36-851 (Delivery of document of gift not required; right to examine): A. A document of gift need not be delivered during the donor's lifetime to be effective.

ARS § 36-851 (Delivery of document of gift not required; right to examine): B. On or after an individual's death, a person in possession of a document of gift or a refusal to make an anatomical gift with respect to the individual shall allow examination and copying of the document of gift or refusal by a person authorized to make or object to the making of an anatomical gift with respect to the individual or by a person to which the gift could pass pursuant to section 36-850.

ARS § 36-851.01 (Procurement organizations; licensure; renewal; fees; penalties; exceptions): A. A person may not act as a procurement organization in this state unless the person is licensed by the department of health services as a procurement organization. The person shall apply in writing to the director of the department on a form specified by the director, shall include all information requested in the application and shall pay the fees prescribed by the director.

ARS § 36-851.01 (Procurement organizations; licensure; renewal; fees; penalties; exceptions): B. The director shall grant a procurement organization license to a person if the organization either is accredited by a nationally recognized accrediting agency that is approved by the department of health services and maintains full accreditation with the accrediting agency or meets the requirements prescribed in section 36-851.03 and the rules adopted by the department.

ARS § 36-851.01 (Procurement organizations; licensure; renewal; fees; penalties; exceptions): C. A license under this section is valid for two years and must be renewed every two years.  A person shall file an application for renewal at least thirty days before the expiration of the current license.

ARS § 36-851.01 (Procurement organizations; licensure; renewal; fees; penalties; exceptions): D. Each procurement organization applying for licensure or license renewal under this section shall pay all applicable fees as prescribed by the director. All fees collected pursuant to this section for the licensure and license renewal of procurement organizations shall be deposited in the health services licensing fund established by section 36-414.

ARS § 36-851.01 (Procurement organizations; licensure; renewal; fees; penalties; exceptions): E. The director may sanction, impose civil penalties on or, pursuant to title 41, chapter 6, article 10, suspend or revoke, in whole or in part, the license of any procurement organization if any person who is an owner, officer, agent or employee of the procurement organization is in or continues to be in violation of this article or the rules of the department of health services adopted pursuant to this article.
ARS § 36-851.01 (Procurement organizations; licensure; renewal; fees; penalties; exceptions): F. This section does not apply to any of the following:

ARS § 36-851.01 (Procurement organizations; licensure; renewal; fees; penalties; exceptions): 1. An organ procurement organization as described by 42 United States Code section 273 that is designated for this state by the secretary of the United States department of health and human services pursuant to 42 United States Code section 1320b-8.

ARS § 36-851.01 (Procurement organizations; licensure; renewal; fees; penalties; exceptions): 2. A procurement organization that is regulated by the United States food and drug administration in connection with the recovery of human tissue intended for transplantation pursuant to 21 Code of Federal Regulations part 1270.
ARS § 36-851.01 (Procurement organizations; licensure; renewal; fees; penalties; exceptions): 3. A procurement organization as defined in section 36-841, paragraph  27, subdivision (d).

ARS § 36-851.01 (Procurement organizations; licensure; renewal; fees; penalties; exceptions): 4. A procurement organization that is affiliated with an accredited educational institution in connection with the education of students enrolled in a degree-granting program for health professionals.

ARS § 36-851.01 (Procurement organizations; licensure; renewal; fees; penalties; exceptions): 5. A procurement organization that recovers anatomical gifts for research or education, including for quality improvement or quality assurance, and that is affiliated with a hospital that is licensed pursuant to chapter 4 of this title.
ARS § 36-851.01 (Procurement organizations; licensure; renewal; fees; penalties; exceptions): 6. A hospital that is licensed pursuant to chapter 4 of this title.
ARS § 36-851.02 (Procurement organizations; deemed status; requirements; inspection): A procurement organization that is licensed pursuant to section 36-851.01 by virtue of its accreditation status:

ARS § 36-851.02 (Procurement organizations; deemed status; requirements; inspection): 1. Is deemed to meet health and safety requirements that are equivalent to those set forth in section 36-851.03 and is not required to meet the requirements prescribed in section 36-851.03 except as specified in paragraph 2 of this section if the procurement organization maintains its accredited status with the accrediting agency.
ARS § 36-851.02 (Procurement organizations; deemed status; requirements; inspection): 2. Shall comply with all of the following as adopted in rule by the department of health services:
ARS § 36-851.02 (Procurement organizations; deemed status; requirements; inspection): (a) The proper use and maintenance of donor consent forms.
ARS § 36-851.02 (Procurement organizations; deemed status; requirements; inspection): (b) The implementation and maintenance of proper identification systems for bodies and disarticulated items.

ARS § 36-851.02 (Procurement organizations; deemed status; requirements; inspection): (c) The implementation and maintenance of protocols and materials for procedures used by the procurement organization to properly screen end users.
ARS § 36-851.02 (Procurement organizations; deemed status; requirements; inspection): (d) The proper documentation and disclosure of the disease status of tissue specimens to end users.
ARS § 36-851.02 (Procurement organizations; deemed status; requirements; inspection): (e) Labeling, packaging, transport and distribution policies and procedures.
ARS § 36-851.02 (Procurement organizations; deemed status; requirements; inspection): (f) Final disposition procedures.

ARS § 36-851.02 (Procurement organizations; deemed status; requirements; inspection): 3. Shall provide a designated area for tissue recovery that does not operate in a funeral establishment for the recovery of whole bodies for medical research and education.

ARS § 36-851.02 (Procurement organizations; deemed status; requirements; inspection): 4. Is subject to inspection by the department of health services at any time with respect to compliance with the requirements of paragraph 2 of this section.

ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): A. Except as provided in section 36-851.02, each procurement organization that is required to be licensed pursuant to section 36-851.01 shall do all of the following:

ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): 1. Designate a medical director who is a physician licensed pursuant to title 32, chapter 13 or 17 and who provides medical guidance to determine donor eligibility.

ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): 2. Employ a director who holds at least a bachelor's degree in a related science from an accredited university and who is responsible for all licensed activities of the organization.
ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): 3. Comply with all of the following as adopted in rule by the department of health services:
ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): (a) The proper use and maintenance of donor consent forms.
ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): (b) The implementation and maintenance of proper identification systems for bodies and disarticulated items.

ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): (c) The implementation and maintenance of protocols and materials for procedures used by the procurement organization to properly screen end users.
ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): (d) The proper documentation and disclosure of the disease status of tissue specimens to end users.
ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): (e) Labeling, packaging, transport and distribution policies and procedures.
ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): (f) Final disposition procedures.
ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): 4. Implement and maintain all of the following:
ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): (a) Standard operating procedures for all licensed functions of the organization.
ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): (b) A safety awareness and blood-borne pathogen training program that complies with state and federal law.
ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): (c) A cleaning program that mitigates potential cross-contamination between donors.
ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): 5. Provide a designated area for tissue recovery that:
ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): (a) Is open to inspection by the department of health services with or without notice.

ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): (b) Does not operate in a funeral establishment for the recovery of whole bodies for medical research and education.
ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): 6. Properly track donors and label tissue by doing both of the following:

ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): (a) Assigning a unique identifying number to each donor and using this number for all tissue from that donor that is recovered and distributed.
ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): (b) Affixing labels with the following information on all nontransplant tissue specimens:
ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): (i) A statement that universal precautions will be used.
ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): (ii) A statement that the specimen is not for transplant or clinical use.
ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): (iii) Any condition or limitation regarding the use of the specimen.
ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): (iv) Contact information for the procurement organization.
ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): 7. Maintain the following records for ten years after the last date of tissue distribution:
ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): (a) A copy or recorded consent of the donation authorization.
ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): (b) A copy of the donor's death certificate and transit permit issued by the state where the death occurred.
ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): (c) A copy of the donor's physical assessment and risk assessment questionnaire.
ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): (d) A copy of the donor's serological results, when applicable.
ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): (e) A copy of all documentation relating to tissue recovery, storage and distribution activities.

ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): B. The department of health services shall adopt rules that follow, as nearly as practicable, the requirements on equivalent subjects specified in subsection A of this section that are set forth in the accreditation requirements of a nationally recognized  accrediting agency that is approved by the department.

ARS § 36-851.03 (Procurement organizations; requirements; records; rules; inspection): C. A procurement organization that is subject to the requirements of this section is subject to inspection by the department of health services at any time to evaluate the compliance by the procurement organization with the requirements of this article and the rules adopted by the department.

ARS § 36-852 (Rights and duties of procurement organizations and others): A. When a hospital refers an individual at or near death to an organ procurement organization, the organization shall make a reasonable search of the records of any donor registry that it knows exists for the geographical area in which the individual resides to determine if the individual has made an anatomical gift.

ARS § 36-852 (Rights and duties of procurement organizations and others): B. A procurement organization must be allowed reasonable access to information in the records of the donor registry to determine if an individual at or near death is a donor.

ARS § 36-852 (Rights and duties of procurement organizations and others): C. When a hospital refers an individual at or near death to an organ procurement organization, the organ procurement organization or the appropriate eye bank or tissue bank may conduct any reasonable examination necessary to ensure the medical suitability of a part that is or could be the subject of an anatomical gift for transplantation, therapy, research or education from a donor or a prospective donor.  During the examination period, measures necessary to ensure the medical suitability of the part may not be withdrawn unless the hospital or procurement organization knows that the individual expressed a contrary intent.

ARS § 36-852 (Rights and duties of procurement organizations and others): D. Unless otherwise prohibited by law, at any time after a donor's death, the person to which a part passes pursuant to section 36-850 may conduct any reasonable examination necessary to ensure the medical suitability of the body or part for its intended purpose.

ARS § 36-852 (Rights and duties of procurement organizations and others): E. Unless otherwise prohibited by law, an examination pursuant to subsection C or D of this section may include an examination of all medical and dental records of the donor or prospective donor.

ARS § 36-852 (Rights and duties of procurement organizations and others): F. On the death of a minor who was a donor or who had signed a refusal, unless a procurement organization knows the minor is emancipated, the appropriate procurement organization shall conduct a reasonable search for the parents of the minor and provide the parents with an opportunity to revoke or amend the anatomical gift or revoke the refusal.

ARS § 36-852 (Rights and duties of procurement organizations and others): G. On referral by a hospital pursuant to subsection A of this section, the appropriate procurement organization must make a reasonable search for any person listed in section 36-848 who has priority to make an anatomical gift on behalf of a prospective donor.  If a procurement organization receives information that an anatomical gift to any other person was made, amended or revoked, it shall promptly advise the other person of all relevant information.

ARS § 36-852 (Rights and duties of procurement organizations and others): H. Subject to the requirements of section 36-850, subsection I and section 36-861, the rights of the person to which a part passes pursuant to section 36-850 are superior to the rights of all others with respect to the part.  The person may accept or reject an anatomical gift in whole or in part.  Subject to the terms of the document of gift and this article, a person who accepts an anatomical gift of an entire body may allow embalming, burial or cremation and use of remains in a funeral service. If the gift is of a part, the person to which the part passes pursuant to section 36-850, on the death of the donor and before embalming, burial or cremation, shall cause the part to be removed without unnecessary mutilation.

ARS § 36-852 (Rights and duties of procurement organizations and others): I. The physician who attends the decedent at death and the physician who determines the time of the decedent's death may not participate in the procedures for removing or transplanting a part from the decedent.

ARS § 36-852 (Rights and duties of procurement organizations and others): J. A physician or technician may remove a donated part from the body of a donor that the physician or technician is qualified to remove.

ARS § 36-853 (Coordination of procurement and use): A. Each hospital in this state shall enter into one or more agreements or affiliations with procurement organizations for coordination of procurement and use of anatomical gifts.

ARS § 36-853 (Coordination of procurement and use): B. If there has been an anatomical gift, the institution where the removal of any donated parts occurs shall notify the funeral director or the person acting in that capacity who first assumes custody of the body about the removal of the body parts.

ARS § 36-854 (Sale or purchase of parts; classification): A. Except as otherwise provided in subsection B, a person who for valuable consideration knowingly purchases or sells a part for transplantation or therapy, if removal of a part from an individual is intended to occur after the individual's death, is guilty of a class 3 felony.

ARS § 36-854 (Sale or purchase of parts; classification): B. This section does not prevent a person from charging a reasonable amount for the removal, processing, preservation, quality control, storage, transportation, implantation or disposal of a part.

ARS § 36-855 (Prohibited acts; classification): A person who, in order to obtain a financial gain, intentionally falsifies, forges, conceals, defaces or obliterates a document of gift, an amendment or revocation of a document of gift or a refusal of gift is guilty of a class 6 felony.

ARS § 36-856 (Immunity): A. A person is not subject to civil liability, criminal prosecution or administrative proceedings for good faith acts or omissions related to procurement of parts in compliance with this article.  All acts and omissions are presumed to be in good faith unless the acts or omissions are done with intent to maliciously cause injury.

ARS § 36-856 (Immunity): B. A person who makes an anatomical gift and the donor's estate are not subject to civil or criminal liability for any injury or damage that results from the making or use of the gift.

ARS § 36-856 (Immunity): C. In determining whether an anatomical gift has been made, amended or revoked pursuant to this article, a person may rely on representations of an individual listed pursuant to section 36-848, subsection A, paragraph 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 or 8 relating to the individual's relationship to the donor or prospective donor unless the person knows that the representation is untrue.
ARS § 36-857 (Choice of law; presumption of validity): A. A document of gift is valid if executed in accordance with:
ARS § 36-857 (Choice of law; presumption of validity): 1. This article.
ARS § 36-857 (Choice of law; presumption of validity): 2. The laws of the state or country where it was executed.

ARS § 36-857 (Choice of law; presumption of validity): 3. The laws of the state or country where the person making the anatomical gift was domiciled, has a place of residence or was a national at the time the document of gift was executed.
ARS § 36-857 (Choice of law; presumption of validity): B. If a document of gift is valid under this section, the laws of this state govern the interpretation of the document of gift.

ARS § 36-857 (Choice of law; presumption of validity): C. A person may presume that a document of gift or amendment of an anatomical gift is valid unless that person knows that it was not validly executed or was revoked.
ARS § 36-858 (Donor registry): A. An organ procurement organization shall establish a donor registry in this state.

ARS § 36-858 (Donor registry): B. The motor vehicle division of the department of transportation shall cooperate with the organ procurement organization that administers a donor registry to transfer to the donor registry all relevant information regarding a donor's making of an anatomical gift.
ARS § 36-858 (Donor registry): C. A donor registry must:

ARS § 36-858 (Donor registry): 1. Allow a donor or other person authorized pursuant to section 36-843 to include on the donor registry a statement or symbol that the anatomical gift was made by the donor.

ARS § 36-858 (Donor registry): 2. Be accessible to a procurement organization to allow it to obtain relevant information on the donor registry to determine, at or near death of the donor or a prospective donor, whether the donor or prospective donor has made an anatomical gift.
ARS § 36-858 (Donor registry): 3. Be accessible seven days a week on a twenty-four hour basis for purposes of paragraphs 1 and 2.

ARS § 36-858 (Donor registry): D. Personally identifiable information on a donor registry about a donor or prospective donor may not be used or disclosed without the express consent of the donor, prospective donor or person who made the anatomical gift for any purpose other than to determine, at or near death of the donor or prospective donor, if the donor or prospective donor has made, amended or revoked an anatomical gift.

ARS § 36-858 (Donor registry): E. This section does not prohibit any person from establishing or maintaining a donor registry that is not established by or under contract with this state.  Any such registry must comply with the requirements of subsections C and D of this section.

ARS § 36-859 (Effect of anatomical gift on health care directive; definitions): A. If the terms of a prospective donor's living will or health care directive and the express or implied terms of an anatomical gift made by the prospective donor, or made by any other person, appear to be in conflict with regard to the administration of measures necessary to ensure the medical suitability of a part for transplantation or therapy, appropriate consultation shall occur to determine the prospective donor's actual or likely intent in resolving that conflict.  Resolution of the conflict shall occur as expeditiously as possible.  If the prospective donor is unable to resolve the conflict, another person authorized by law to make health care decisions on behalf of the prospective donor shall resolve the conflict. Before resolution of the conflict, measures necessary to ensure the medical suitability of the part may not be withheld or withdrawn from the prospective donor if withholding or withdrawing of the measures is not contraindicated by appropriate end of life care.

ARS § 36-859 (Effect of anatomical gift on health care directive; definitions): B. For the purposes of subsection A of this section, appropriate consultation must include the prospective donor's attending physician, the hospital’s ethics committee or, if none, a designated representative of the hospital, and the agent acting under the prospective donor's health care directive or, if none, any other individual authorized by law to make health care decisions on behalf of the prospective donor and may include the appropriate procurement organization and any other person authorized to make an anatomical gift pursuant to section 36-848.  If the appropriate consultation does not resolve the conflict, the agent acting under the prospective donor's health care directive or, if none, any other individual authorized by law to make health care decisions on behalf of the prospective donor, or the majority of such individuals, is empowered to make the final decision of how to proceed.
ARS § 36-859 (Effect of anatomical gift on health care directive; definitions): C. For the purposes of this section:
ARS § 36-859 (Effect of anatomical gift on health care directive; definitions): 1. "Health care decision" means any decision made regarding the health care of the prospective donor.
ARS § 36-859 (Effect of anatomical gift on health care directive; definitions): 2. "Health care directive" has the same meaning prescribed in section 36-3201.
ARS § 36-859 (Effect of anatomical gift on health care directive; definitions): 3. "Living will" has the same meaning prescribed in section 36-3201.

ARS § 36-860 (County medical examiners; authorization): A. The medical examiner or individual legally delegated that authority may release and permit the removal of a part from or all of a body within the custody of that official for transplantation, therapy, research or education pursuant to title 11, chapter 3, article 12 if the part is the subject of an anatomical gift and:
ARS § 36-860 (County medical examiners; authorization): 1. A request has been received from a procurement organization.

ARS § 36-860 (County medical examiners; authorization): 2. The organ procurement organization has made a reasonable effort, taking into account the useful life of the part, to locate and examine the decedent's medical records and, if the decedent has not executed a document of gift or has not refused to make an anatomical gift, inform persons listed in section 36-848, subsection A, of the person's option to make or object to making an anatomical gift.

ARS § 36-860 (County medical examiners; authorization): 3. The official does not know of a refusal by the decedent or an objection by a person having priority to act as listed in section 36-848, subsection A.
ARS § 36-860 (County medical examiners; authorization): 4. The removal will be by a physician, surgeon or trained technician.
ARS § 36-860 (County medical examiners; authorization): 5. The removal will be in accordance with accepted medical standards.
ARS § 36-860 (County medical examiners; authorization): 6. The removal will not interfere with any death investigation.
ARS § 36-860 (County medical examiners; authorization): 7. Cosmetic restoration will be done, if appropriate.

ARS § 36-860 (County medical examiners; authorization): B. An official who releases and permits the removal of a part shall maintain a permanent record of the name of the decedent, the person making the request, the date and purpose of the request, the part requested and the person to whom it was released.

ARS § 36-861 (Medical examiner; release of information): A. The county medical examiner or individual legally delegated that authority shall release the name, contact information and available medical and social history of a decedent whose body is under the jurisdiction of the medical examiner to:

ARS § 36-861 (Medical examiner; release of information): 1. The designated procurement organization, hospital, accredited medical school, dental school, college or university of an anatomical gift executed pursuant to section 36-844.
ARS § 36-861 (Medical examiner; release of information): 2. Any procurement organization under procedures adopted by the medical examiner for coordination of the procurement of anatomical gifts.

ARS § 36-861 (Medical examiner; release of information): B. If the decedent's body or part is medically suitable for transplantation, therapy, research or education, the medical examiner, or individual legally delegated that authority, shall release postmortem examination results to a procurement organization. The procurement organization may make a subsequent disclosure of the postmortem examination results or other information received from the medical examiner only if relevant to transplantation or therapy.

ARS § 36-862 (Uniformity of application and construction): In applying and construing this article, consideration must be given to the need to promote uniformity of the law with respect to its subject matter among states that enact it.

ARS § 36-863 (Relation to electronic signatures in global and national commerce act): This act modifies, limits and supersedes the electronic signatures in global and national commerce act, but does not modify, limit or supersede section 101(a) of that act (15 United States Code section 7001) or authorize electronic delivery of any of the notices described in section 103(b) of that act (15 United States Code section 7003(b)).

ARS § 36-864 (Document of gift; transfer by department of transportation; requirements): Each executed document of gift transferred by the department of transportation to an organ procurement organization is presumed to be a valid document of gift that establishes an anatomical gift for transplantation or therapy if all of the following apply:

ARS § 36-864 (Document of gift; transfer by department of transportation; requirements): 1. The organ procurement organization that maintains an anatomical gift registry established pursuant to this article contacted each person who executed the document of gift before that person's death or incapacity.
ARS § 36-864 (Document of gift; transfer by department of transportation; requirements): 2. The person had not amended or revoked the anatomical gift before death.
ARS § 36-864 (Document of gift; transfer by department of transportation; requirements): 3. The organ procurement organization provided the person with notice of:
ARS § 36-864 (Document of gift; transfer by department of transportation; requirements): (a) The inclusion of the person's name in an anatomical gift registry established pursuant to this article.
ARS § 36-864 (Document of gift; transfer by department of transportation; requirements): (b) The opportunity to amend or revoke the anatomical gift.
ARS § 36-864 (Document of gift; transfer by department of transportation; requirements): (c) Instructions about how to amend or revoke the anatomical gift.
ARS § 36-881 (Definitions): In this article, unless the context otherwise requires:

ARS § 36-881 (Definitions): 1. "Child" means any person through the age of fourteen years.  Child also means a person who is under eighteen years of age if the child has a developmental disability as defined in section 36-551 or has at least one of the disabilities listed in section 15-761, paragraph 2 and requires special education as defined in section 15-761.

ARS § 36-881 (Definitions): 2. "Child care" means the care, supervision and guidance of a child or children, unaccompanied by a parent, guardian or custodian, on a regular basis, for periods of less than twenty-four hours per day, in a place other than the child's or the children's own home or homes.
ARS § 36-881 (Definitions): 3. "Child care facility" means any facility in which child care is regularly provided for compensation for five or more children not related to the proprietor.
ARS § 36-881 (Definitions): 4. "Controlling person" means a person who:
ARS § 36-881 (Definitions): (a) Through ownership, has the power to vote at least ten per cent of the outstanding voting securities.
ARS § 36-881 (Definitions): (b) If the applicant or licensee is a partnership, is the general partner or a limited partner who holds at least ten per cent of the voting rights of the partnership.

ARS § 36-881 (Definitions): (c) If the applicant or licensee is a corporation, an association or a limited liability company, is the president, the chief executive officer, the incorporator, an agent or any person who owns or controls at least ten per cent of the voting securities.
ARS § 36-881 (Definitions): (d) Holds a beneficial interest in ten per cent or more of the liabilities of the applicant or the licensee.
ARS § 36-881 (Definitions): 5. "Department" means the department of health services.
ARS § 36-881 (Definitions): 6. "Director" means the director of the department of health services.

ARS § 36-881 (Definitions): 7. "Person" means an individual, partnership, corporation, limited liability company, association, day nursery, nursery school, day camp, kindergarten, child care agency, school governing board, charter school or child care center that operates a child care facility.

ARS § 36-881 (Definitions): 8. "Substantial compliance" means that the nature or number of violations revealed by any type of inspection or investigation of an applicant for licensure or a licensed child care facility does not pose a direct risk to the life, health or safety of children.

ARS § 36-882 (License; posting; transfer prohibited; fees; provisional license; renewal; exemption from rule making): A. A child care facility shall not receive any child for care, supervision or training unless the facility is licensed by the department of health services.

ARS § 36-882 (License; posting; transfer prohibited; fees; provisional license; renewal; exemption from rule making): B. An application for a license shall be made on a written or electronic form prescribed by the department and shall include:

ARS § 36-882 (License; posting; transfer prohibited; fees; provisional license; renewal; exemption from rule making): 1. Information required by the department for the proper administration of this chapter and rules adopted pursuant to this chapter.
ARS § 36-882 (License; posting; transfer prohibited; fees; provisional license; renewal; exemption from rule making): 2. The name and business or residential address of each controlling person.

ARS § 36-882 (License; posting; transfer prohibited; fees; provisional license; renewal; exemption from rule making): 3. An affirmation by the applicant that no controlling person has been denied a certificate to operate a child care group home or a license to operate a child care facility for the care of children in this state or another state or has had a license to operate a child care facility or a certificate to operate a child care group home revoked for reasons that relate to the endangerment of the health and safety of children.
ARS § 36-882 (License; posting; transfer prohibited; fees; provisional license; renewal; exemption from rule making): C. An application for an initial license shall include:

ARS § 36-882 (License; posting; transfer prohibited; fees; provisional license; renewal; exemption from rule making): 1. The form that is required pursuant to section 36-883.02, subsection C and that is completed by the applicant.

ARS § 36-882 (License; posting; transfer prohibited; fees; provisional license; renewal; exemption from rule making): 2. A copy of a valid fingerprint clearance card issued to the applicant pursuant to section 41-1758.07.

ARS § 36-882 (License; posting; transfer prohibited; fees; provisional license; renewal; exemption from rule making): 3. If the applicant's facility is located within one-fourth mile of any agricultural land, the names and addresses of the owners and lessees of the agricultural land and a copy of the agreement required pursuant to subsection D of this section.

ARS § 36-882 (License; posting; transfer prohibited; fees; provisional license; renewal; exemption from rule making): D. The department shall deny any license that affects agricultural land regulated pursuant to section 3-365, except that the owner of the agricultural land may agree to comply with the buffer zone requirements of section 3-365. If the owner agrees in writing to comply with the buffer zone requirements and records the agreement in the office of the county recorder as a restrictive covenant running with the title to the land, the department may license the child care facility to be located within the affected buffer zone.  The agreement may include any stipulations regarding the child care facility, including conditions for future expansion of the facility and changes in the operational status of the facility that will result in a breach of the agreement. This subsection shall not apply to the issuance or renewal of a license for a child care facility located in the same location for which a child care facility license was previously issued.

ARS § 36-882 (License; posting; transfer prohibited; fees; provisional license; renewal; exemption from rule making): E. On receipt of an application for an initial license, the department shall inspect the applicant's physical space, activities and standards of care.  If the department determines that the applicant and the applicant's facility are in substantial compliance with this chapter and rules adopted pursuant to this chapter and the applicant agrees to carry out a plan acceptable to the department to eliminate any deficiencies, the department shall issue an initial license to the applicant.

ARS § 36-882 (License; posting; transfer prohibited; fees; provisional license; renewal; exemption from rule making): F. Beginning January 1, 2010, subject to the availability of monies, the department may establish a discount program for licensing fees paid by child care facilities, including a public health discount.

ARS § 36-882 (License; posting; transfer prohibited; fees; provisional license; renewal; exemption from rule making): G. The director, by rule, may establish and collect fees for child care facilities and a fee for late filing of applications.  Beginning January 1, 2010, ninety per cent of the fees collected pursuant to this section shall be deposited, pursuant to sections 35-146 and 35-147, in the health services licensing fund established by section 36-414 and ten per cent of the fees collected pursuant to this section shall be deposited, pursuant to sections 35-146 and 35-147, in the state general fund.
ARS § 36-882 (License; posting; transfer prohibited; fees; provisional license; renewal; exemption from rule making): H. Pursuant to available funding, the department shall collect annual fees.

ARS § 36-882 (License; posting; transfer prohibited; fees; provisional license; renewal; exemption from rule making): I. A license is valid from the date of issuance unless it is subsequently revoked or suspended or the licensee does not pay the licensure fee and shall specify the following:
ARS § 36-882 (License; posting; transfer prohibited; fees; provisional license; renewal; exemption from rule making): 1. The name of the applicant.
ARS § 36-882 (License; posting; transfer prohibited; fees; provisional license; renewal; exemption from rule making): 2. The exact address where the applicant will locate the facility.

ARS § 36-882 (License; posting; transfer prohibited; fees; provisional license; renewal; exemption from rule making): 3. The maximum number and age limitations of children that shall be cared for at any one time.
ARS § 36-882 (License; posting; transfer prohibited; fees; provisional license; renewal; exemption from rule making): 4. The classification of services that the facility is licensed to provide.

ARS § 36-882 (License; posting; transfer prohibited; fees; provisional license; renewal; exemption from rule making): J. The department may issue a provisional license, not to exceed six months, to an applicant or a licensed child care facility if:
ARS § 36-882 (License; posting; transfer prohibited; fees; provisional license; renewal; exemption from rule making): 1. The facility changes director.

ARS § 36-882 (License; posting; transfer prohibited; fees; provisional license; renewal; exemption from rule making): 2. The department determines that an applicant for an initial license or a licensed child care facility is not in substantial compliance with this chapter and rules adopted pursuant to this chapter and the immediate interests of children, families and the general public are best served if the child care facility or the applicant is given an opportunity to correct deficiencies.
