ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 12. "Home state" means the member state that is the licensee's primary state of residence.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 13. "Impaired practitioner" means an individual whose professional practice is adversely affected by substance abuse, addiction or another health-related condition.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 14. "Investigative information" means investigative information that a licensing board, after an inquiry or investigation that includes notification and an opportunity for the audiologist or speech-language pathologist to respond, if required by state law, has reason to believe is not groundless and, if proved true, would indicate more than a minor infraction.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 15. "Licensee" means an individual who currently holds an authorization from the state licensing board to practice as an audiologist or speech-language pathologist.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 16. "Member state" means a state that has enacted the compact.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 17. "Privilege to practice" means a legal authorization allowing the practice of audiology or speech-language pathology in a remote state.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 18. "Remote state" means a member state other than the home state where a licensee is exercising or seeking to exercise the compact privilege.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 19. "Rule" means a regulation, principle or directive promulgated by the commission that has the force of law.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 20. "Single-state license" means an audiology or speech-language pathology license issued by a member state that authorizes practice only within the issuing state and does not include a privilege to practice in any other member state.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 21. "Speech-language pathologist" means an individual who is licensed by a state to practice speech-language pathology.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 22. "Speech-language pathology" means the care and services provided by a licensed speech-language pathologist as set forth in the member state's statutes and rules.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 23. "State" means any state, commonwealth, district or territory of the United States that regulates the practice of audiology and speech-language pathology.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 24. "State practice laws" means a member state's laws, rules and regulations that govern the practice of audiology or speech-language pathology, define the scope of audiology or speech-language pathology practice, and create the methods and grounds for imposing discipline.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 25. "Telehealth" means the application of telecommunication technology to deliver audiology or speech-language pathology services at a distance for assessment, intervention or consultation.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): SECTION 3. STATE PARTICIPATION IN THE COMPACT

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): A. A license issued to an audiologist or speech-language pathologist by a home state to a resident in that state shall be recognized by each member state as authorizing the audiologist or speech-language pathologist to practice audiology or speech-language pathology, under a privilege to practice, in each member state.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): B. A state must implement or use procedures for considering the criminal history records of applicants for initial privilege to practice. These procedures shall include the submission of fingerprints or other biometric-based information by applicants for the purpose of obtaining an applicant's criminal history record information from the federal bureau of investigation and the agency responsible for retaining that state's criminal records, as follows:

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 1. A member state must fully implement a criminal background check requirement, within a time frame established by rule, by receiving the results of the federal bureau of investigation record search on criminal background checks and use the results in making licensure decisions.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 2. Communication between a member state and the commission and among member states regarding the verification of eligibility for licensure through the compact shall not include any information received from the federal bureau of investigation relating to a federal criminal records check performed by a member state under Public Law 92-544.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): C. On application for a privilege to practice, the licensing board in the issuing remote state shall ascertain, through the data system, whether the applicant has ever held, or is the holder of, a license issued by any other state, whether there are any encumbrances on any license or privilege to practice held by the applicant, and whether any adverse action has been taken against any license or privilege to practice held by the applicant.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): D. Each member state shall require an applicant to obtain or retain a license in the home state and meet the home state's qualifications for licensure or renewal of licensure as well as all other applicable state laws.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): E. An audiologist must meet all of the following requirements:
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 1. One of the following educational requirements:

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): (a) On or before December 31, 2007, graduated with a master's degree or doctorate in audiology, or an equivalent degree regardless of degree name, from a program that is accredited by an accrediting agency recognized by the council for higher education accreditation, or its successor, or by the United States department of education and operated by a college or university accredited by a regional or national accrediting organization recognized by the board.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): (b) On or after January 1, 2008, graduated with a doctoral degree in audiology, or an equivalent degree, regardless of degree name, from a program that is accredited by an accrediting agency recognized by the council for higher education accreditation, or its successor, or by the United States department of education and operated by a college or university accredited by a regional or national accrediting organization recognized by the board.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): (c) Graduated from an audiology program that is housed in an institution of higher education outside of the United States, and the program and institution have been approved by the authorized accrediting body in the applicable country and the degree program has been verified by an independent credentials review agency to be comparable to a state licensing board-approved program.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 2. Completed a supervised clinical practicum experience from an accredited educational institution or its cooperating programs as required by the commission.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 3. Successfully passed a national examination approved by the commission.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 4. Hold an active, unencumbered license.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 5. Not have been convicted or found guilty, and not have entered into an agreed disposition, of a felony related to the practice of audiology, under applicable state or federal criminal law.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 6. Have a valid United States social security or national practitioner identification number.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): F. A speech-language pathologist must meet all of the following requirements:
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 1. One of the following educational requirements:

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): (a) Graduated with a master's degree from a speech-language pathology program that is accredited by an organization recognized by the United States department of education and operated by a college or university accredited by a regional or national accrediting organization recognized by the board.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): (b) Graduated from a speech-language pathology program that is housed in an institution of higher education outside of the United States, and the program and institution have been approved by the authorized accrediting body in the applicable country and the degree program has been verified by an independent credentials review agency to be comparable to a state licensing board-approved program.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 2. Completed a supervised clinical practicum experience from an educational institution or its cooperating programs as required by the commission.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 3. Completed a supervised postgraduate professional experience as required by the commission.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 4. Successfully passed a national examination approved by the commission.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 5. Hold an active, unencumbered license.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 6. Not have been convicted or found guilty, and not have entered into an agreed disposition, of a felony related to the practice of speech-language pathology, under applicable state or federal criminal law.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 7. Have a valid United States social security or national practitioner identification number.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): G. The privilege to practice is derived from the home state license.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): H. An audiologist or speech-language pathologist practicing in a member state must comply with the state practice laws of the state in which the client is located at the time service is provided. The practice of audiology and speech-language pathology shall include all audiology and speech-language pathology practices as defined by the state practice laws of the member state in which the client is located. The practice of audiology and speech-language pathology in a member state under a privilege to practice shall subject an audiologist or speech-language pathologist to the jurisdiction of the licensing board, the courts and the laws of the member state in which the client is located at the time service is provided.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): I. Individuals not residing in a member state shall continue to be able to apply for a member state's single-state license as provided under the laws of each member state. However, the single-state license granted to these individuals shall not be recognized as granting the privilege to practice audiology or speech-language pathology in any other member state.  This compact does not affect the requirements established by a member state for the issuance of a single-state license.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): J. Member states may charge a fee for granting a compact privilege.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): K. Member states must comply with the bylaws and rules and regulations of the commission.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): SECTION 4. COMPACT PRIVILEGE

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): A. To exercise the compact privilege under the terms and provisions of the compact, the audiologist or speech-language pathologist shall:
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 1. Hold an active license in the home state.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 2. Have no encumbrance on any state license.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 3. Be eligible for a compact privilege in any member state in accordance with section 3 of this compact.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 4. Not have had any adverse action against any license or compact privilege within the previous two years from date of application.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 5. Notify the commission that the licensee is seeking the compact privilege within a remote state or remote states.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 6. Pay any applicable fees, including any state fee, for the compact privilege.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 7. Report to the commission any adverse action taken by any nonmember state within thirty days after the date the adverse action is taken.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): B. For the purposes of the compact privilege, an audiologist or speech-language pathologist shall hold only one home state license at a time.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): C. Except as provided in section 6 of this compact, if an audiologist or speech-language pathologist changes the person's primary state of residence by moving between two member states, the audiologist or speech-language pathologist must apply for licensure in the new home state, and the license issued by the prior home state shall be deactivated in accordance with applicable rules adopted by the commission.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): D. The audiologist or speech-language pathologist may apply for licensure in advance of a change in primary state of residence.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): E. A license shall not be issued by the new home state until the audiologist or speech-language pathologist provides satisfactory evidence of a change in primary state of residence to the new home state and satisfies all applicable requirements to obtain a license from the new home state.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): F. If an audiologist or speech-language pathologist changes the person's primary state of residence by moving from a member state to a nonmember state, the license issued by the prior home state shall convert to a single-state license, valid only in the former home state.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): G. The compact privilege is valid until the expiration date of the home state license. The licensee must comply with the requirements of subsection A of this section to maintain the compact privilege in the remote state.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): H. A licensee providing audiology or speech-language pathology services in a remote state under the compact privilege shall function within the laws and regulations of the remote state.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): I. A licensee providing audiology or speech-language pathology services in a remote state is subject to that state's regulatory authority.  A remote state may, in accordance with due process and that state's laws, remove a licensee's compact privilege in the remote state for a specific period of time, impose fines and take any other necessary actions to protect the health and safety of its citizens.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): J. If a home state license is encumbered, the licensee shall lose the compact privilege in any remote state until both of the following occur:
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 1. The home state license is no longer encumbered.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 2. Two years have elapsed from the date of the adverse action.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): K. Once an encumbered license in the home state is restored to good standing, the licensee must meet the requirements of subsection A of this section to obtain a compact privilege in any remote state.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): L. Once the requirements of subsection J of this section have been met, the licensee must meet the requirements prescribed in subsection A of this section to obtain a compact privilege in a remote state.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): SECTION 5. COMPACT PRIVILEGE TO PRACTICE TELEHEALTH

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): Member states shall recognize the right of an audiologist or speech-language pathologist who is licensed by a home state in accordance with section 3 of this compact and under rules promulgated by the commission to practice audiology or speech-language pathology in any member state via telehealth under a privilege to practice as provided in the compact and rules promulgated by the commission.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): SECTION 6. ACTIVE DUTY MILITARY PERSONNEL OR THEIR SPOUSES

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): Active duty military personnel, or their spouse, shall designate a home state where the individual has a current license in good standing.  The individual may retain the home state designation during the period the service member is on active duty. Subsequent to designating a home state, the individual shall change the individual's home state only through an application for licensure in the new state.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): SECTION 7. ADVERSE ACTIONS

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): A. In addition to the other powers conferred by state law, a remote state shall have the authority, in accordance with existing state due process law, to:

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 1. Take adverse action against an audiologist's or speech-language pathologist's privilege to practice within that member state.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 2. Issue subpoenas for both hearings and investigations that require the attendance and testimony of witnesses as well as the production of evidence.  Subpoenas issued by a licensing board in a member state for the attendance and testimony of witnesses or the production of evidence from another member state shall be enforced in the latter state by any court of competent jurisdiction, according to the practice and procedure of that court applicable to subpoenas issued in proceedings pending before it. The issuing authority shall pay any witness fees, travel expenses, mileage and other fees required by the service statutes of the state in which the witnesses or evidence are located.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 3. Only the home state shall have the power to take adverse action against an audiologist's or speech-language pathologist's license issued by the home state.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): B. For the purposes of taking adverse action, the home state shall give the same priority and effect to reported conduct received from a member state as it would if the conduct had occurred within the home state. In so doing, the home state shall apply its own state laws to determine appropriate action.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): C. The home state shall complete any pending investigations of an audiologist or speech-language pathologist who changes the individual's primary state of residence during the course of the investigations.  The home state shall also have the authority to take appropriate action or actions and shall promptly report the conclusions of the investigations to the administrator of the data system. The administrator of the coordinated licensure information system shall promptly notify the new home state of any adverse actions.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): D. If otherwise allowed by state law, the member state may recover from the affected audiologist or speech-language pathologist the costs of investigations and disposition of cases resulting from any adverse action taken against that audiologist or speech-language pathologist.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): E. The member state may take adverse action based on the factual findings of the remote state, provided that the member state follows the member state's own procedures for taking the adverse action.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): F. With respect to joint investigations:

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 1. In addition to the authority granted to a member state by its respective audiology or speech-language pathology practice act or other applicable state law, any member state may participate with other member states in joint investigations of licensees.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 2. Member states shall share any investigative, litigation or compliance materials in furtherance of any joint or individual investigation initiated under the compact.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): G. If an adverse action is taken by the home state against an audiologist's or speech-language pathologist's license, the audiologist's or speech-language pathologist's privilege to practice in all other member states shall be deactivated until all encumbrances have been removed from the state license.  All home state disciplinary orders that impose adverse action against an audiologist's or speech-language pathologist's license shall include a statement that the audiologist's or speech-language pathologist's privilege to practice is deactivated in all member states during the pendency of the order.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): H. If a member state takes adverse action, it shall promptly notify the administrator of the data system. The administrator of the data system shall promptly notify the home state of any adverse actions by remote states.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): I. This compact does not override a member state's decision that participation in an alternative program may be used in lieu of adverse action.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): SECTION 8. ESTABLISHMENT OF THE AUDIOLOGY AND
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): SPEECH-LANGUAGE PATHOLOGY COMPACT COMMISSION

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): A. The compact member states hereby create and establish a joint public agency known as the audiology and speech-language pathology compact commission, to which the following apply:
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 1. The commission is an instrumentality of the compact states.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 2. Venue is proper and judicial proceedings by or against the commission shall be brought solely and exclusively in a court of competent jurisdiction where the principal office of the commission is located.  The commission may waive venue and jurisdictional defenses to the extent it adopts or consents to participate in alternative dispute resolution proceedings.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 3. Nothing in this compact shall be construed to be a waiver of sovereign immunity.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): B. Membership, voting and meetings of the commission are as follows:

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 1. Each member state shall have two delegates selected by that member state's licensing board.  The delegates shall be current members of the licensing board.  One shall be an audiologist and one shall be a speech-language pathologist.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 2. An additional five delegates, who are either public members or board administrators from a state licensing board, shall be chosen by the executive committee from a pool of nominees provided by the commission at large.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 3. Any delegate may be removed or suspended from office as provided by the law of the state from which the delegate is appointed.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 4. The member state board shall fill any vacancy occurring on the commission within ninety days.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 5. Each delegate shall be entitled to one vote with regard to the promulgation of rules and creation of bylaws and shall otherwise have an opportunity to participate in the business and affairs of the commission.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 6. A delegate shall vote in person or by other means as provided in the bylaws. The bylaws may provide for delegates' participation in meetings by telephone or other means of communication.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 7. The commission shall meet at least once during each calendar year. Additional meetings shall be held as set forth in the bylaws.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): C. The commission shall have the following powers and duties:
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 1. Establish the fiscal year of the commission.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 2. Establish bylaws.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 3. Establish a code of ethics.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 4. Maintain its financial records in accordance with the bylaws.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 5. Meet and take actions as are consistent with the provisions of this compact and the bylaws.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 6. Promulgate uniform rules to facilitate and coordinate implementation and administration of this compact. The rules shall have the force and effect of law and shall be binding in all member states.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 7. Bring and prosecute legal proceedings or actions in the name of the commission, provided that the standing of any state audiology or speech-language pathology licensing board to sue or be sued under applicable law shall not be affected.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 8. Purchase and maintain insurance and bonds.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 9. Borrow, accept or contract for services of personnel, including employees of a member state.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 10. Hire employees, elect or appoint officers, fix compensation, define duties, grant individuals appropriate authority to carry out the purposes of this compact, and establish the commission's personnel policies and programs relating to conflicts of interest, qualifications of personnel and other related personnel matters.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 11. Accept any appropriate donations and grants of monies, equipment, supplies, materials and services and receive, use and dispose of the same, provided that at all times the commission shall avoid any appearance of impropriety and conflict of interest.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 12. Lease, purchase, accept appropriate gifts or donations of or otherwise own, hold, improve or use any property, whether real, personal or mixed, provided that at all times the commission shall avoid any appearance of impropriety.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 13. Sell, convey, mortgage, pledge, lease, exchange, abandon or otherwise dispose of any property, whether real, personal or mixed.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 14. Establish a budget and make expenditures.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 15. Borrow monies.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 16. Appoint committees, including standing committees composed of members and other interested persons as may be designated in this compact and the bylaws.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 17. Provide and receive information from, and cooperate with, law enforcement agencies.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 18. Establish and elect an executive committee.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 19. Perform other functions as may be necessary or appropriate to achieve the purposes of this compact consistent with the state regulation of audiology and speech-language pathology licensure and practice.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): D. The executive committee shall have the power to act on behalf of the commission according to the terms of this compact. The executive committee shall be composed of ten members as follows:
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 1. Seven voting members who are elected by the commission from the current membership of the commission.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 2. Two ex officio members, one of whom is a nonvoting member from a recognized national audiology professional association and one of whom is a nonvoting member from a recognized national speech-language pathology association.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 3. One ex officio member who is a nonvoting member from the recognized membership organization of the audiology and speech-language pathology licensing boards.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): E. The following pertain to the executive committee:

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 1. Ex officio members shall be selected by their respective organizations, and the commission may remove any member of the executive committee as provided in the bylaws.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 2. The executive committee shall meet at least annually.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 3. The executive committee shall have the following duties and responsibilities:

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): (a) Recommend to the entire commission changes to the rules or bylaws, this compact legislation, fees paid by compact member states such as annual dues and any commission compact fee charged to licensees for the compact privilege.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): (b) Ensure that compact administration services are appropriately provided, contractual or otherwise.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): (c) Prepare and recommend the budget.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): (d) Maintain financial records on behalf of the commission.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): (e) Monitor compact compliance of member states and provide compliance reports to the commission.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): (f) Establish additional committees as necessary.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): (g) Perform any other duties as provided in rules or bylaws.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): F. All meetings of the commission shall be open to the public, and public notice of meetings shall be given in the same manner as required under the rulemaking provisions prescribed in section 10 of this compact.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): G. The commission or the executive committee or other committees of the commission may convene in a closed, nonpublic meeting if the commission or executive committee or other committees of the commission must discuss any of the following:
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 1. Noncompliance of a member state with its obligations under this compact.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 2. The employment, compensation, discipline or other matters, practices or procedures related to specific employees or other matters related to the commission's internal personnel practices and procedures.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 3. Current, threatened or reasonably anticipated litigation.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 4. Negotiation of contracts for the purchase, lease or sale of goods, services or real estate.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 5. The accusation of any person of a crime or the formal censuring of any person.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 6. The disclosure of trade secrets or commercial or financial information that is privileged or confidential.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 7. The disclosure of information of a personal nature if the disclosure would constitute a clearly unwarranted invasion of personal privacy.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 8. The disclosure of investigative records compiled for law enforcement purposes.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 9. The disclosure of information related to any investigative reports prepared by or on behalf of or for use of the commission or other committee charged with responsibility of investigation or determination of compliance issues pursuant to the compact.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 10. Matters specifically exempted from disclosure by federal or member state statute.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): H. If a meeting, or portion of a meeting, is closed pursuant to this section, the commission's legal counsel or designee shall certify that the meeting may be closed and shall reference each relevant exempting provision.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): I. The commission shall keep minutes that fully and clearly describe all matters discussed in a meeting and shall provide a full and accurate summary of actions taken, and the reasons therefore, including a description of the views expressed. All documents considered in connection with an action shall be identified in minutes.  All minutes and documents of a closed meeting shall remain under seal, subject to release by a majority vote of the commission or order of a court of competent jurisdiction.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): J. Financing of the commission is as follows:

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 1. The commission shall pay, or provide for the payment of, the reasonable expenses of its establishment, organization and ongoing activities.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 2. The commission may accept any appropriate revenue sources, donations and grants of monies, equipment, supplies, materials and services.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 3. The commission may levy on and collect an annual assessment from each member state or impose fees on other parties to cover the cost of the operations and activities of the commission and its staff, which must be in a total amount sufficient to cover its annual budget as approved each year for which revenue is not provided by other sources.  The aggregate annual assessment amount shall be allocated based on a formula to be determined by the commission, which shall promulgate a rule binding on all member states.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 4. The commission shall not incur obligations of any kind before securing the monies adequate to meet the same, and the commission shall not pledge the credit of any of the member states, except by and with the authority of the member state.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 5. The commission shall keep accurate accounts of all receipts and disbursements. The receipts and disbursements of the commission are subject to the audit and accounting procedures established under its bylaws. All receipts and disbursements of monies handled by the commission shall be audited yearly by a certified or licensed public accountant, and the report of the audit shall be included in and become part of the annual report of the commission.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): K. Qualified immunity, defense and indemnification are as follows:

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 1. The members, officers, executive director, employees and representatives of the commission are immune from suit and liability, either personally or in their official capacity, for any claim for damage to or loss of property or personal injury or other civil liability caused by or arising out of any actual or alleged act, error or omission that occurred, or that the person against whom the claim is made had a reasonable basis for believing occurred within the scope of commission employment, duties or responsibilities.  This paragraph does not protect any person from suit or liability for any damage, loss, injury or liability caused by the intentional or wilful or wanton misconduct of that person.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 2. The commission shall defend any member, officer, executive director, employee or representative of the commission in any civil action seeking to impose liability arising out of any actual or alleged act, error or omission that occurred within the scope of commission employment, duties or responsibilities, or that the person against whom the claim is made had a reasonable basis for believing occurred within the scope of commission employment, duties or responsibilities, provided that this paragraph shall not be construed to prohibit that person from retaining his or her own counsel, and provided further, that the actual or alleged act, error or omission did not result from that person's intentional or wilful or wanton misconduct.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 3. The commission shall indemnify and hold harmless any member, officer, executive director, employee or representative of the commission for the amount of any settlement or judgment obtained against that person arising out of any actual or alleged act, error or omission that occurred within the scope of commission employment, duties or responsibilities, or that person had a reasonable basis for believing occurred within the scope of commission employment, duties or responsibilities, if the actual or alleged act, error or omission did not result from the intentional or wilful or wanton misconduct of that person.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): SECTION 9. DATA SYSTEM

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): A. The commission shall provide for the development, maintenance and use of a coordinated database and reporting system containing licensure, adverse action and investigative information on all licensed individuals in member states.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): B. Notwithstanding any other provision of state law to the contrary, a member state shall submit a uniform data set to the data system on all individuals to whom this compact applies as required by the rules of the commission, including:
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 1. Identifying information.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 2. Licensure data.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 3. Adverse actions against a license or compact privilege.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 4. Nonconfidential information related to alternative program participation.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 5. Any denial of an application for licensure and the reason or reasons for denial.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 6. Other information that may facilitate the administration of this compact, as determined by the rules of the commission.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): C. Investigative information pertaining to a licensee in any member state shall be available only to other member states.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): D. The commission shall promptly notify all member states of any adverse action taken against a licensee or an individual applying for a license. Adverse action information pertaining to a licensee in any member state shall be available to any other member state.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): E. Member states contributing information to the data system may designate information that may not be shared with the public without the express permission of the contributing state.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): F. Any information submitted to the data system that is subsequently required to be expunged by the laws of the member state contributing the information shall be removed from the data system.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): SECTION 10. RULEMAKING

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): A. The commission shall exercise its rulemaking powers pursuant to the criteria set forth in this section and the rules adopted thereunder. Rules and amendments shall become binding as of the date specified in each rule or amendment.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): B. If a majority of the legislatures of the member states rejects a rule, by enacting a statute or resolution in the same manner used to adopt the compact within four years after the date of adoption of the rule, the rule shall have no further force and effect in any member state.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): C. Rules or amendments to the rules shall be adopted at a regular or special meeting of the commission.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): D. Before promulgation and adoption of a final rule or rules by the commission, and at least thirty days in advance of the meeting at which the rule shall be considered and voted on, the commission shall file a notice of proposed rulemaking both:
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 1. On the website of the commission or other publicly accessible platform.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 2. On the website of each member state audiology or speech-language pathology licensing board or other publicly accessible platform or the publication in which each state would otherwise publish proposed rules.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): E. The notice of proposed rulemaking shall include all of the following:
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 1. The proposed time, date and location of the meeting in which the rule shall be considered and voted on.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 2. The text of the proposed rule or amendment and the reason for the proposed rule.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 3. A request for comments on the proposed rule from any interested person.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 4. The manner in which interested persons may submit notice to the commission of their intention to attend the public hearing and any written comments.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): F. Before the adoption of a proposed rule, the commission shall allow persons to submit written data, facts, opinions and arguments, which shall be made available to the public.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): G. The commission shall grant an opportunity for a public hearing before it adopts a rule or amendment if a hearing is requested by either:
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 1. At least twenty-five persons.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 2. A state or federal governmental subdivision or agency.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 3. An association having at least twenty-five members.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): H. If a hearing is held on the proposed rule or amendment, the commission shall publish the place, time and date of the scheduled public hearing. If the hearing is held via electronic means, the commission shall publish the mechanism for access to the electronic hearing. Additionally:

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 1. All persons wishing to be heard at the hearing shall notify the executive director of the commission or other designated member in writing of their desire to appear and testify at the hearing at least five business days before the scheduled date of the hearing.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 2. Hearings shall be conducted in a manner providing each person who wishes to comment a fair and reasonable opportunity to comment orally or in writing.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 3. All hearings shall be recorded.  A copy of the recording shall be made available on request.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 4. This section does not require a separate hearing on each rule. Rules may be grouped for the convenience of the commission at hearings required by this section.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): I. Following the scheduled hearing date, or by the close of business on the scheduled hearing date if the hearing was not held, the commission shall consider all written and oral comments received.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): J. If no written notice of intent to attend the public hearing by interested parties is received, the commission may proceed with promulgation of the proposed rule without a public hearing.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): K. The commission, by majority vote of all members, shall take final action on the proposed rule and shall determine the effective date of the rule, if any, based on the rulemaking record and the full text of the rule.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): L. On determination that an emergency exists, the commission may consider and adopt an emergency rule without prior notice, opportunity for comment or a hearing, provided that the usual rulemaking procedures provided in the compact and in this section shall be retroactively applied to the rule as soon as reasonably possible but not later than ninety days after the effective date of the rule. For the purposes of this subsection, an emergency rule is one that must be adopted immediately in order to do any of the following:
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 1. Meet an imminent threat to public health, safety, or welfare.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 2. Prevent a loss of commission or member state monies.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 3. Meet a deadline for the promulgation of an administrative rule that is established by federal law or rule.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): M. The commission or an authorized committee of the commission may direct revisions to a previously adopted rule or amendment for purposes of correcting typographical errors, errors in format, errors in consistency or grammatical errors.  Public notice of any revisions shall be posted on the website of the commission.  The revision shall be subject to challenge by any person for a period of thirty days after posting. The revision may be challenged only on grounds that the revision results in a material change to a rule.  A challenge shall be made in writing and delivered to the chairperson of the commission before the end of the notice period.  If no challenge is made, the revision shall take effect without further action.  If the revision is challenged, the revision may not take effect without the approval of the commission.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): SECTION 11. OVERSIGHT, DISPUTE RESOLUTION AND ENFORCEMENT
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): A. Dispute resolution shall be as follows:

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 1. On request by a member state, the commission shall attempt to resolve disputes related to the compact that arise among member states and between member and nonmember states.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 2. The commission shall promulgate a rule providing for both mediation and binding dispute resolution for disputes as appropriate.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): B. Enforcement shall be as follows:
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 1. The commission, in the reasonable exercise of its discretion, shall enforce the provisions and rules of this compact.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 2. By majority vote, the commission may initiate legal action in the United States district court for the District of Columbia or the federal district where the commission has its principal offices against a member state in default to enforce compliance with the provisions of this compact and its promulgated rules and bylaws. The relief sought may include both injunctive relief and damages. If judicial enforcement is necessary, the prevailing member state shall be awarded all costs of litigation, including reasonable attorney fees.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 3. The remedies in this compact are not the exclusive remedies of the commission. The commission may pursue any other remedies available under federal or state law.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): SECTION 12. DATE OF IMPLEMENTATION OF THE INTERSTATE COMMISSION
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): FOR AUDIOLOGY AND SPEECH-LANGUAGE PATHOLOGY PRACTICE AND
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): ASSOCIATED RULES, WITHDRAWAL AND AMENDMENT

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): A. This compact is effective on the date on which the compact statute is enacted into law in the tenth member state.  The provisions, which become effective at that time, shall be limited to the powers granted to the commission relating to assembly and the promulgation of rules. Thereafter, the commission shall meet and exercise rulemaking powers necessary to implement and administer this compact.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): B. Any state that joins this compact after the commission's initial adoption of the rules is subject to the rules as they exist on the date on which the compact becomes law in that state. Any rule that has been previously adopted by the commission shall have the full force and effect of law on the day the compact becomes law in that state.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): C. Any member state may withdraw from this compact by enacting a statute repealing the compact, as follows:
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 1. A member state's withdrawal shall not take effect until six months after enactment of the repealing statute.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): 2. Withdrawal shall not affect the continuing requirement of the withdrawing state's audiology or speech-language pathology licensing board to comply with the investigative and adverse action reporting requirements of this compact before the effective date of withdrawal.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): D. This compact does not invalidate or prevent any audiology or speech-language pathology licensure agreement or other cooperative arrangement between a member state and a nonmember state that does not conflict with the provisions of this compact.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): E. This compact may be amended by the member states. An amendment to this compact does not become effective and binding on any member state until it is enacted into the laws of all member states.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): SECTION 13. CONSTRUCTION AND SEVERABILITY

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): This compact shall be liberally construed so as to effectuate the purposes thereof.  The provisions of this compact shall be severable and if any phrase, clause, sentence or provision of this compact is declared to be contrary to the constitution of any member state or of the United States or the applicability thereof to any government, agency, person or circumstance is held invalid, the validity of the remainder of this compact and the applicability thereof to any government, agency, person or circumstance shall not be affected thereby. If this compact is held contrary to the constitution of any member state, the compact shall remain in full force and effect as to the remaining member states and in full force and effect as to the member state affected as to all severable matters.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): SECTION 14. BINDING EFFECT OF COMPACT AND OTHER LAWS

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): A. This compact does not prevent the enforcement of any other law of a member state that is not inconsistent with this compact.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): B. All laws in a member state in conflict with this compact are superseded to the extent of the conflict.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): C. All lawful actions of the commission, including all rules and bylaws promulgated by the commission, are binding on the member states.
ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): D. All agreements between the commission and the member states are binding in accordance with their terms.

ARS § 36-1940.11 (Audiologists and speech-language pathologists; compact): E. If any provision of this compact exceeds the constitutional limits imposed on the legislature of any member state, the provision shall be ineffective to the extent of the conflict with the constitutional provision in question in that member state.
ARS § 36-1941 (Definitions): In this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires:
ARS § 36-1941 (Definitions): 1. "Commission" means the commission for the deaf and the hard of hearing.
ARS § 36-1941 (Definitions): 2. "Deaf" means a person who cannot generally understand speech sounds with or without a hearing aid when in optimal listening conditions.

ARS § 36-1941 (Definitions): 3. "Deafblind" means a person who is deaf or hard of hearing, who has a central visual acuity of 20/200 or less in the better eye with corrective lenses, or a field defect such that the peripheral diameter of visual field subtends an angular distance not greater than twenty degrees, or a progressive visual loss having a prognosis leading to one or both of these conditions, and for whom the combination of the hearing and vision loss described affects the person's ability to communicate and receive environmental information both visually and auditorily.
ARS § 36-1941 (Definitions): 4. "Hard of hearing" means a person who has a degree of hearing loss greater than 40dB PTA-2, but less than 85dB PTA-2, in the better ear.

ARS § 36-1941 (Definitions): 5. "Interpreting" means translating or transliterating English concepts to any necessary specialized vocabulary used by a consumer or translating a consumer specialized vocabulary to English concepts.
ARS § 36-1941 (Definitions): 6. "Necessary specialized vocabulary" includes American sign language, English based sign language, cued speech and oral interpreting.
ARS § 36-1941 (Definitions): 7. "PTA-2" means the average of hearing levels at one thousand, two thousand and four thousand Hz.
ARS § 36-1942 (Commission for the deaf and the hard of hearing): A. The commission for the deaf and the hard of hearing is established consisting of the following members appointed by the governor:
ARS § 36-1942 (Commission for the deaf and the hard of hearing): 1. One member who is selected from the department of economic security.

ARS § 36-1942 (Commission for the deaf and the hard of hearing): 2. One member who is selected from the Arizona state schools for the deaf and the blind at Tucson or the Phoenix day school for the deaf.
ARS § 36-1942 (Commission for the deaf and the hard of hearing): 3. One member who is a dispensing clinical audiologist licensed pursuant to chapter 17 of this title.
ARS § 36-1942 (Commission for the deaf and the hard of hearing): 4. One member who is a hearing aid dispenser licensed pursuant to chapter 17 of this title.
ARS § 36-1942 (Commission for the deaf and the hard of hearing): 5. Four members who are deaf persons.
ARS § 36-1942 (Commission for the deaf and the hard of hearing): 6. One member who is a licensed sign language interpreter.
ARS § 36-1942 (Commission for the deaf and the hard of hearing): 7. One member who is a parent of a deaf person.
ARS § 36-1942 (Commission for the deaf and the hard of hearing): 8. Four members who are hard of hearing.
ARS § 36-1942 (Commission for the deaf and the hard of hearing): B. Commission members serve three years and may be reappointed once. The governor may remove a commission member for cause.

ARS § 36-1942 (Commission for the deaf and the hard of hearing): C. The commission shall meet at least four times a year at the call of the chairman, who shall be selected by the commission from among its membership.

ARS § 36-1942 (Commission for the deaf and the hard of hearing): D. Members of the commission are not eligible to receive compensation but are eligible to receive reimbursement of expenses pursuant to title 38, chapter 4, article 2.

ARS § 36-1943 (Executive director; duties): A. Subject to title 41, chapter 4, article 4, the commission shall appoint an executive director who serves at the pleasure of the commission.  Subject to title 41, chapter 4, article 4, the commission may employ other employees as necessary, determine their compensation pursuant to section 38-611 and prescribe their powers and duties.  With the approval of the commission, the executive director may contract for professional, technical and clerical services necessary to carry out functions of the commission.

ARS § 36-1943 (Executive director; duties): B. The executive director shall be a trained professional experienced in problems of the deaf and the hard of hearing and skilled in the use of manual communication, commonly referred to as sign language, and may be either a deaf person, a person who is hard of hearing or a person with normal hearing.  The executive director shall assist the commission to implement its programs and activities and to implement this chapter. The executive director shall not be a commission member. The executive director is eligible to receive compensation set by the commission within the range determined pursuant to section 38-611.

ARS § 36-1944 (Duties): The commission shall act as a bureau of information to the deaf, the hard of hearing and the deafblind, state agencies and institutions providing services to the deaf, the hard of hearing and the deafblind, local agencies of government and other public or private community agencies and programs.  In this capacity, the commission shall:

ARS § 36-1944 (Duties): 1. Inform the deaf, the hard of hearing and the deafblind of the availability of the programs and activities of the commission and other services available for the deaf, the hard of hearing and the deafblind at all levels of government.

ARS § 36-1944 (Duties): 2. Develop and foster a framework for consultation and cooperation with the rehabilitation services bureau of the department of economic security and with all institutions represented on the commission.

ARS § 36-1944 (Duties): 3. Study issues relating to the deaf, the hard of hearing and the deafblind, review the administration and operation of the various programs for the deaf, the hard of hearing and the deafblind in this state and make recommendations concerning these problems and programs to the several agencies and institutions represented on the commission as it deems necessary.
ARS § 36-1944 (Duties): 4. Submit an annual report to the governor and the legislature concerning its findings and recommendations.
ARS § 36-1944 (Duties): 5. Review the problems of the deaf, the hard of hearing and the deafblind as they relate to the need for effective and appropriate auxiliary aids in public places.
ARS § 36-1944 (Duties): 6. Review and compile information on the development of acoustical technology for the hard of hearing and advocate the use of this technology if it deems appropriate.
ARS § 36-1944 (Duties): 7. Make recommendations to state agencies, political subdivisions and institutions on how to meet the needs of the deaf, the hard of hearing and the deafblind.
ARS § 36-1944 (Duties): 8. Make recommendations to the legislature regarding statutory changes needed:
ARS § 36-1944 (Duties): (a) To develop and support statewide newborn child hearing loss screening programs.
ARS § 36-1944 (Duties): (b) To develop and update assessment standards that optimize the language acquisition and literacy development of deaf and hard of hearing newborns, infants and children.

ARS § 36-1945 (Commission for the deaf and the hard of hearing fund; gifts and donations; annual report): A. The commission for the deaf and the hard of hearing fund is established consisting of fees, penalties and any legislative appropriations. The commission shall administer the fund.  Monies in the fund are subject to legislative appropriation.

ARS § 36-1945 (Commission for the deaf and the hard of hearing fund; gifts and donations; annual report): B. The commission may accept and spend federal monies and private grants, gifts, contributions and devises to assist in carrying out the purposes of this chapter.  These monies do not revert to the state general fund at the end of a fiscal year.

ARS § 36-1945 (Commission for the deaf and the hard of hearing fund; gifts and donations; annual report): C. The commission shall submit an annual report to the governor on all monies accepted by the commission pursuant to subsection B, the names of the donors and the respective amounts contributed and the amount of all disbursements from the fund.
ARS § 36-1946 (Interpreters for the deaf and the hard of hearing; certification; licensure): The commission shall:
ARS § 36-1946 (Interpreters for the deaf and the hard of hearing; certification; licensure): 1. Adopt rules necessary to achieve the purposes of section 12-242.

ARS § 36-1946 (Interpreters for the deaf and the hard of hearing; certification; licensure): 2. By rule, classify interpreters for the deaf and the hard of hearing based on the level of interpreting skills acquired by that person.

ARS § 36-1946 (Interpreters for the deaf and the hard of hearing; certification; licensure): 3. By rule, establish standards and procedures for the qualification and licensure of each classification of interpreters.

ARS § 36-1946 (Interpreters for the deaf and the hard of hearing; certification; licensure): 4. Help establish partnerships with colleges and universities in this state to provide interpreter and support service provider training and degree programs.

ARS § 36-1946 (Interpreters for the deaf and the hard of hearing; certification; licensure): 5. By rule, establish standards and procedures to certify sign language teachers to teach American sign language.

ARS § 36-1946 (Interpreters for the deaf and the hard of hearing; certification; licensure): 6. Beginning on September 1, 2007, license interpreters for the deaf and the hard of hearing pursuant to article 2 of this chapter.

ARS § 36-1947 (Telecommunication devices for the deaf and the hearing and speech impaired; fund): A. The commission shall establish and administer a statewide program to purchase, repair and distribute telecommunication devices to residents of this state who are deaf or severely hearing or speech impaired and establish a dual party relay system making all phases of public telephone service available to persons who are deaf or severely hearing or speech impaired.

ARS § 36-1947 (Telecommunication devices for the deaf and the hearing and speech impaired; fund): B. The commission may adopt administrative procedures, rules, criteria and forms to establish and administer the telecommunication device program under this section.

ARS § 36-1947 (Telecommunication devices for the deaf and the hearing and speech impaired; fund): C. Telecommunication devices furnished by the commission under this section remain the property of this state.  A person who receives a telecommunication device from the commission under this section is liable for the loss of or damage to the device.  The commission may impose a civil penalty against the person in an amount equal to the cost of the device or the amount of damage done to the device.  If a person objects to the imposition of a civil penalty, the commission shall conduct a hearing as prescribed in title 41, chapter 6, article 10.  Monies collected by the commission under this subsection shall be deposited in the telecommunication fund for the deaf established by subsection D of this section.

ARS § 36-1947 (Telecommunication devices for the deaf and the hearing and speech impaired; fund): D. The telecommunication fund for the deaf is established.  The commission shall administer the fund.  Monies in the fund shall be derived from the telecommunication services excise tax revenues distributed pursuant to section 42-5252, subsection B.  Interest accruing to the fund shall be deposited in the fund.  Monies in the fund are exempt from section 35-190 relating to lapsing of appropriations.  Subject to legislative appropriation, the commission shall use fund monies to purchase and repair telecommunication devices, to administer the program established by this section and for the operating costs of the commission.

ARS § 36-1971 (Licensure; acts and persons not affected): A. A person shall not practice as an interpreter for the deaf and the hard of hearing without a license issued pursuant to this article.  The licensure requirements of this article also apply to interpreters who provide services for legal proceedings as prescribed in section 12-242.

ARS § 36-1971 (Licensure; acts and persons not affected): B. The commission by rule shall prescribe education, examination and work history requirements for the following three categories of licenses:
ARS § 36-1971 (Licensure; acts and persons not affected): 1. Legal.
ARS § 36-1971 (Licensure; acts and persons not affected): 2. Generalist.
ARS § 36-1971 (Licensure; acts and persons not affected): 3. Provisional.
ARS § 36-1971 (Licensure; acts and persons not affected): C. This article does not apply to:

ARS § 36-1971 (Licensure; acts and persons not affected): 1. An interpreter who works in this state for less than twenty days if that person registers with the commission to provide interpreting services in nonlegal situations.
ARS § 36-1971 (Licensure; acts and persons not affected): 2. An interpreter who provides interpreting services at religious activities.

ARS § 36-1971 (Licensure; acts and persons not affected): 3. An interpreter who provides interpreting services on an emergency basis if the delay necessary to obtain a licensed interpreter is likely to cause injury or loss to the consumer.
ARS § 36-1971 (Licensure; acts and persons not affected): 4. An interpreter who works without compensation in nonlegal situations.

ARS § 36-1971 (Licensure; acts and persons not affected): 5. An interpreter who works in a school in this state pursuant to the individual education plan of a deaf or hard of hearing pupil.  The qualifications of an interpreter working in a school in this state shall be determined by the individualized education program team.  A school district shall inform a parent or guardian of a deaf or hard of hearing pupil of the parent or guardian's right to request a licensed interpreter.
ARS § 36-1971 (Licensure; acts and persons not affected): 6. Activities and services of an interpreter intern or student in training if both of the following are true:
ARS § 36-1971 (Licensure; acts and persons not affected): (a) The interpreter is enrolled in a program of study in interpreting at an accredited institution of higher learning.

ARS § 36-1971 (Licensure; acts and persons not affected): (b) The interpreter works under the supervision of a person licensed pursuant to this article as part of a supervised program of study and is identified to all consumers as an interpreter intern or student in training.
ARS § 36-1972 (Use of title; prohibited acts; violation; classification): A. A person who is not licensed pursuant to this article shall not:

ARS § 36-1972 (Use of title; prohibited acts; violation; classification): 1. Use any title, abbreviation, words, letters, signs or figures to indicate that the person is licensed pursuant to this chapter.
ARS § 36-1972 (Use of title; prohibited acts; violation; classification): 2. Practice as an interpreter for the deaf and the hard of hearing.
ARS § 36-1972 (Use of title; prohibited acts; violation; classification): 3. Use another person's license.
ARS § 36-1972 (Use of title; prohibited acts; violation; classification): B. A person who violates this section is guilty of a class 2 misdemeanor.

ARS § 36-1973 (Qualifications for licensure): A. To receive a license to practice as an interpreter pursuant to this article a person shall submit an application and application fee as prescribed by the commission.

ARS § 36-1973 (Qualifications for licensure): B. The applicant shall document to the commission's satisfaction that the applicant has successfully completed the education, examination and work history requirements for the specific category of license for which the licensee is applying.

ARS § 36-1974 (Issuance and renewal of license; continuing education): A. The executive director shall issue a license if the applicant has satisfied all of the requirements for licensure under this article.

ARS § 36-1974 (Issuance and renewal of license; continuing education): B. A license issued pursuant to this article is subject to renewal one year after the date it was issued and terminates thirty days after the renewal date unless it is renewed.

ARS § 36-1974 (Issuance and renewal of license; continuing education): C. Each licensee shall renew the license not earlier than sixty days before and not later than thirty days after the license expires by submitting the renewal fee and a completed renewal form.  A licensee who does not renew a license as required by this article must also pay a penalty fee as prescribed by the commission for late renewal.  A person who practices interpreting in this state after that person's license has expired is in violation of this article.
ARS § 36-1974 (Issuance and renewal of license; continuing education): D. A person whose license terminates shall submit an application and application fee as an original applicant for licensure.
ARS § 36-1974 (Issuance and renewal of license; continuing education): E. The commission by rule may prescribe continuing education requirements as a condition of license renewal.
ARS § 36-1975 (Denial of licensure): The commission may refuse to issue or renew a license if the commission finds that any of the following is true:
ARS § 36-1975 (Denial of licensure): 1. The applicant committed fraud or misrepresentation in applying for a license in this state or another state.
ARS § 36-1975 (Denial of licensure): 2. The applicant was convicted of a felony offense or any other offense involving moral turpitude.
ARS § 36-1975 (Denial of licensure): 3. The applicant does not meet minimum qualifications as prescribed by this article.
ARS § 36-1975 (Denial of licensure): 4. The applicant was adjudicated insane or incompetent.
ARS § 36-1975 (Denial of licensure): 5. The applicant engaged in fraud, dishonesty or corruption on a certification examination in another state.

ARS § 36-1976 (Revocation or suspension of license): A. The commission may revoke or suspend a license issued under this article, place a licensee on probation, issue a reprimand or impose a civil penalty for any of the following reasons:
ARS § 36-1976 (Revocation or suspension of license): 1. Unprofessional conduct.
ARS § 36-1976 (Revocation or suspension of license): 2. A violation of this article.
ARS § 36-1976 (Revocation or suspension of license): 3. Gross negligence or incompetence in the performance of duties.
ARS § 36-1976 (Revocation or suspension of license): 4. Fraud, dishonesty or corruption.
ARS § 36-1976 (Revocation or suspension of license): 5. Inability to perform the duties of an interpreter at a level of skill that is required by the commission.
ARS § 36-1976 (Revocation or suspension of license): 6. Conviction of a felony offense or any other offense involving moral turpitude.
ARS § 36-1976 (Revocation or suspension of license): 7. Failing to meet minimum qualifications as prescribed by this article.
ARS § 36-1976 (Revocation or suspension of license): 8. Adjudication of insanity or incompetency.

ARS § 36-1976 (Revocation or suspension of license): B. Before it takes disciplinary action pursuant to this section, the commission shall give a licensee notice and an opportunity for a hearing pursuant to its rules.
ARS § 36-1976 (Revocation or suspension of license): C. The commission may issue subpoenas, examine witnesses and administer oaths pursuant to a hearing held under this section.

ARS § 36-1977 (Right to examine and copy evidence): In connection with a commission investigation conducted pursuant to section 36-1976, the commission at all reasonable times has the right to examine and copy any documents, reports, records or other physical evidence of any person being investigated or reports, records and any other documents maintained by and in the possession of any public or private agency if the commission believes this information is related to unprofessional conduct or the mental or physical ability of a licensee to practice pursuant to this article.

ARS § 36-1978 (Injunctive relief; bond; service of process): A. In addition to all other available remedies, if the commission has any reason to believe that a person has violated this article or a commission rule, the commission through the attorney general or the county attorney of the county in which the violation is alleged to have occurred may apply to the superior court in that county for an injunction restraining that person from engaging in the violation.

ARS § 36-1978 (Injunctive relief; bond; service of process): B. The court shall issue a temporary restraining order, a preliminary injunction or a permanent injunction without requiring the commission to post a bond.
ARS § 36-1978 (Injunctive relief; bond; service of process): C. Service of process may be on the defendant in any county of this state where the defendant is found.
