If the department fails to adopt regulations to implement this chapter within one hundred twenty days of the effective date of this chapter, any citizen may commence a mandamus action in superior court to compel the department to perform the actions mandated under this chapter.

ARS § 36-2818 (Enforcement of this act; mandamus): B. If the department fails to issue a registry identification card within forty-five days of the submission of a valid application or renewal, the registry identification card shall be deemed issued, and a copy of the registry identification card application or renewal is deemed a valid registry identification card.

ARS § 36-2818 (Enforcement of this act; mandamus): C. If at any time after the one hundred forty days following the effective date of this chapter the department is not accepting applications or has not promulgated rules allowing qualifying patients to submit applications, a notarized statement by a qualifying patient containing the information required in an application pursuant to section 36-2804.02, subsection A, paragraph 3, together with a written certification issued by a physician within the ninety days immediately preceding the notarized statement, shall be deemed a valid registry identification card.
ARS § 36-2819 (Fingerprinting requirements): (Caution:  1998 Prop. 105 applies)

ARS § 36-2819 (Fingerprinting requirements): Each person applying as a designated caregiver, a principal officer, agent or employee of a nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary, a nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary agent or an independent third-party laboratory agent may submit a current level I fingerprint clearance card issued pursuant to section 41-1758.07 or shall submit a full set of fingerprints to the department for the purpose of obtaining a state and federal criminal records check pursuant to section 41-1750 and Public Law 92-544. The department of public safety may exchange this fingerprint data with the federal bureau of investigation without disclosing that the records check is related to the medical marijuana act and acts allowed by it.  The department shall destroy each set of fingerprints after the criminal records check is completed.
ARS § 36-2820 (Use of outside counsel): (Added with a 1998 Prop. 105 clause pursuant to L19, Ch. 318)

ARS § 36-2820 (Use of outside counsel): Notwithstanding section 41-192, the department may employ legal counsel and make an expenditure or incur an indebtedness for legal services to implement, advise on or defend this chapter, chapter 28.2 or the rules adopted pursuant to this chapter or chapter 28.2.
ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): (Added with a 1998 Prop. 105 clause pursuant to L19, Ch. 318)

ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): A. The director shall establish a medical marijuana testing advisory council to assist and make recommendations to the director regarding administering and implementing this chapter. The director or the director's designee shall serve as the chairperson of the advisory council and shall appoint the following additional members to the council:

ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): 1. The president or executive director of a statewide nonprofit association representing the marijuana dispensaries, or the person's designee.

ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): 2. The president or executive director of a statewide nonprofit cannabis testing association, or the person's designee.

ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): 3. The president or executive director of a medical marijuana trade association that does not primarily consist of dispensaries or cannabis laboratory testing facility owners, or the person's designee.

ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): 4. A representative of a nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary who is employed by the dispensary to cultivate medical marijuana and who has at least three years of medical marijuana cultivation experience.

ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): 5. A representative of an Arizona-based nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary that produces medical marijuana concentrates and that has been regularly sending products for testing who has at least three years of medical marijuana extraction experience.

ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): 6. A representative of an Arizona-based nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary that is primarily focused on producing medical marijuana edibles who has at least three years of medical marijuana edible production experience.
ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): 7. An owner of an Arizona-based cannabis testing laboratory.

ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): 8. A laboratory scientist who holds a doctorate or a bachelor of science degree and who has at least three years of experience in cannabis laboratory testing.
ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): 9. A registered qualifying patient.
ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): 10. A registered designated caregiver.
ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): 11. A representative of the department of public safety.

ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): 12. A licensed health care provider who specializes in treating substance use disorders and who has at least five years of experience.

ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): 13. One university faculty member from each university under the jurisdiction of the Arizona board of regents who is an academic appointment in the chemistry department or another related analytical lab testing area to function as independent subject matter experts.

ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): 14. A representative of a laboratory that conducts proficiency testing for laboratories in this state.

ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): B. The medical marijuana testing advisory council shall make recommendations and consult with the director regarding:
ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): 1. Establishing a required testing program.
ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): 2. Testing and potency standards for medical marijuana.
ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): 3. Procedural requirements for collecting, storing and testing samples of medical marijuana.
ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): 4. Reporting results to patients and the department.

ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): 5. Remediation and disposal requirements for medical marijuana that fails to meet testing standards.
ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): 6. Additional items as necessary.

ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): C. The advisory council shall annually review the marijuana testing programs under this chapter and chapter 28.2 of this title and, on or before the second Monday in January of each year, shall submit to the president of the senate, the speaker of the house of representatives, the health and human services committee chairpersons of the senate and the house of representatives and the department of health services a report that does not disclose any identifying information and that includes at least the following:

ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): 1. An assessment as to whether an analyte should be removed from the required statutory testing panel.

ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): 2. The number of statements of deficiencies relating to testing that were issued to each nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary, third-party independent laboratory, marijuana establishment and marijuana testing facility in the preceding year, the remediation efforts made to address each deficiency and the resolution of each statement of deficiency. The information may not disclose any identifying information but shall delineate the information by entity.
ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): 3. Any other recommendations on improving the testing programs.

ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): D. Members of the advisory council are not eligible to receive compensation but are eligible for reimbursement of expenses pursuant to title 38, chapter 4, article 2.

ARS § 36-2821 (Medical marijuana testing advisory council; membership; duties; report; definitions): E. For the purposes of this section, "marijuana establishment" and "marijuana testing facility" have the same meanings prescribed in section 36-2850.
ARS § 36-2822 (Arizona biomedical research centre; medical marijuana fund; grants; marijuana clinical trials; requirements; exemption): (Added with a 1998 Prop. 105 clause pursuant to L21, Ch. 419)

ARS § 36-2822 (Arizona biomedical research centre; medical marijuana fund; grants; marijuana clinical trials; requirements; exemption): A. The Arizona biomedical research centre in the department shall provide competitive grants from monies in the medical marijuana fund established by section 36-2817 for marijuana clinical trials that are approved by the United States food and drug administration for evaluating both the safety and efficacy of using marijuana in humans and researching the impacts of marijuana interactions with prescription drugs, nonprescription drugs and illicit drugs.

ARS § 36-2822 (Arizona biomedical research centre; medical marijuana fund; grants; marijuana clinical trials; requirements; exemption): B. Clinical trials funded pursuant to subsection A of this section shall be conducted by Arizona-based researchers from nonprofit organizations or universities, be approved by the United States food and drug administration, the United States drug enforcement administration and an institutional review board and be publishable in peer-reviewed medical and public health journals. The centre shall prioritize randomized controlled clinical trials that study the treatment of autism, epilepsy, post-traumatic stress disorder and pain.

ARS § 36-2822 (Arizona biomedical research centre; medical marijuana fund; grants; marijuana clinical trials; requirements; exemption): C. Notwithstanding title 13, chapter 34, a person who receives a grant for a marijuana clinical trial pursuant to this section and any of the person's employees working on the clinical trial may not be charged with or prosecuted for possession of marijuana that is cultivated for medical use when the person is working on the clinical trial.

ARS § 36-2822 (Arizona biomedical research centre; medical marijuana fund; grants; marijuana clinical trials; requirements; exemption): D. The Arizona biomedical research centre may provide up to $5,000,000 annually for five consecutive years from the medical marijuana fund established by section 36-2817 to administer and award competitive grants pursuant to this section. The centre may not use more than five percent of these monies for administrative purposes.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): (Caution:  1998 Prop. 105 applies)
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): In this chapter, unless the context requires otherwise:

ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 1. "Advertise," "advertisement" and "advertising" mean any public communication in any medium that offers or solicits a commercial transaction involving the sale, purchase or delivery of marijuana or marijuana products.

ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 2. "Child-resistant" means designed or constructed to be significantly difficult for children under five years of age to open, and not difficult for normal adults to use properly.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 3. "Consume," "consuming" and "consumption" mean the act of ingesting, inhaling or otherwise introducing marijuana into the human body.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 4. "Consumer" means an individual who is at least twenty-one years of age and who purchases marijuana or marijuana products.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 5. "Cultivate" and "cultivation" mean to propagate, breed, grow, prepare and package marijuana.

ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 6. "Deliver" and "delivery" mean the transportation, transfer or provision of marijuana or marijuana products to a consumer at a location other than the designated retail location of a marijuana establishment.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 7. "Department" means the department of health services or its successor agency.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 8. "Designated caregiver" has the same meaning prescribed in section 36-2801.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 9. "Dual licensee" means an entity that holds both a nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary registration and a marijuana establishment license.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 10. "Early applicant" means either of the following:
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): (a) An entity seeking to operate a marijuana establishment in a county with fewer than two registered nonprofit medical marijuana dispensaries.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): (b) A nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary that is registered and in good standing with the department.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 11. "Employee," "employer," "health care facility," and "places of employment" have the same meanings prescribed in the smoke-free Arizona act, section 36-601.01.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 12. "Excluded felony offense" has the same meaning prescribed in section 36-2801.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 13. "Good standing" means that a nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary is not the subject of a pending notice of intent to revoke issued by the department.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 14. "Independent third-party laboratory" has the same meaning prescribed in section 36-2801.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 15. "Industrial hemp" has the same meaning prescribed in section 3-311.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 16. "Licensee" means a person that obtains a license pursuant to section 36-2854.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 17. "Locality" means a city, town or county.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 18. "Manufacture" and "manufacturing" mean to compound, blend, extract, infuse or otherwise make or prepare a marijuana product.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 19. "Marijuana":

ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): (a) Means all parts of the plant of the genus cannabis, whether growing or not, as well as the seeds from the plant, the resin extracted from any part of the plant, and every compound, manufacture, salt, derivative, mixture or preparation of the plant or its seeds or resin.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): (b) Includes cannabis as defined in 13-3401.

ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): (c) Does not include industrial hemp, the fiber produced from the stalks of the plant of the genus cannabis, oil or cake made from the seeds of the plant, sterilized seeds of the plant that are incapable of germination, or the weight of any other ingredient combined with marijuana to prepare topical or oral administrations, food, drink or other products.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 20. "Marijuana concentrate":

ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): (a) Means resin extracted from any part of a plant of the genus cannabis and every compound, manufacture, salt, derivative, mixture or preparation of that resin or tetrahydrocannabinol.

ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): (b) Does not include industrial hemp or the weight of any other ingredient combined with cannabis to prepare topical or oral administrations, food, drink or other products.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 21. "Marijuana establishment" means an entity that is licensed by the department to operate all of the following:
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): (a) A single retail location at which the licensee may sell marijuana and marijuana products to consumers, cultivate marijuana and manufacture marijuana products.

ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): (b) A single off-site cultivation location at which the licensee may cultivate marijuana, process marijuana and manufacture marijuana products, but from which marijuana and marijuana products may not be transferred or sold to consumers.

ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): (c) A single off-site location at which the licensee may manufacture marijuana products and package and store marijuana and marijuana products, but from which marijuana and marijuana products may not be transferred or sold to consumers.

ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 22. "Marijuana facility agent" means a principal officer, board member or employee of a marijuana establishment or marijuana testing facility who is at least twenty-one years of age and who has not been convicted of an excluded felony offense.

ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 23. "Marijuana products" means marijuana concentrate and products that are composed of marijuana and other ingredients and that are intended for use or consumption, including edible products, ointments and tinctures.

ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 24. "Marijuana testing facility" means the department or another entity that is licensed by the department to analyze the potency of marijuana and test marijuana for harmful contaminants.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 25. "Nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary" has the same meaning prescribed in section 36-2801.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 26. "Nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary agent" has the same meaning prescribed in section 36-2801.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 27. "Open space" means a public park, public sidewalk, public walkway or public pedestrian thoroughfare.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 28. "Process" and "processing" mean to harvest, dry, cure, trim or separate parts of the marijuana plant.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 29. "Public place" has the same meaning prescribed in section 36-601.01.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 30. "Qualifying patient" has the same meaning prescribed in section 36-2801.
ARS § 36-2850 (Definitions): 31. "Smoke" means to inhale, exhale, burn, carry or possess any lighted marijuana or lighted marijuana products, whether natural or synthetic.
ARS § 36-2851 (Employers; driving; minors; control of property; smoking in public places and open spaces): (Caution:  1998 Prop. 105 applies)
ARS § 36-2851 (Employers; driving; minors; control of property; smoking in public places and open spaces): This chapter:

ARS § 36-2851 (Employers; driving; minors; control of property; smoking in public places and open spaces): 1. Does not restrict the rights of employers to maintain a drug-and-alcohol-free workplace or affect the ability of employers to have workplace policies restricting the use of marijuana by employees or prospective employees.

ARS § 36-2851 (Employers; driving; minors; control of property; smoking in public places and open spaces): 2. Does not require an employer to allow or accommodate the use, consumption, possession, transfer, display, transportation, sale or cultivation of marijuana in a place of employment.

ARS § 36-2851 (Employers; driving; minors; control of property; smoking in public places and open spaces): 3. Does not allow driving, flying or boating while impaired to even the slightest degree by marijuana or prevent this state from enacting and imposing penalties for driving, flying or boating while impaired to even the slightest degree by marijuana.

ARS § 36-2851 (Employers; driving; minors; control of property; smoking in public places and open spaces): 4. Does not allow an individual who is under twenty-one years of age to purchase, possess, transport or consume marijuana or marijuana products.

ARS § 36-2851 (Employers; driving; minors; control of property; smoking in public places and open spaces): 5. Does not allow the sale, transfer or provision of marijuana or marijuana products to an individual who is under twenty-one years of age.

ARS § 36-2851 (Employers; driving; minors; control of property; smoking in public places and open spaces): 6. Does not restrict the rights of employers, schools, day care centers, adult day care facilities, health care facilities or corrections facilities to prohibit or regulate conduct otherwise allowed by this chapter when such conduct occurs on or in their properties.

ARS § 36-2851 (Employers; driving; minors; control of property; smoking in public places and open spaces): 7. Does not restrict the ability of an individual, partnership, limited liability company, private corporation, private entity or private organization of any character that occupies, owns or controls property to prohibit or regulate conduct otherwise allowed by this chapter on or in such property.
ARS § 36-2851 (Employers; driving; minors; control of property; smoking in public places and open spaces): 8. Does not allow any person to:
ARS § 36-2851 (Employers; driving; minors; control of property; smoking in public places and open spaces): (a) Smoke marijuana in a public place or open space.

ARS § 36-2851 (Employers; driving; minors; control of property; smoking in public places and open spaces): (b) Consume marijuana or marijuana products while driving, operating or riding in the passenger seat or compartment of an operating motor vehicle, boat, vessel, aircraft or another vehicle used for transportation.

ARS § 36-2851 (Employers; driving; minors; control of property; smoking in public places and open spaces): 9. Does not prohibit this state or a political subdivision of this state from prohibiting or regulating conduct otherwise allowed by this chapter when such conduct occurs on or in property that is occupied, owned, controlled or operated by this state or a political subdivision of this state.

ARS § 36-2851 (Employers; driving; minors; control of property; smoking in public places and open spaces): 10. Does not authorize a person to process or manufacture marijuana by means of any liquid or gas, other than alcohol, that has a flashpoint below one hundred degrees fahrenheit, unless performed by a marijuana establishment.

ARS § 36-2851 (Employers; driving; minors; control of property; smoking in public places and open spaces): 11. Does not require a person to violate federal law or to implement or fail to implement a restriction on the possession, consumption, display, transfer, processing, manufacturing or cultivation of marijuana if by so doing the person will lose a monetary or licensing-related benefit under federal law.

ARS § 36-2851 (Employers; driving; minors; control of property; smoking in public places and open spaces): 12. Does not supersede or eliminate any existing rights or privileges of any person except as specifically set forth in this chapter.

ARS § 36-2851 (Employers; driving; minors; control of property; smoking in public places and open spaces): 13. Does not limit any privilege or right of a nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary under chapter 28.1 of this title except as expressly set forth in this chapter.

ARS § 36-2851 (Employers; driving; minors; control of property; smoking in public places and open spaces): 14. Does not limit any privilege or right of a qualifying patient or designated caregiver under chapter 28.1 of this title.
ARS § 36-2852 (Allowable possession and personal use of marijuana, marijuana products and marijuana paraphernalia): (Caution:  1998 Prop. 105 applies)

ARS § 36-2852 (Allowable possession and personal use of marijuana, marijuana products and marijuana paraphernalia): A. Except as specifically and expressly provided in sections 36-2851 and 36-2853 and notwithstanding any other law, the following acts by an individual who is at least twenty-one years of age are lawful, are not an offense under the laws of this state or any locality, may not constitute the basis for detention, search or arrest, and cannot serve as the sole basis for seizure or forfeiture of assets, for imposing penalties of any kind under the laws of this state or any locality or for abrogating or limiting any right or privilege conferred or protected by the laws of this state or any locality:

ARS § 36-2852 (Allowable possession and personal use of marijuana, marijuana products and marijuana paraphernalia): 1. Possessing, consuming, purchasing, processing, manufacturing by manual or mechanical means, including sieving or ice water separation but excluding chemical extraction or chemical synthesis, or transporting one ounce or less of marijuana, except that not more than five grams of marijuana may be in the form of marijuana concentrate.

ARS § 36-2852 (Allowable possession and personal use of marijuana, marijuana products and marijuana paraphernalia): 2. Possessing, transporting, cultivating or processing not more than six marijuana plants for personal use at the individual's primary residence, and possessing, processing and manufacturing by manual or mechanical means, including sieving or ice water separation but excluding chemical extraction or chemical synthesis, the marijuana produced by the plants on the premises where the marijuana plants were grown if all of the following apply:

ARS § 36-2852 (Allowable possession and personal use of marijuana, marijuana products and marijuana paraphernalia): (a) Not more than twelve plants are produced at a single residence where two or more individuals who are at least twenty-one years of age reside at one time.

ARS § 36-2852 (Allowable possession and personal use of marijuana, marijuana products and marijuana paraphernalia): (b) Cultivation takes place within a closet, room, greenhouse or other enclosed area on the grounds of the residence equipped with a lock or other security device that prevents access by minors.

ARS § 36-2852 (Allowable possession and personal use of marijuana, marijuana products and marijuana paraphernalia): (c) Cultivation takes place in an area where the marijuana plants are not visible from public view without using binoculars, aircraft or other optical aids.

ARS § 36-2852 (Allowable possession and personal use of marijuana, marijuana products and marijuana paraphernalia): 3. Transferring one ounce or less of marijuana, of which not more than five grams may be in the form of marijuana concentrate, to an individual who is at least twenty-one years of age if the transfer is without remuneration and is not advertised or promoted to the public.

ARS § 36-2852 (Allowable possession and personal use of marijuana, marijuana products and marijuana paraphernalia): 4. Transferring up to six marijuana plants to an individual who is at least twenty-one years of age if the transfer is without remuneration and is not advertised or promoted to the public.

ARS § 36-2852 (Allowable possession and personal use of marijuana, marijuana products and marijuana paraphernalia): 5. Acquiring, possessing, manufacturing, using, purchasing, selling or transporting paraphernalia relating to the cultivation, manufacture, processing or consumption of marijuana or marijuana products.

ARS § 36-2852 (Allowable possession and personal use of marijuana, marijuana products and marijuana paraphernalia): 6. Assisting another individual who is at least twenty-one years of age in any of the acts described in this subsection.

ARS § 36-2852 (Allowable possession and personal use of marijuana, marijuana products and marijuana paraphernalia): B. Notwithstanding any other law, a person with metabolites or components of marijuana in the person's body is guilty of violating section 28-1381, subsection A, paragraph 3 only if the person is also impaired to the slightest degree.

ARS § 36-2852 (Allowable possession and personal use of marijuana, marijuana products and marijuana paraphernalia): C. Notwithstanding any other law, the odor of marijuana or burnt marijuana does not by itself constitute reasonable articulable suspicion of a crime.  This subsection does not apply when a law enforcement officer is investigating whether a person has violated section 28-1381.
ARS § 36-2853 (Violations; classification; civil penalty; additional fine; enforcement): (Caution:  1998 Prop. 105 applies)

ARS § 36-2853 (Violations; classification; civil penalty; additional fine; enforcement): A. Notwithstanding any other law and except as otherwise provided in this chapter, a person who possesses an amount of marijuana greater than the amount allowed pursuant to section 36-2852, but not more than two and one-half ounces of marijuana, of which not more than twelve and one-half grams is in the form of marijuana concentrate, is guilty of a petty offense.

ARS § 36-2853 (Violations; classification; civil penalty; additional fine; enforcement): B. Notwithstanding any other law, a person who is under twenty-one years of age and who possesses, consumes, transports or transfers without remuneration one ounce or less of marijuana, of which not more than five grams is in the form of marijuana concentrate, or paraphernalia relating to the consumption of marijuana or marijuana products:

ARS § 36-2853 (Violations; classification; civil penalty; additional fine; enforcement): 1. For a first violation, shall pay a civil penalty of not more than $100 to the smart and safe Arizona fund established by section 36-2856 and in the court's discretion may be ordered to attend up to four hours of drug education or counseling.

ARS § 36-2853 (Violations; classification; civil penalty; additional fine; enforcement): 2. For a second violation, is guilty of a petty offense, and in the court's discretion may be ordered to attend up to eight hours of drug education or counseling.
ARS § 36-2853 (Violations; classification; civil penalty; additional fine; enforcement): 3. For a third or subsequent violation, is guilty of a class 1 misdemeanor.
ARS § 36-2853 (Violations; classification; civil penalty; additional fine; enforcement): C. A person who smokes marijuana in a public place or open space is guilty of a petty offense.

ARS § 36-2853 (Violations; classification; civil penalty; additional fine; enforcement): D. Except as otherwise provided in chapter 28.1 of this title and notwithstanding any other law, any unlicensed person who cultivates marijuana plants pursuant to section 36-2852 where they are visible from public view without using binoculars, aircraft or other optical aids or outside of an enclosed area that is equipped with a lock or other security device that prevents access by minors is guilty of:
ARS § 36-2853 (Violations; classification; civil penalty; additional fine; enforcement): 1. For a first violation, a petty offense.
ARS § 36-2853 (Violations; classification; civil penalty; additional fine; enforcement): 2. For a second or subsequent violation, a class 3 misdemeanor.

ARS § 36-2853 (Violations; classification; civil penalty; additional fine; enforcement): E. A person who is under twenty-one years of age and who misrepresents the person's age to any other person by means of a written instrument of identification or who uses a fraudulent or false written instrument of identification with the intent to induce a person to sell or otherwise transfer marijuana or a marijuana product to the person who is under twenty-one years of age is guilty of:
ARS § 36-2853 (Violations; classification; civil penalty; additional fine; enforcement): 1. For a first violation, a petty offense.
ARS § 36-2853 (Violations; classification; civil penalty; additional fine; enforcement): 2. For a second or subsequent violation, a class 1 misdemeanor.

ARS § 36-2853 (Violations; classification; civil penalty; additional fine; enforcement): F. A person who is under twenty-one years of age and who solicits another person to purchase marijuana or a marijuana product in violation of this chapter is guilty of:
ARS § 36-2853 (Violations; classification; civil penalty; additional fine; enforcement): 1. For a first violation, a petty offense.
ARS § 36-2853 (Violations; classification; civil penalty; additional fine; enforcement): 2. For a second or subsequent violation, a class 3 misdemeanor.
ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (Caution:  1998 Prop. 105 applies)

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): A. The department shall adopt rules to implement and enforce this chapter and regulate marijuana, marijuana products, marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities. Those rules shall include requirements for:

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 1. Licensing marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities, including conducting investigations and background checks to determine eligibility for licensing for marijuana establishment and marijuana testing facility applicants, except that:

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (a) An application for a marijuana establishment license or marijuana testing facility license may not require the disclosure of the identity of any person who is entitled to a share of less than ten percent of the profits of an applicant that is a publicly traded corporation.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (b) The department may not issue more than one marijuana establishment license for every ten pharmacies that have registered under section 32-1929, that have obtained a pharmacy permit from the Arizona board of pharmacy and that operate within this state.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (c) Notwithstanding subdivision (b) of this paragraph, the department may issue a marijuana establishment license to not more than two marijuana establishments per county that contains no registered nonprofit medical marijuana dispensaries, or one marijuana establishment license per county that contains one registered nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary. Any license issued pursuant to this subdivision shall be for a fixed county and may not be relocated outside of that county.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (d) The department shall accept applications for marijuana establishment licenses from early applicants beginning January 19, 2021 through March 9, 2021. Not later than sixty days after receiving an application pursuant to this subdivision, the department shall issue a marijuana establishment license to each qualified early applicant. If the department has not adopted final rules pursuant to this section at the time marijuana establishment licenses are issued pursuant to this subdivision, licensees shall comply with the rules adopted by the department to implement chapter 28.1 of this title except those that are inconsistent with this chapter.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (e) After issuing marijuana establishment licenses to qualified early applicants, the department shall issue marijuana establishment licenses available under subdivisions (b) and (c) of this paragraph by random selection and according to rules adopted pursuant to this section. At least sixty days before any random selection, the department shall prominently publicize the random selection on its website and through other means of general distribution intended to reach as many interested parties as possible and shall provide notice through an email notification system to which interested parties can subscribe.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (f) Notwithstanding subdivisions (b) and (c) of this paragraph, and not later than six months after the department adopts final rules to implement a social equity ownership program pursuant to paragraph 9 of this subsection, the department shall issue twenty-six additional marijuana establishment licenses to entities that are qualified pursuant to the social equity ownership program.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (g) Licenses issued by the department to marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities shall be valid for a period of two years.  A dual licensee's initial renewal date, which will be the ongoing renewal date for both the dual licensee's marijuana establishment license and nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary registration, is the earlier of:
ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (i) The date of the marijuana establishment license renewal.
ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (ii) The date of the nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary registration renewal.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (h) The department may not issue a marijuana establishment or marijuana testing facility license to an applicant who has an ownership interest in an out-of-state marijuana establishment or marijuana testing facility, or the other state's equivalent, that has had its license revoked by the other state.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 2. Licensing fees and renewal fees for marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities in amounts that are reasonable and related to the actual cost of processing applications for licenses and renewals and that do not exceed five times the fees prescribed by the department to register or renew a nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary.
ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 3. The security of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 4. Marijuana establishments to safely cultivate, process and manufacture marijuana and marijuana products. The department shall require licensees to procure, develop, acquire and maintain a system to track marijuana and marijuana products at all points of cultivation, manufacturing and sale.  The system developed and maintained pursuant to this paragraph shall:

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (a) Ensure an accurate accounting and reporting of the production, processing and sale of marijuana and marijuana products.
ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (b) Ensure compliance with rules adopted by the department.
ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (c) Be capable of tracking, at a minimum:
ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (i) The propagation of immature marijuana plants and the production of marijuana by a marijuana establishment.
ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (ii) The processing of marijuana and marijuana products by a marijuana establishment.
ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (iii) The sale and purchase of marijuana and marijuana products between licensees.
ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (iv) The transfer of marijuana and marijuana products between premises for which licenses have been issued.
ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (v) The disposal of marijuana waste.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (vi) The identity of the person making the entry in the system and the time, date and location of each entry into the system, including any corrections or changes to that information.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (vii) Any other information that the department determines is reasonably necessary to accomplish the duties, functions and powers of the department.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (d) Contain a transactional stamp to ensure accuracy, provide for chain of custody of the information and foreclose tampering of the data, human error or intentional misreporting.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 5. Tracking, testing, labeling consistent with section 36-2854.01 and packaging marijuana and marijuana products, including requirements that marijuana and marijuana products be:

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (a) Sold to consumers in clearly and conspicuously labeled containers that contain accurate warnings regarding the use of marijuana or marijuana products.
ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (b) Placed in child-resistant packaging on exit from a marijuana establishment.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 6. Forms of government-issued identification that are acceptable by a marijuana establishment verifying a consumer's age and procedures related to verifying a consumer's age consistent with section 4-241.  Until the department adopts final rules related to verifying a consumer's age, marijuana establishments shall comply with the proof of legal age requirements prescribed in section 4-241.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 7. The potency of edible marijuana products that may be sold to consumers by marijuana establishments at reasonable levels on consideration of industry standards, except that the rules:

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (a) Shall limit the strength of edible marijuana products to not more than ten milligrams of tetrahydrocannabinol per serving or one hundred milligrams of tetrahydrocannabinol per package.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (b) Shall require that if a marijuana product contains more than one serving, it must be delineated or scored into standard serving sizes and homogenized to ensure uniform disbursement throughout the marijuana product.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 8. Ensuring the health, safety and training of employees of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 9. The creation and implementation of a social equity ownership program to promote the ownership and operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities by individuals from communities disproportionately impacted by the enforcement of previous marijuana laws.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 10. Prohibiting a marijuana testing facility from having any direct or indirect familial relationship with or financial ownership interest in a marijuana establishment or related marijuana business entity or management company. The rules shall include prohibiting a marijuana establishment from having any direct or indirect familial relationship with or financial ownership interest in a marijuana testing facility or related marijuana business entity or management company.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 11. Requiring marijuana establishments to display in a conspicuous location a sign that warns pregnant women about the potential dangers to fetuses caused by smoking or ingesting marijuana while pregnant or to infants while breastfeeding and the risk of being reported to the department of child safety during pregnancy or at the birth of the child by persons who are required to report. The rules shall include the specific warning language that must be included on the sign. The cost and display of the sign required by rule shall be borne by the marijuana establishment.
ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): B. The department may:

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 1. Subject to title 41, chapter 6, article 10, deny any application submitted or deny, suspend or revoke, in whole or in part, any registration or license issued under this chapter if the registered or licensed party or an officer, agent or employee of the registered or licensed party does any of the following:
ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (a) Violates this chapter or any rule adopted pursuant to this chapter.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): (b) Has been, is or may continue to be in substantial violation of the requirements for licensing or registration and, as a result, the health or safety of the general public is in immediate danger.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 2. Subject to title 41, chapter 6, article 10, and unless another penalty is provided elsewhere in this chapter, assess a civil penalty against a person that violates this chapter or any rule adopted pursuant to this chapter in an amount not to exceed $2,000 for each violation. Each day a violation occurs constitutes a separate violation. In determining the amount of a civil penalty assessed against a person, the department shall consider all of the factors set forth in section 36-2816, subsection H. All civil penalties collected by the department pursuant to this paragraph shall be deposited in the smart and safe Arizona fund established by section 36-2856.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 3. At any time during regular hours of operation, visit and inspect a marijuana establishment, marijuana testing facility or dual licensee to determine if it complies with this chapter and rules adopted pursuant to this chapter. The department shall make at least one unannounced visit annually to each facility licensed pursuant to this chapter.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 4. Adopt any other rules that are not expressly stated in this section and that are necessary to ensure the safe and responsible cultivation, sale, processing, manufacture, testing and transport of marijuana and marijuana products.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): C. Until the department adopts rules allowing and regulating delivery by marijuana establishments pursuant to subsection D of this section, delivery is unlawful under this chapter.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): D. On or after January 1, 2023, the department may, and not later than January 1, 2025 the department shall, adopt rules to allow and regulate delivery by marijuana establishments.  The rules shall:

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 1. Require that delivery and the marijuana and marijuana products to be delivered originate from a designated retail location of a marijuana establishment and only after an order is made with the marijuana establishment by a consumer. The rules may not limit the distance between the delivery location and the originating designated retail location of the marijuana establishment.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 2. Prohibit delivery to any property owned or leased by the United States, this state, a political subdivision of this state or the Arizona board of regents.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 3. Limit the amount of marijuana and marijuana products based on retail price that may be in a delivery vehicle during a single trip from the designated retail location of a marijuana establishment.
ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 4. Prohibit extra or unallocated marijuana or marijuana products in delivery vehicles.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 5. Require that deliveries be made only by marijuana facility agents in unmarked vehicles that are equipped with a global positioning system or similar location tracking system and video surveillance and recording equipment, and that contain a locked compartment in which marijuana and marijuana products must be stored.  The rules may not limit the number of vehicles that a marijuana establishment may use for delivery.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 6. Require delivery logs necessary to ensure compliance with this subsection and rules adopted pursuant to this subsection.
ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 7. Require inspections to ensure compliance with this subsection and rules adopted pursuant to this subsection.
ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 8. Include any other provisions necessary to ensure safe and restricted delivery.
ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 9. Require dual licensees to comply with the rules adopted pursuant to this subsection.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): E. Except as provided in subsection D of this section, the department may not allow delivery of marijuana or marijuana products under this chapter by any individual or entity. In addition to any other penalty imposed by law, an individual or entity that delivers marijuana or marijuana products in a manner that is not authorized by this chapter shall pay a civil penalty of $20,000 per violation to the smart and safe Arizona fund established by section 36-2856. This subsection may be enforced by the attorney general.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): F. All rules adopted by the department pursuant to this section shall be consistent with the purpose of this chapter.
ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): G. The department may not adopt any rule that:

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 1. Prohibits the operation of marijuana establishments, either expressly or through requirements that make the operation of a marijuana establishment unduly burdensome.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 2. Prohibits or interferes with the ability of a dual licensee to operate a marijuana establishment and a nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary at shared locations.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): H. Notwithstanding section 41-192, the department may employ legal counsel and make an expenditure or incur an indebtedness for legal services for the purposes of:
ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 1. Defending this chapter or rules adopted pursuant to this chapter.
ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 2. Defending chapter 28.1 of this title or rules adopted pursuant to chapter 28.1 of this title.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): I. The department shall deposit all license fees, application fees and renewal fees paid to the department pursuant to this chapter in the smart and safe Arizona fund established by section 36-2856.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): J. On request, the department of health services shall share with the department of revenue information regarding a marijuana establishment, marijuana testing facility or dual licensee, including its name, physical address, cultivation site and transaction privilege tax license number.
ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): K. Notwithstanding any other law, the department may:
ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 1. License an independent third-party laboratory to also operate as a marijuana testing facility.
ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 2. Operate a marijuana testing facility.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): L. The department shall maintain and publish a current list of all marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities by name and license number.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): M. Notwithstanding any other law, the issuance of an occupational, professional or other regulatory license or certification to a person by a jurisdiction or regulatory authority outside this state does not entitle that person to be issued a marijuana establishment license, a marijuana testing facility license, or any other license, registration or certification under this chapter.
ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): N. Until the department adopts rules as required by subsection A, paragraph 10 of this section:

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 1. A marijuana testing facility is prohibited from having any direct or indirect familial relationship with or financial ownership interest in a marijuana establishment or related marijuana business entity or management company.

ARS § 36-2854 (Rules; licensing; early applicants; fees; civil penalty; legal counsel): 2. A marijuana establishment is prohibited from having any direct or indirect familial relationship with or financial ownership interest in a marijuana testing facility or related marijuana business entity or management company.
ARS § 36-2854.01 (Marijuana products; labeling; packaging): (Added with a 1998 Prop. 105 clause pursuant to L21, Ch. 394)

ARS § 36-2854.01 (Marijuana products; labeling; packaging): Not later than December 31, 2023, any marijuana product packaging labeled for sale shall include a consumer scannable tetrahydrocannabinol quick response code or similar technology linking to a webpage that displays all of the following for the specific marijuana product:
ARS § 36-2854.01 (Marijuana products; labeling; packaging): 1. The date of harvest of the marijuana.
ARS § 36-2854.01 (Marijuana products; labeling; packaging): 2. The tetrahydrocannabinol strain of the marijuana.
ARS § 36-2854.01 (Marijuana products; labeling; packaging): 3. The tetrahydrocannabinol extraction method used to extract the tetrahydrocannabinol from the marijuana.
ARS § 36-2854.01 (Marijuana products; labeling; packaging): 4. A laboratory report of impurities containing at least heavy metals and agrochemicals.
ARS § 36-2854.01 (Marijuana products; labeling; packaging): 5. The date of manufacture of the marijuana product.
ARS § 36-2854.01 (Marijuana products; labeling; packaging): 6. The distribution chain, including at least a point of intended sale.
ARS § 36-2854.01 (Marijuana products; labeling; packaging): 7. A warning that states, "using marijuana during pregnancy could cause birth defects or other health issues to your unborn child."
ARS § 36-2855 (Marijuana facility agents; registration; card; rules): (Caution:  1998 Prop. 105 applies)

ARS § 36-2855 (Marijuana facility agents; registration; card; rules): A. A marijuana facility agent shall be registered with the department before working at a marijuana establishment or marijuana testing facility.

ARS § 36-2855 (Marijuana facility agents; registration; card; rules): B. A person who wishes to be registered as a marijuana facility agent or renew the person's registration as a marijuana facility agent shall:

ARS § 36-2855 (Marijuana facility agents; registration; card; rules): 1. Submit a completed application on a form prescribed by the department and pay a nonrefundable fee that is reasonable and related to the actual cost of processing applications submitted pursuant to this section.

ARS § 36-2855 (Marijuana facility agents; registration; card; rules): 2. Submit evidence that the applicant holds a current level I fingerprint clearance card issued pursuant to section 41-1758.07, or submit a full set of the applicant's fingerprints for the purpose of obtaining a state and federal criminal records check pursuant to section 41-1750 and Public Law 92-544.  The department of public safety may exchange this fingerprint data with the federal bureau of investigation without disclosing that the records check is related to this chapter and acts allowed by this chapter.  The department of public safety shall destroy each set of fingerprints after the criminal records check is completed.

ARS § 36-2855 (Marijuana facility agents; registration; card; rules): C. If the department determines that an applicant meets the criteria for registration under this chapter and rules pursuant to this chapter, the department shall issue the applicant a marijuana facility agent card that is valid for two years.

ARS § 36-2855 (Marijuana facility agents; registration; card; rules): D. A registered marijuana facility agent may be employed by or associated with any marijuana establishment or marijuana testing facility. A marijuana establishment or marijuana testing facility shall promptly notify the department when it employs or becomes associated with a new marijuana facility agent.  A marijuana facility agent shall promptly notify the department when the marijuana facility agent is employed by or becomes associated with a marijuana establishment or marijuana testing facility and when the marijuana facility agent is no longer employed by or associated with a marijuana establishment or marijuana testing facility.

ARS § 36-2855 (Marijuana facility agents; registration; card; rules): E. A nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary agent of a dual licensee who has applied to be registered as a marijuana facility agent may serve as a marijuana facility agent of that dual licensee until the department has approved or rejected the agent's application.
ARS § 36-2855 (Marijuana facility agents; registration; card; rules): F. The department shall adopt rules to implement this section.
ARS § 36-2856 (Smart and safe Arizona fund; disposition of monies; exemption): (Caution:  1998 Prop. 105 applies)

ARS § 36-2856 (Smart and safe Arizona fund; disposition of monies; exemption): A. The smart and safe Arizona fund is established consisting of all monies deposited pursuant to sections 36-2853, 36-2854, 36-2859, 42-5452 and 42-5453, private donations and interest earned on those monies.  Monies in the fund are continuously appropriated. Monies in the fund and its accounts may not be transferred to any other fund except as provided in this section, do not revert to the state general fund and are exempt from the provisions of section 35-190 relating to the lapsing of appropriations.  The state treasurer shall administer the fund.

ARS § 36-2856 (Smart and safe Arizona fund; disposition of monies; exemption): B. All monies in the smart and safe Arizona fund must first be spent, and the state treasurer shall transfer monies from the fund, to pay:

ARS § 36-2856 (Smart and safe Arizona fund; disposition of monies; exemption): 1. The actual reasonable costs incurred by the department to implement, carry out and enforce this chapter and rules adopted pursuant to this chapter.

ARS § 36-2856 (Smart and safe Arizona fund; disposition of monies; exemption): 2. The actual reasonable costs incurred by the department of revenue to impose and enforce the tax authorized and levied by section 42-5452.

ARS § 36-2856 (Smart and safe Arizona fund; disposition of monies; exemption): 3. The actual reasonable costs incurred by the supreme court and the department of public safety to process petitions for expungement and expungement orders pursuant to section 36-2862 and to otherwise implement section 36-2862.
ARS § 36-2856 (Smart and safe Arizona fund; disposition of monies; exemption): 4. The actual reasonable costs incurred by the state treasurer to administer the fund.

ARS § 36-2856 (Smart and safe Arizona fund; disposition of monies; exemption): 5. Any other mandatory expenditure of state revenues required by this chapter to implement or enforce the provisions of this chapter.

ARS § 36-2856 (Smart and safe Arizona fund; disposition of monies; exemption): C. The state treasurer may prescribe forms necessary to make transfers from the smart and safe Arizona fund pursuant to subsection B of this section.

ARS § 36-2856 (Smart and safe Arizona fund; disposition of monies; exemption): D. On or before June 30 and December 31 of each year, the state treasurer shall transfer all monies in the smart and safe Arizona fund in excess of the amounts paid pursuant to subsection B of this section as follows:

ARS § 36-2856 (Smart and safe Arizona fund; disposition of monies; exemption): 1. Thirty-three percent to community college districts and provisional community college districts, but not to community college tuition financing districts established pursuant to section 15-1409, for the purposes of investing in and providing workforce development programs, job training, career and technical education, and science, technology, engineering and mathematics programs, as follows:
ARS § 36-2856 (Smart and safe Arizona fund; disposition of monies; exemption): (a) Fifteen percent of the thirty-three percent divided equally between each community college district.

ARS § 36-2856 (Smart and safe Arizona fund; disposition of monies; exemption): (b) One-half of one percent of the thirty-three percent divided equally between each provisional community college district, if one or more provisional community college districts exist.

ARS § 36-2856 (Smart and safe Arizona fund; disposition of monies; exemption): (c) The remainder to community college districts and provisional community colleges districts in proportion to each district's full-time equivalent student enrollment percentage of the total statewide audited full-time equivalent student enrollment in the preceding fiscal year prescribed in section 15-1466.01.

ARS § 36-2856 (Smart and safe Arizona fund; disposition of monies; exemption): 2. 31.4 percent to municipal police departments, municipal fire departments, fire districts and joint powers authorities established pursuant to title 48, chapter 5 and county sheriffs' departments in proportion to the number of members as defined in section 38-842 for each such agency in the public safety personnel retirement system established by title 38, chapter 5, article 4 and the public safety personnel defined contribution retirement plan established pursuant to title 38, chapter 5, article 4.1, for personnel costs.
ARS § 36-2856 (Smart and safe Arizona fund; disposition of monies; exemption): 3. 25.4 percent to the Arizona highway user revenue fund established by section 28-6533.
ARS § 36-2856 (Smart and safe Arizona fund; disposition of monies; exemption): 4. Ten percent to the justice reinvestment fund established by section 36-2863.
ARS § 36-2856 (Smart and safe Arizona fund; disposition of monies; exemption): 5. 0.2 percent to the attorney general to use to enforce this chapter or to grant to localities to enforce this chapter.
ARS § 36-2856 (Smart and safe Arizona fund; disposition of monies; exemption): E. The monies transferred and received pursuant to this section:

ARS § 36-2856 (Smart and safe Arizona fund; disposition of monies; exemption): 1. Are in addition to any other appropriation, transfer or other allocation of monies and may not supplant, replace or cause a reduction in other funding sources.
ARS § 36-2856 (Smart and safe Arizona fund; disposition of monies; exemption): 2. Are not considered local revenues for the purposes of article IX, sections 20 and 21, Constitution of Arizona.
ARS § 36-2857 (Localities; marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): (Caution: 1998 Prop. 105 applies)
ARS § 36-2857 (Localities; marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): A. A locality may:

ARS § 36-2857 (Localities; marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 1. Enact reasonable zoning regulations that limit the use of land for marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities to specified areas.
ARS § 36-2857 (Localities; marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 2. Limit the number of marijuana establishments or marijuana testing facilities, or both.
ARS § 36-2857 (Localities; marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 3. Prohibit marijuana establishments or marijuana testing facilities, or both.
ARS § 36-2857 (Localities; marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 4. Regulate the time, place and manner of marijuana establishment and marijuana testing facility operations.

ARS § 36-2857 (Localities; marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 5. Establish reasonable restrictions on public signage regarding marijuana, marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities.
ARS § 36-2857 (Localities; marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 6. Prohibit or restrict delivery within its jurisdiction.

ARS § 36-2857 (Localities; marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): B. A county may exercise its authority pursuant to subsection A of this section only in unincorporated areas of the county.
ARS § 36-2857 (Localities; marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): C. A locality may not enact any ordinance, regulation or rule that:

ARS § 36-2857 (Localities; marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 1. Is more restrictive than a comparable ordinance, regulation or rule that applies to nonprofit medical marijuana dispensaries.

ARS § 36-2857 (Localities; marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 2. Makes the operation of a marijuana establishment or marijuana testing facility unduly burdensome if the locality has not prohibited marijuana establishments or marijuana testing facilities.
ARS § 36-2857 (Localities; marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 3. Conflicts with this chapter or rules adopted pursuant to this chapter.

ARS § 36-2857 (Localities; marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 4. Prohibits the transportation of marijuana by a marijuana establishment or marijuana testing facility on public roads.

ARS § 36-2857 (Localities; marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 5. Restricts or interferes with the ability of a dual licensee or an entity eligible to become a dual licensee to operate a nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary and a marijuana establishment cooperatively at shared locations.

ARS § 36-2857 (Localities; marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 6. Except as expressly authorized by this section or section 36-2851, prohibits or restricts any conduct or transaction allowed by this chapter, or imposes any liability or penalty in addition to that prescribed by this chapter for any conduct or transaction constituting a violation of this chapter.

ARS § 36-2857 (Localities; marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 7. Allows a marijuana establishment to locate within five hundred feet of a public or private school, a child care facility or a facility that provides preschool programs.
ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): (Caution:  1998 Prop. 105 applies)

ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): A. Except as specifically and expressly provided in section 36-2857 and notwithstanding any other law, it is lawful and is not an offense under the laws of this state or any locality, may not constitute the basis for detention, search or arrest, and may not constitute the sole basis for seizure or forfeiture of assets or the basis for imposing penalties under the laws of this state or any locality for:
ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 1. A marijuana establishment, or an agent acting on behalf of a marijuana establishment, to:
ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): (a) Possess marijuana or marijuana products.
ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): (b) Purchase, sell or transport marijuana and marijuana products to or from a marijuana establishment.

ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): (c) Sell marijuana and marijuana products to consumers, except that a marijuana establishment may not sell more than one ounce of marijuana to a consumer in a single transaction, not more than five grams of which may be in the form of marijuana concentrate.

ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): (d) Cultivate, produce, test or process marijuana or manufacture marijuana or marijuana products by any means, including chemical extraction or chemical synthesis.

ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 2. An agent acting on behalf of a marijuana establishment to sell or otherwise transfer marijuana to an individual under twenty-one years of age, if the agent reasonably verified that the individual appeared to be twenty-one years of age or older by means of a government-issued photographic identification in compliance with rules adopted pursuant to section 36-2854, subsection A, paragraph 6.

ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 3. A marijuana testing facility, or an agent acting on behalf of a marijuana testing facility, to obtain, possess, process, repackage, transfer, transport or test marijuana and marijuana products.

ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 4. A nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary or a marijuana establishment, or an agent acting on behalf of a nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary or a marijuana establishment, to sell or otherwise transfer marijuana or marijuana products to a nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary, a marijuana establishment or an agent acting on behalf of a nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary or a marijuana establishment.

ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 5. Any individual, corporation or other entity to sell, lease or otherwise allow property or goods that are owned, managed or controlled by the individual, corporation or other entity to be used for any activity authorized by this chapter, or to provide services to a marijuana establishment, or marijuana testing facility or agent acting on behalf of a marijuana establishment or marijuana testing facility in connection with any activity authorized by this chapter.

ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): B. This section does not preclude the department from imposing penalties against a marijuana establishment or marijuana testing facility for failing to comply with this chapter or rules adopted pursuant to this chapter.
ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): C. A marijuana establishment may be owned or operated by a publicly traded company.
ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): D. Notwithstanding any other law, a dual licensee:

ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 1. May hold a marijuana establishment license and operate a marijuana establishment pursuant to this chapter.

ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 2. May operate on a for-profit basis if the dual licensee promptly notifies the department and department of revenue and takes any actions necessary to enable its for-profit operation, including converting its corporate form and amending its organizational and operating documents.

ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 3. Must continue to hold both its marijuana establishment license and nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary registration, regardless of any change in ownership of the dual licensee, unless it terminates its status as a dual licensee and forfeits either its marijuana establishment license or nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary registration by notifying the department of such a termination and forfeiture.
ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 4. Is not required to:
ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): (a) Employ or contract with a medical director.

ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): (b) Obtain nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary agent or marijuana facility agent registrations for outside vendors that do not have regular, unsupervised access to the interior of the dual licensee's premises.

ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): (c) Have a single secure entrance as required by section 36-2806, subsection C, but may be required to implement appropriate security measures to deter and prevent the theft of marijuana and to reasonably regulate customer access to the premises.

ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): (d) Comply with any other provision of chapter 28.1 of this title or any rule adopted pursuant to chapter 28.1 of this title that makes its operation as a dual licensee unduly burdensome.

ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): E. Notwithstanding any other law, a dual licensee that elects to operate on a for-profit basis pursuant to subsection D, paragraph 2 of this section:
ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 1. Is subject to the taxes imposed pursuant to title 43.

ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 2. Is not required to submit its annual financial statements or an audit report to the department for purposes of renewing its nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary registration.

ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): F. Notwithstanding any other law, a dual licensee must conduct both of the following operations at a shared location:
ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 1. Sell marijuana and marijuana products to consumers pursuant to this chapter.

ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 2. Dispense marijuana to registered qualifying patients and registered designated caregivers pursuant to chapter 28.1 of this title.

ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): G. Notwithstanding chapter 28.1 of this title or any rule adopted pursuant to chapter 28.1 of this title, a dual licensee may engage in any act, practice, conduct or transaction allowed for a marijuana establishment by this chapter.
ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): H. Notwithstanding any other law:

ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 1. An individual may be an applicant, principal officer or board member of more than one marijuana establishment or more than one dual licensee regardless of the establishment's location.

ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): 2. Two or more marijuana establishments or dual licensees may designate a single off-site location as prescribed in section 36-2850, paragraph 21, subdivision (c) to be jointly used by those dual licensees or marijuana establishments.

ARS § 36-2858 (Lawful operation of marijuana establishments and marijuana testing facilities): I. Marijuana establishments, marijuana testing facilities and dual licensees that are subject to applicable federal or state antidiscrimination laws may not pay their employees differently based solely on a protected class status such as sex, race, color, religion, national origin, age or disability. This subsection does not expand or modify the jurisdictional reach, provisions or requirements of any applicable antidiscrimination law.
ARS § 36-2859 (Advertising restrictions; enforcement; civil penalty): (Eff. until 7/1/26. Caution:  1998 Prop. 105 applies)
ARS § 36-2859 (Advertising restrictions; enforcement; civil penalty): A. A marijuana establishment or nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary may engage in advertising.
ARS § 36-2859 (Advertising restrictions; enforcement; civil penalty): B. An advertising platform may host advertising only if all of the following apply:
ARS § 36-2859 (Advertising restrictions; enforcement; civil penalty): 1. The advertising is authorized by a marijuana establishment or nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary.

ARS § 36-2859 (Advertising restrictions; enforcement; civil penalty): 2. The advertising accurately and legibly identifies the marijuana establishment or nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary responsible for the content of the advertising by name and license number or registration number.

ARS § 36-2859 (Advertising restrictions; enforcement; civil penalty): C.
